_readme: Known symbols for VSHELL.EXE: confirmed address -> meaning mappings, applied to the Ghidra project by ES2ApplySymbolNames.java.
Schema, confidence rules and run order: tools/ghidra_scripts/README.md, 'Known symbols'.
Entries are in address order. tools/scripts/es2_naming.py insert and edit keep it, and check that it holds.

entries.name: Shell_BuildScreensAndStart
entries.description: Builds every screen, starts the music, then by 0048227e: 3 or 4 (-X3/-X4) Game_LoadSlot(10), Game_ProcessMissionResults and a fade in; 6 (-X6, after a demo) a fade in, a blank, palette 1 and the startup sequence; anything else the two intro movies (0x44, 0x45), a blank, palette 1 and the startup sequence.

entries.name: ShellMap_RunIntro
entries.description: Main-loop hook: when Mission_Show set DAT_0046c075, installs the briefing palette and loops ShellMap_IntroStep until it returns false; a click (DAT_0046c07c) or scancode 1/0x39 calls ShellMap_SkipIntro.

entries.name: Shell_Main
entries.description: The shell's WinMain body: allocates the shell pool, parses the command line and copies -X into 0048227e, refuses without -eggplant, opens the CD volume, loads the catalogs and the career table, builds the display root and cursors, starts the sound, runs Shell_BuildScreensAndStart, then loops the dispatcher, events, palette commit, dirty-list flush, Movie_PlayQueue(1) and ShellMap_RunIntro until WM_QUIT or Shell_QuitFlag, and on the way out autosaves slot 10 (Game_SaveSlot(10, NULL)).

entries.name: Shell_RunFrames
entries.description: Runs up to 24 shell frames, stopping early when the quit flag 0046c074 is set or Shell_PumpMessages sees WM_QUIT. Each frame, when 0046c094 is set: Dispatcher_RunQueue on 004810f4 with all masks, Shell_PumpEvents, Shell_CommitPalette and DirtyList_Flush on the screen object at [004810f0]. Called from Game_ProcessMissionResults and the main menu's Credits, Instant Action and View Demo handlers, among others.

entries.name: Shell_BusyWaitSeconds
entries.description: Spins on GetTickCount for the argument in seconds, pumping nothing. Movie_PlayQueue holds the location picture up with it for 2.

entries.name: Shell_MonoPrintFps
entries.description: Advances an 8-entry ring of GetTickCount stamps (index 00481140, stamps 00481120), takes 8000 / (now - the stamp eight calls ago) as frames per second, and prints it as 'fps %f' with Mono_Printf at column 0, row 0x14. Shell_Main calls it.

entries.name: Volume_Ctor
entries.description: (volume): zeroes +0, +4, +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c of the 0x30-byte volume. Volume_LoadVolume constructs each volume with it.

entries.name: Volume_Dtor
entries.description: (volume, flags): frees the arrays at +0x24, +0x28 and +0x2c, destroys the streams at +4 and +0 through their own destructors (flag 3), and frees the 0x30-byte volume when flags bit 0 is set. Volume_LoadVolume destroys a volume it fails to finish with it; 00403622 and VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume call it too.

entries.name: Volume_LoadVolume
entries.description: Volume::loadVolume. Confirmed via matching Class::method assert string ('VolRStream revision' mismatch check) and clean decompile after the parameter-commit fix.

entries.name: Volume_FindEntry
entries.description: Looks a path up in one loaded volume: (volume, path, entryInfo). Splits the path into directory and file name, matches the directory against the volume's directory list (+0x1d count, +0x24 names) and then the name and directory index against its 18-byte entries (+0x1e count, +0x2c table), case-insensitively. On a hit it seeks the volume's stream (+4) to the entry, reads the 9-byte prefix and fills entryInfo: [0] the volume stream, [2] and [4] the data offset (entry offset + 9), [5] the prefix's first byte (compression type), [6] the prefix's size dword. Returns 1 on a hit, 0 otherwise.

entries.name: VolRStream_Ctor
entries.description: VolRStream::VolRStream() from src\volrstrm.cpp (vtable 0046d014, RTTI name 'VolRStream', 0x2f bytes). Asserts 'A volume group must be defined before a volume stream can be used.' when g_VolumeGroup is null, clears the entry fields and the filter pointers, handle -1, status 5 (no file). VolRStream layout: +8 int16 file handle (-1 when reading from a volume), +0xa the volume's own stream, +0xe the stream reads go through (the volume stream for a stored entry, else the filter), +0x12 entry data offset in the volume, +0x16 position within the entry, +0x1a expected position of the volume stream, +0x1e compression type, +0x22 entry size, +0x26 byte: the stream owns the handle, +0x27 RLERStream*, +0x2b LZHRStream*.

entries.name: VolRStream_CtorFromHandle
entries.description: VolRStream::VolRStream(handle) from src\volrstrm.cpp: as VolRStream_Ctor, but adopts an open file handle without owning it (+0x26 = 0) and probes it with _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR); failure goes to VolRStream_SetIoError. The 'errno == EBADF' tests before its asserts read the dword at 0046b6f6, which is the cw3220 _errno import thunk's own code bytes (FF 25 3C E3), not errno, so in this image they are never true.

entries.name: VolRStream_CtorFromPath
entries.description: VolRStream::VolRStream(path) from src\volrstrm.cpp: as VolRStream_Ctor, then VolRStream_Open(path). The usual way the shell opens a data file, loose or inside a volume.

entries.name: VolRStream_Dtor
entries.description: VolRStream destructor (vtable 0046d014). Deletes the RLERStream at +0x27 and the LZHRStream at +0x2b through their virtual destructors, closes via VolRStream_Close, runs Stream_BaseDtor, frees when flag&1.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; src\volrstrm.cpp assert strings in the class's constructors

entries.name: VolRStream_SetFile
entries.description: VolRStream::setFile(handle) (assert 'VolRStream::setFile: Bad file Handle.'): VolRStream_Close, adopt the handle without owning it, probe it with _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR); status 0 on success, else VolRStream_SetIoError. The 'errno == EBADF' tests before its asserts read the dword at 0046b6f6, which is the cw3220 _errno import thunk's own code bytes (FF 25 3C E3), not errno, so in this image they are never true.

entries.name: VolRStream_Close
entries.description: VolRStream::close. _close on the handle at +8 when the stream owns it (+0x26), releases the filters at +0x27 (RLERStream_Close) and +0x2b (LZHRStream_Close), zeroes the position fields +0xa, +0xe and +0x16, sets the handle to -1 and the status at +4 to 5. Returns 0 with status 3 if _close fails.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; class identified by VolRStream_Dtor's vtable

entries.name: VolRStream_Open
entries.description: VolRStream::open(path) from src\volrstrm.cpp. Closes, then tries _open(path, O_BINARY|O_RDONLY) first, so a loose file on disk overrides a volume entry of the same name. Otherwise looks the path up with VolumeGroup_FindEntry (g_VolumeGroup) and switches on the entry's compression type (the first byte of its 9-byte prefix): 2 reads the volume stream directly, 7 attaches the RLERStream at +0x27, 9 the LZHRStream at +0x2b (each created on first use, asserting 'Insufficient memory to allocate filter stream.'), anything else asserts 'Unknown compression type in volume file.'. Returns 1 with status 0 and +0x26 set, or 0 with status 1 when neither source has the file.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetGroup
entries.description: VolRStream::setGroup (assert 'VolRStream::setGroup: Insufficient memory...' in src\volrstrm.cpp): (a, b, c, d). Creates g_VolumeGroup (0x79 bytes, VolumeGroup_Ctor) on first use, otherwise passes the same arguments to VolumeGroup_SetGroup on the existing group.

entries.name: VolRStream_LoadVolume
entries.description: VolRStream::loadVolume (assert 'VolRStream::loadVolume: A volume group must be defined...' in src\volrstrm.cpp when g_VolumeGroup is null): passes path to VolumeGroup_LoadVolume on g_VolumeGroup.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetSize
entries.description: Returns a VolRStream's length: _filelength of the handle for a plain file, the entry size at +0x22 for an open volume entry, else 0.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +4: _lseek(h, 0, SEEK_CUR) for a file handle, else the position within the volume entry (+0x16), or 0 when no entry is open.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetPosition
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +8 (assert 'VolRStream::setPosition: Unknown compression type in volume file.'): (stream, pos). Clears an end-of-data status first. A file handle seeks with _lseek(h, pos, SEEK_SET), failure to VolRStream_SetIoError. A volume entry records pos at +0x16 and seeks the volume stream to data offset + pos; for type 7/9 it closes the filter, seeks the volume stream to the entry's data start, reopens the filter on it and seeks the filter to pos. A pos at or past the entry size sets status 2 and stores the size itself (not data offset + size) as the volume position.

entries.name: VolRStream_GetCapabilities
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0xc (assert 'VolRStream:getCapabilities: Unknown capability.'): answers capability queries 0-4. Query 0 is the compression type for a volume entry (2 for a plain file); 2 and 3 answer 1; 4 answers 1 only for a compressed volume entry; 1 answers 0.

entries.name: VolRStream_Flush
entries.description: VolRStream vtable 0046d014 slot +0x10: returns 1; a read stream has nothing to flush.

entries.name: VolRStream_SetIoError
entries.description: Sets the stream status at +4 to 1 when the dword at 0046b6f6 is nonzero, else 3, and returns 0. That dword is the _errno import thunk's code bytes (0xE33C25FF), so it always stores 1. Stream status codes at +4 seen in these classes: 0 ok, 1 I/O error, 2 end of data, 3 close failed, 4 write to a read-only stream, 5 no file, 6 filter stream not attached.

entries.name: VolRStream_Write
entries.description: VolRStream vtable slot +0x14: asserts 'VolRStream::write: Cannot write to read only stream.', sets status 4 and returns 0.

entries.name: VolRStream_Read
entries.description: VolRStream::read, vtable slot +0x18: (stream, count, buffer); returns nonzero on success, 0 with status set otherwise, and nothing when status is already nonzero. A file handle _reads; a short read sets status 2, an error goes to VolRStream_SetIoError. A volume entry first re-seeks (VolRStream_SetPosition) when the volume stream has moved from +0x1a, then reads through +0xe. When position + count passes the entry size it instead reads size - position + 1 bytes from the volume stream at +0xa, which is the rest of the entry plus the one-byte trailer after it, and sets status 2. The 'errno == EBADF' tests before its asserts read the dword at 0046b6f6, which is the cw3220 _errno import thunk's own code bytes (FF 25 3C E3), not errno, so in this image they are never true.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_Ctor
entries.description: (group, mask, extension, dir, dirFirst): clears the 0x1e volume pointers and the count byte +0x78, sets VolumeGroup_BufferSize to 0x400, then VolumeGroup_SetGroup(group, mask, extension, dir, dirFirst). VolRStream_SetGroup builds g_VolumeGroup (0x79 bytes) with it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's VolumeGroup_Ctor (00467a98).

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize
entries.description: (size): stores max(size, 0x80) in VolumeGroup_BufferSize. Shell_Main calls it with 0x200 immediately before the only VolRStream_SetGroup call; when that call creates the group, VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 over it before any volume is loaded.

entries.name: Path_JoinSkipDrive
entries.description: (dir, name): copies dir, or the empty string at 0046d077 when it is null, into the static buffer 00481144, appends name without a leading 'X:' drive prefix and returns the buffer. VolumeGroup_SetGroup builds each volume's path with it.

entries.name: Path_SkipDrive
entries.description: (path): returns path + 2 when path[1] is ':', else path. VolumeGroup_SetGroup compares loaded volume names through it.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_SetGroup
entries.description: VolumeGroup::setGroup (assert 'VolumeGroup::setGroup: Volume group FULL...' in src\volgroup.cpp): (group, mask, extension, dir, dirFirst). Removes the volumes whose flags +0x20 share no bit with mask (VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume; the volume that slides into a removed index is not tested). When the group holds 0x1e volumes it asserts and stops. Otherwise scans 'vol\*<extension>' with findfirst/findnext twice, once under dir and once without it (dirFirst nonzero puts the dir pass first), and adds each file whose 'vol\<name>' matches no loaded volume's name (+8, compared through Path_SkipDrive) with VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, Path_JoinSkipDrive(dir, name), mask). Shell_Main's call passes mask 0x100 and extension '.vol'.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00403723; strings at 0046d089, 0046d0d3 and 0046c4a9

entries.name: VolumeGroup_RemoveVolume
entries.description: VolumeGroup::removeVolume (asserts 'VolumeGroup::removeVolume: Index...' and '...NULL p...' in src\volgroup.cpp): (group, index). Volume_Dtor(volume, 3) on the volume at index, shifts the later pointers down one, decrements the count byte +0x78 and clears the freed last slot.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_AddVolume
entries.description: (group, path, mask): Volume_LoadVolume(path, mask, VolumeGroup_BufferSize) and, when it loads, inserts the volume so the list stays in descending order of the byte at volume +0x1c (read from the volume header), then increments the count byte +0x78.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_LoadVolume
entries.description: VolumeGroup::loadVolume (assert 'VolumeGroup::loadVolume: Volume group FULL, could not add any more to list.' in src\volgroup.cpp): (group, path). Returns 0 for a null path or a full group (0x1e volumes); otherwise, unless a loaded volume's name (+8) equals path, VolumeGroup_AddVolume(group, path, 0xffffffff); returns 1. VolRStream_LoadVolume calls it on g_VolumeGroup.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_FindEntry
entries.description: Tries Volume_FindEntry on each volume in a VolumeGroup (volume pointers from +0, count byte at +0x78) in order and returns 1 at the first hit. VolRStream_Open calls it on g_VolumeGroup.

entries.name: ClassItem_RegisterBucket
entries.description: (entries, count): appends an {entries, count} bucket to VshellClassItem_RegistryBuckets (count at 0046d1cc) unless count is 0. The static initialisers at 004529b8, 0045fa04 (g_TSObjectTypeRegistry), 0046370c and 00468168 register their class-item tables with it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's ClassItem_RegisterBucket (00479fac).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00403b98; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00479fac

entries.name: VshellClassItem_LoadItem
entries.description: classio.cpp, ClassItem::loadItem (confirmed via the literal assert string). VSHELL's own copy of the generic ClassItem registry-dispatch loader -- reads an 8-byte type tag via VshellClassItem_ReadTypeTag, looks up a handler via VshellClassItem_FindHandler, calls its loadFn(stream, mode). Structurally identical to but a separate compiled instance from DBSIM's ClassItem_LoadResource.

entries.name: ClassItem_StoreItem
entries.description: (item, stream, mode): the write counterpart of VshellClassItem_LoadItem. Points ClassItem_CurrentFrame at a local frame (restoring it after); when the item's stream size (vtable +4) is 0 and the stream's GetCapabilities(3) (vtable +0xc) returns 0, wraps the stream in a local BuffWStream (BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget) and writes through that: 00404208 writes the type tag from the item's class tag and size, the item's WriteToStream (vtable +0x10) follows with mode, 00404392 closes the item, then the BuffWStream is destroyed (BuffWStream_Dtor with 2). Otherwise the same three steps straight onto the stream. The part lists, TSGroup, ANShape and ANAnimList write their children with it.

entries.name: Arena_Alloc2
entries.description: A second copy of Arena_Alloc (00403dc4) with an identical body. (size, arena{base, capacity, used}): bump-allocates size bytes from the arena, returning base + used and advancing used; with no arena, or when the request would pass the capacity, falls back to Mem_NewArray(size). GLFont_ReadFromStream allocates its variable-length blocks with it.

entries.name: Arena_Alloc
entries.description: (size, arena): carves size bytes from an arena (+0 base, +4 capacity, +8 bytes used) and advances it; with no arena, or when the arena lacks room, falls back to Mem_NewArray. The 3Space part constructors (TSSolidPoly_Construct, TSTexture4Poly_Construct) and GLFont_Construct allocate through it.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_FindHandler
entries.description: Searches VSHELL's registry (bucket base VshellClassItem_RegistryBuckets, count-global at 0046d1cc) for a matching type-tag id, returns a 12-byte {id, loadFn, extra} descriptor. VSHELL's copy of ClassItem_FindHandler. Note: the registry itself is populated by C++ static initializers at runtime, so it reads as empty/zero in the static binary image -- don't try to walk it directly, trace call graphs from a known class-id literal instead (see GLFont_GetClassTag).

entries.name: VshellClassItem_TryEveryLoader
entries.description: (stream, tag): walks the registry buckets at 004812e8 ({entries, count}, count of buckets 0046d1d0) and calls each 12-byte entry's loadFn (+4) with (00481338, tag, stream), returning 1 at the first that returns nonzero and 0 when none does. VshellClassItem_ReadTypeTag and 00403e00 call it. VSHELL's copy of ClassItem_TryEveryLoader.

entries.name: ClassItem_TagTotalSize
entries.description: (tag): an item's total length from its 8-byte class type tag: the size dword at +4 as it is when the high nibble of byte 3 is set, else size + 8 (the tag itself) rounded up to an even length. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's ClassItem_TagTotalSize.

entries.name: ClassItem_ItemTotalSize
entries.description: (item): the bytes the item occupies in a stream with its 8-byte type tag: builds {tag = vtable slot 0, size = vtable slot +4} and returns ClassItem_TagTotalSize of it, or 0 when the item's stream size is 0. The part lists', groups' and ANAnimList's GetStreamSize sum it over their children.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType
entries.description: The class-item interface's debug print, slot +0x14 of ClassItem's vtable and of every class that does not override it (GLFont, the GL classes, TSBase and its unspecialised subclasses): (item, verbose, indent) writes indent spaces to stdout, then 'Class type: %d %d' from the item's class tag (vtable slot 0), and, when VshellClassItem_FindHandler finds the tag's registry entry, its third field -- the class name, as the GL, AN and TS class-item tables show -- as ' %s ', then a newline. Overrides such as TSPoly's call it first and add their own fields when verbose is set. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047a488.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00404120; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00404120 DBSIM 0047a488; class-item tables 0047bcd0, 0047f750, 0047f258

entries.name: ClassItem_FormatError
entries.description: (format): sprintf(format, the class name of the current frame's handler -- VshellClassItem_FindHandler(*ClassItem_CurrentFrame) + 8, or '[No class entry]') into a 256-byte stack buffer, which is then dropped: nothing is printed or returned. ClassItem_CloseItem reports an overread through it.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_ReadTypeTag
entries.description: Reads the 8-byte type tag ([typeId][0x0028][totalSize]) from a resource stream, called by VshellClassItem_LoadItem. VSHELL's copy of ClassItem_ReadTypeTag.

entries.name: ClassItem_CloseItem
entries.description: ClassItem::closeItem (src32\classio.cpp): (stream). Asserts (line 0x288) that ClassItem_CurrentFrame is set; when the stream position (vtable +4) is already past the frame's end (+8), reports 'ClassItem::closeItem:%s: Have read more than declared class size.' through 004041cd; then reads single bytes (vtable +0x18) until the stream status goes non-zero or the position reaches the end. VshellClassItem_LoadItem runs it after the item's loader.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Ctor
entries.description: DVKeyboard::DVKeyboard (assert 'DVKeyboard::DVKeyboard: Attempt construct multiple times' in src\dv_ky.cpp): (this) GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 1, this); when this is the claimed keyboard (0048e164) and 00404663 succeeds, registers atexit 0040456c, assert hook 0040456d and KeyListener_Register(this, 00404677, an empty code list). WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor builds it at +0x10. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's KeyboardDriver_Ctor.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Dtor
entries.description: DVKeyboard destructor (assert 'DVKeyboard::DVKeyboard: Attempt to destroy multiple times' in src\dv_ky.cpp when 0048e164 is already clear): (this, flags) 00404670 and clears the claimed keyboard 0048e164, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. WinKeyboardProducer_Dtor runs it on +0x10.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Init
entries.description: (this): returns bit 0 of the keyboard's first dword and does nothing else. DVKeyboard_Ctor registers the keyboard's handlers only when it returns non-zero.

entries.name: DVKeyboard_Shutdown
entries.description: Returns 0 and does nothing else. DVKeyboard_Dtor calls it.

entries.name: Keyboard_PopKey
entries.description: (keyboard): pops the next 16-bit key code off the keyboard ring (256 words at 004813bc, read index 004815c0, write index 004815bc) and returns it, 0 when the ring is empty; clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags when it empties the ring. Keyboard_PostEvents drains the ring with it; ShellMap_RunIntro and Avi_Play read keys with it directly.

entries.name: KeyListener_Register
entries.description: (unused, callback, wantedCodes): stores {1, wantedCodes, callback} in the first free of the ten 12-byte slots at 004815c4 and returns 1, or 0 when all ten are taken. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's KeyListener_Register; KeyListener_RegisterCopy is byte-identical. DVKeyboard_Ctor and WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor (callback 00408f3e, codes Key_CommandFilter) register through it.

entries.name: KeyListener_RegisterCopy
entries.description: A byte-identical copy of KeyListener_Register (004047ca) at a different address, as in DBSIM. WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor registers callback 00404677 with a 255-byte code list (1..255) through it.

entries.name: Keyboard_FlushKeys
entries.description: (keyboard): empties the keyboard ring (read index = write index) and clears bit 1 (keys pending) of the keyboard object's flags. ShellMap_RunIntro calls it before its loop.

entries.name: DVMouse_Ctor
entries.description: DVMouse::DVMouse (assert 'DVMouse::DVMouse: Attempt to construct multiple times' in src32\dv_mse.cpp): (this) GL_ClaimGlobal(this, 2, this); when this is the claimed mouse (0048e168) and 004053bf succeeds, registers assert hook 0040550a. WinMouseProducer_Ctor builds it at +0x10. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's MouseDriver_Ctor.

entries.name: DVMouse_Dtor
entries.description: DVMouse::~DVMouse (assert 'DVMouse::~DVMouse: Attempt to destroy multiple times' in src32\dv_mse.cpp when 0048e168 is already clear): (this, flags) 0040541b(this) and clears the claimed mouse 0048e168, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. WinMouseProducer_Dtor runs it on +0x10.

entries.name: DVMouse_Init
entries.description: (this): when bit 0 of the mouse's first dword is set, calls 0040550f(this, 1), 00405446 on +0x24 and on +0xe, sets the four dwords at +0xe to 0, 0, 480, 640 and passes +0xe to 00405470. Returns that bit. DVMouse_Ctor registers its assert hook only when it returns non-zero.

entries.name: DVMouse_Shutdown
entries.description: (this): when bit 0 of the mouse's first dword is set, clears that dword, passes +0x24 to 00405470 and returns 1; otherwise returns 0. DVMouse_Dtor calls it.

entries.name: MouseDriver_SetBounds
entries.description: (driver, record): sets the bounds rect at driver+0xe..+0x1a from the record's first four ints and the shorts at driver+0x1e/+0x20/+0x22 from its +0x10/+0x12/+0x14. DVMouse_Init passes the driver's own +0xe record, DVMouse_Shutdown the one at +0x24. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's MouseDriver_SetBounds (00480658).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00405470; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00480658

entries.name: MouseDriver_SetBoundsRect
entries.description: (driver, rect): copies the four ints of rect into the pointer's bounds at driver+0xe..+0x1a.

entries.name: MouseListener_Register
entries.description: (unused, callback, eventMask): stores {1, eventMask, callback} in the first free of the ten 12-byte slots at 00481780 and returns the slot index, or 0xffff in the low word when all ten are taken. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's MouseListener_Register.

entries.name: Display_SetDrawOrigin
entries.description: (unused, point): points the back-buffer surface's draw pointer ([00481834]+0xa, mirrored at [0046d73c]) at (x, y) using the pitch at +2, and stores the point as the present destination 0048185c/00481860.

entries.name: Display_PresentStoredRect
entries.description: Display_PresentRect with the stored destination point 0048185c and source rect 0048183c. Mission_OnMapUp/Down/Left/Right call it.

entries.name: Display_PresentRegion
entries.description: (rect): presents rect offset by the stored source origin 0048183c and destination 0048185c (and, when [0048e184]+0x20c is set, by that object's scroll offset) through Display_PresentRect.

entries.name: Shell_PumpMessages
entries.description: Drains the Windows message queue with PeekMessageA(PM_REMOVE), translating and dispatching each message; bumps the counter at 0046d748 and prints it to the DarkMono monitor ('counter: %d', Mono_Printf at 40,2) per message. Returns 1 as soon as it sees WM_QUIT (0x12), 0 once the queue is empty.

entries.name: Display_ResetGlobals
entries.description: Zeroes the back-buffer globals (bitmap header 00481864, display 00481868, bits 0048186c, memory DC 00481878, DIB 0048187c, palette 00481870, sound timer id 00481e4c), sets the size to 640 x 480 (00481884, 00481888) and the BITMAPINFOHEADER at 00481890 to size 0x28, one plane, 8 bits. Shell_CreateMainWindow runs it first.

entries.name: Display_Init
entries.description: Shell_CreateMainWindow's display setup once the window exists: GL_RegisterClassItems, Light_ResetSystem and AN_RegisterClassItems; the 15 ms sound-service timer (id 1, sfxWndProc, id kept at 00481e4c); a memory DC (00481878); the system palette into 004818b8 with red and blue swapped in each entry; a top-down 8-bit DIB section of the back buffer's size (bits 0048186c; 'Bad WinGBitmap' when it fails) selected into the DC; a 0xe-byte bitmap header over it (00481864); a GLDisplay of kind 'BMP 8' on that header (00481868), reopened by GLDisplay_OpenWithSize with half the width and height; then Gfx_SelectRenderTarget and GLDisplay_SetAttribute(9, 0).

entries.name: Shell_EmptyExitStep
entries.description: Returns at once. Shell_Main's four error exits and MainWndProc's message-2 path call it just before SfxTimer_Kill.

entries.name: SfxTimer_Kill
entries.description: KillTimer on the shell's sound-service timer: the 15 ms timer (id 1, callback sfxWndProc) that Display_Init creates on window 00481e54 and whose id it keeps at 00481e4c; nothing when that id is 0. Display_ToggleFullScreen calls it.

entries.name: Shell_RegisterWindowClass
entries.description: (hInstance): loads BWCC.DLL and registers the window class 'shell': MainWndProc, icon 'es2icon', the arrow cursor, no background brush. Shell_WinMain calls it when there is no previous instance.

entries.name: Shell_CreateMainWindow
entries.description: (hInstance, nCmdShow): Display_ResetGlobals, then creates the 'EarthSiege II' window of class 'shell' centred on the desktop with a 640 x 480 client area, or the whole screen and topmost when 0046d740 (option 6, full screen) is set. On failure SfxTimer_Kill and returns 0; otherwise Display_Init, ShowWindow, UpdateWindow unless full screen, and returns 1.

entries.name: Shell_SplitCommandLine
entries.description: (cmdLine, argv): argv[0] = 'dbsim', then each space-separated word copied into a Mem_NewArray block; returns the count. Shell_WinMain passes the result to Shell_Main.

entries.name: Shell_WinMain
entries.description: (hInstance, hPrevInstance, cmdLine, nCmdShow): Shell_SplitCommandLine; Shell_RegisterWindowClass for a first instance; a -d or /d argument clears 0046d740, which ShellOptions_Init's option 6 (ShellOption_DisplayMode) then overwrites; Shell_CreateMainWindow ('Unable to initialize Instance' on failure); the joystick count and capabilities with threshold 0x200; Display_ToggleFullScreen when 0046d740 is set; Shell_BlankScreen; Shell_Main with the split arguments; Shell_PumpMessages until WM_QUIT; Display_ReleaseDirectDraw; returns Shell_GetExitCode.

entries.name: Display_PresentRect
entries.description: (destPoint, srcRect): copies a rectangle of the 8-bit back buffer to the screen. Without DirectDraw (00481e68 clear): BitBlt from the memory DC 00481878 with the palette 00481870 selected, inside BeginPaint/EndPaint. With DirectDraw: restores a lost primary surface (00481e5c), locks it and copies rows from the back buffer 0048186c (dimensions at [00481864]), clamped to 640x480.

entries.name: Palette_CopyEntries
entries.description: (dst, first, count): copies count dwords from the palette entry table at 00481e70, starting at entry first. Avi_BuildPalette takes entries 10-245 with it.

entries.name: Palette_CreateForDisplay
entries.description: (quads, count): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Palette_CreateForDisplay, building the LOGPALETTE at 00481e6c, except that in SYSPAL_NOSTATIC use it flags the copied entries 5 (PC_RESERVED | PC_NOCOLLAPSE) where DBSIM flags them 1. Display_RealizePalette makes its result the palette 00481870.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0040698f, compared with DBSIM 00465920

entries.name: Palette_ClearSystemPalette
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Palette_ClearSystemPalette: realizes and deletes an all-black palette flagged 5 on the screen DC. Display_RealizePalette runs it first.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00406bb9, diffed against DBSIM 00465b3c

entries.name: Display_RealizePalette
entries.description: (palette): does nothing unless 0046c080 is set. Counts its calls at 0046db80 (Mono_Printf '%d times in realize palette'), converts the palette's 256 entries (+8) to RGBQUADs as DBSIM's Screen_SetPalette does (flags bit 0: 6-bit, shifted left 2; otherwise copied only with flags bit 1), runs Palette_ClearSystemPalette, makes Palette_CreateForDisplay(quads, 256) the palette 00481870, selects and realizes it on the screen DC and sets the DIB colour table of 00481878. Full screen (00481e68) it also flags entries 10-245 5, creates a DirectDraw palette (IDirectDraw slot +0x14, flags 0x4c) into 00481e64 and sets it on the primary 00481e5c (slot +0x7c), asserting 'create pal failed' (winstuff.cpp) on failure. Palette_ApplyToDisplay calls it.

entries.name: Vshell_LoadItemFromPath
entries.description: (path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath and loads one item with VshellClassItem_LoadItem, asserting (winstuff.cpp lines 0x2eb, 0x2ee) when the open or the load fails, and returns the item. Shell_InstallPalette loads its .dpl with it.

entries.name: Display_CreateDirectDrawExclusive
entries.description: DirectDrawCreate into 00481e58, then IDirectDraw::SetCooperativeLevel (vtable +0x50) with the window 00481e54 and flags 0x17 (FULLSCREEN | ALLOWREBOOT | NOWINDOWCHANGES | EXCLUSIVE). Returns 1 when both succeed, else 0. Display_ToggleFullScreen calls it on the way into full screen.

entries.name: DDraw_SetModeAndCreatePrimary
entries.description: (width, height, bpp): IDirectDraw::SetDisplayMode on 00481e58 (slot +0x54); on success releases 00481e60, the primary 00481e5c and the palette 00481e64, and creates a single primary surface (caps 0x4200) into 00481e5c, retrying once without DDSCAPS_VIDEOMEMORY; a second failure asserts 'coulnd't create dd surface' (winstuff.cpp). Returns 1 on success. DBSIM's DDraw_SetModeAndCreateSurfaces without the ModeX flip chain. Display_ToggleFullScreen calls it.

entries.name: Display_ReleaseDirectDraw
entries.description: Releases the four DirectDraw interface pointers 00481e60, 00481e5c, 00481e64 and 00481e58 through their COM Release slot (vtable +8), zeroing each. Display_ToggleFullScreen calls it.

entries.name: Display_ToggleFullScreen
entries.description: Flips the shell between windowed and full screen (flag 00481e68, which Display_PresentRect branches on). Entering: an exclusive DirectDraw object (00406eb5), a display mode of the back buffer's size at 8 bits and the primary surface (00406eeb), a topmost window with its frame pushed off the screen, the first and last ten palette entries flagged 5 and a palette (IDirectDraw slot +0x14) set on the primary surface (slot +0x7c), the cursor clipped to the screen and centred; on failure 004062b0 and PostQuitMessage. Leaving: clears those palette flags, releases the DirectDraw objects (00407011) and re-centres the window at its framed size. Behaviour and callers: docs/shell/screen-layout.md.

entries.name: Display_LeaveFullScreen
entries.description: Display_ToggleFullScreen when full screen (00481e68 set), otherwise nothing. Callers: Movie_PlayQueue, OnlineManual_Open, StartupAnim_OnTick, ShellSound_Init.

entries.name: Shell_BlankScreen
entries.description: Fills the window with palette index 0: windowed, zeroes the shell bitmap and StretchBlts 10x10 of it over the client rect; full screen (DAT_00481e68), locks the primary surface and zeroes every row. QUIT's handler calls it.

entries.name: Shell_OpenHelp
entries.description: WinHelpA(main window, path, HELP_CONTENTS, 0).

entries.name: Shell_InstallPalette
entries.description: esglobal.cpp. Frees the palette at 0046dcd0 and loads dpl\<name>.dpl named by index into the 20-entry table at 0046dcdc, then sets the dirty flag at 0046dcd8.

entries.name: Shell_CommitPalette
entries.description: Installs the palette loaded by Shell_InstallPalette to the display when 0046dcd8 is set, then clears it.

entries.name: ShellRandom_StaticInitMain
entries.description: Static initialiser (stored pointer at 00480fc4): ShellRandom_Reset(0x482325), the main shell generator. Ghidra has no function here. ShellRandom_Seed resets the state again before any campaign draw.

entries.name: Memory_Init
entries.description: Initialises a src\mymem.cpp pool over a caller-supplied buffer: (pool, size, buffer). Stores base and size, makes the whole buffer one free block of size & ~7 tagged 'KLBF', and sets the free and lowest-free byte counts to that size. The pool object (e.g. 0048239c): +0 base, +4 byte size, +8 free-list head, +0xc free bytes, +0x10 lowest free bytes seen. Every block starts with an 8-byte header: an allocated block holds 'KLBA' (0x41424c4b) at +0 and its size including the header at +4, the caller's data at +8; a free block holds the next free block at +0, its size at +4 and 'KLBF' (0x46424c4b) at +8. Called once at startup (00401576) for the shell pool 0048239c, with a buffer of [0046c090] bytes from Mem_NewArray.

entries.name: Memory_IsAllocatedBlock
entries.description: Returns 1 when ptr (a data pointer, header at ptr-8) lies inside the pool's [base, base+size) and its header holds 'KLBA'. Memory_Free, Memory_Realloc, Mem_Delete and Mem_DeleteArray use it to tell pool blocks from heap blocks.

entries.name: Memory_IsBlockHeader
entries.description: Returns 1 when a header address lies in [base, base+size-0x10] and is tagged either as a free block ('KLBF' at +8) or an allocated one ('KLBA' at +0). The free-list walks in Memory_Alloc and Memory_Free assert on it.

entries.name: Memory_CheckOverrun
entries.description: The 'Block overrun' check behind Memory_Free and Memory_Realloc. Fails when Memory_IsAllocatedBlock fails; passes when the block ends exactly at base + [pool+4]*8; otherwise returns Memory_IsBlockHeader of the block's own header (ptr-8), not of the header that follows it. [pool+4] is a byte count (Memory_Init), so the *8 end test only matches a block ending far past the pool, and for any block that passed Memory_IsAllocatedBlock the fallback re-tests a header already known good: as coded, the check does not inspect the bytes after the block.

entries.name: Memory_LargestFreeBlock
entries.description: Returns the size of the largest block on the pool's free list minus 0x6c, clamped to 0. Mem_New and Mem_NewArray send a request to the pool only when it is below the pool's free byte count (004823a8, pool +0xc) and no larger than this.

entries.name: Memory_Alloc
entries.description: Memory::alloc from src\mymem.cpp: (pool, size, trackLow). First fit over the free list for (size + 15) & ~7 bytes; an exact fit unlinks the block, a larger one is split when at least 0x10 bytes would remain. Tags the block 'KLBA', zeroes the data, subtracts from the free byte count and, when trackLow is nonzero, lowers the lowest-free mark at +0x10. Returns header + 8, or 0 after asserting 'Memory::alloc: Allocation failed'. Asserts 'Free list corrupted' when a list entry fails Memory_IsBlockHeader. The pool object (e.g. 0048239c): +0 base, +4 byte size, +8 free-list head, +0xc free bytes, +0x10 lowest free bytes seen. Every block starts with an 8-byte header: an allocated block holds 'KLBA' (0x41424c4b) at +0 and its size including the header at +4, the caller's data at +8; a free block holds the next free block at +0, its size at +4 and 'KLBF' (0x46424c4b) at +8.

entries.name: Memory_Free
entries.description: Memory::free from src\mymem.cpp: (pool, ptr). Asserts 'Memory::free: Bad pointer' unless Memory_IsAllocatedBlock, and 'Block overrun' unless Memory_CheckOverrun. Adds the block size back to the free count, tags it 'KLBF', inserts it into the address-ordered free list (asserting 'Free list corrupted' on a bad entry) and coalesces it with the free blocks on either side. A null ptr is ignored.

entries.name: Memory_Realloc
entries.description: Memory::realloc from src\mymem.cpp: (pool, ptr, newSize). newSize 0 frees and returns 0. Asserts 'Memory::realloc:: Bad pointer' / 'Block overrun' like Memory_Free. Shrinks in place (giving the tail to a following free block, or splitting it off as its own block when over 0x10 bytes), grows in place into a following free block when it has room, and otherwise allocates, copies and frees. Updates the lowest-free mark. Returns the (possibly moved) pointer.

entries.name: Memory_DrawUsageMap
entries.description: Draws the shell pool 0048239c as a cols x rows grid of characters on the DarkMono debug monitor: (unused, x, y, cols, rows). Walks the pool with Memory_BlockIterBegin/Next, giving each cell an equal share of the pool's bytes, and prints one CP437 character per cell with Mono_Printf('%c'): 07 for no allocated bytes, B1 under 50%, B2 under 100%, DB fully allocated.

entries.name: Memory_PrevLinkedHeader
entries.description: Memory::prevLinkedHeader from src\mymem.cpp: (pool, freeBlock). Returns the free-list entry that links to freeBlock, 0 when freeBlock is the list head. Asserts 'Block is not free' when freeBlock is tagged 'KLBA', and 'Free list corrupted' when no entry links to it. Memory_Realloc uses it to relink a free block it moved.

entries.name: Memory_BlockIterBegin
entries.description: Starts a walk over every block in a pool, free or allocated: (iter, pool) sets iter[0] = pool and iter[1] = the pool base (the first header). Memory_BlockIterNext advances it.

entries.name: Memory_BlockIterNext
entries.description: Advances a Memory_BlockIterBegin walk by the current header's size (+4) and returns the next header, or 0 (and clears the iterator) once past base + size.

entries.name: maybe_Memory_OperatorNew
entries.description: Memory_Alloc(pool, size, 1) with its arguments taken as (size, pool). The name assumes the argument order is that of a class placement operator new(size_t, Memory*); the image has no string for it.

entries.name: Mem_HeapAlloc
entries.description: Mem_New's path for a block the pool will not take: _calloc(1, size), then adds the heap block's size word at p[-4] to the heap byte count at 004823b0, which Mem_Delete subtracts from. Returns the _calloc pointer in EAX (the decompile drops the return).

entries.name: Mem_New
entries.description: The global operator new, used for every heap object in the shell -- widgets, events, streams. A size below g_ShellPool's free byte count (004823a8, pool +0xc) and no larger than Memory_LargestFreeBlock is carved from that pool by Memory_Alloc; anything else goes to Mem_HeapAlloc (004080ec). Either way the block is returned zeroed. Mem_Delete is its pair; Mem_NewArray is the same routine with 8 bytes added to the size.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; src\mymem.cpp assert strings in the pool routines; callers include Window_RepaintRecursive and FileWStream users

entries.name: Mem_NewArray
entries.description: The global array operator new (the name is the C++ convention; the image has no string for it). Mem_New's body with 8 added to the size: g_ShellPool via Memory_Alloc when the size fits, else Mem_HeapAlloc; zeroed. Returns the block start, so the 8 extra bytes are unused slack. Rtl_VectorNew allocates through it, and callers pass count * element size (e.g. the three byte buffers in 0044f65c, the tables in MsnGen_ParseMsnFile).

entries.name: Mem_Delete
entries.description: The global operator delete. A pointer for which Memory_IsAllocatedBlock holds (inside g_ShellPool, header tag 'KLBA') goes back to the pool through Memory_Free; anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 004823b0. Mem_DeleteArray has the identical body. Pairs with Mem_New.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile; src\mymem.cpp assert strings in the pool routines

entries.name: Mem_DeleteArray
entries.description: The global array operator delete (the name is the C++ convention). Body identical to Mem_Delete: a 'KLBA' block inside the pool at 0048239c goes to Memory_Free, anything else is _free'd and its size at p[-1] subtracted from the heap byte count at 004823b0. Rtl_VectorDelete frees through it; destructor 0044f69c frees its member buffers with it and the object itself with Mem_Delete. Some Mem_NewArray blocks are released with Mem_Delete instead (0042be3c's failure path), which is harmless as the two bodies match.

entries.name: WeaponsBin_LookupName
entries.description: Bounds-checked weapon-name lookup into weapons.bin by weapon id (offsets[id] + stringPoolStart). Structure verified byte-exact against the real retail file in ES2/VOL/LANG0.VOL.

entries.name: Text_LoadDataFile
entries.description: Text::loadDataFile, named by its assert string (ctxt.cpp line 0x3f): (text, stream) reads two dword counts into +8 and +0xc, then +8 * 2 bytes into a new array at +0 and +0xc bytes into a new array at +4, all through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18). Returns true when the stream status (+4) is 0. WeaponsBin_Open calls it.

entries.name: Path_GetDataPrefix
entries.description: Returns the path prefix the utility.cpp loaders (loadDBM, loadDBA, loadText) copy ahead of a file name: the empty string at 0046e238. TSBase_LoadDba and WeaponsBin_Open call it.

entries.name: Util_LoadDBM
entries.description: loadDBM (asserts in src\utility.cpp): (name). Opens Path_GetDataPrefix() + name with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserting the open, loads one class item from it (VshellClassItem_LoadItem), asserting it loaded, closes the stream and returns the item. MainMenu_BuildScreen loads its art with it.

entries.name: TSBase_LoadDba
entries.description: Prefixes the install-root path onto the given relative .dba path, loads it through VshellClassItem_LoadItem (the same generic Dynamix ClassItem-registry resource loader used for .DFN/.DCI, see project_es2_exe_recon memory). Returns the loaded DBA handle later bound into a TSShapeInstance's +0x26 field or read via array[frame] by TSBitmapPart_Render. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: WeaponsBin_Open
entries.description: Opens weapons.bin by its literal filename string found in VSHELL.EXE.

entries.name: Shell_SetExitCode
entries.description: Stores the shell's exit code in 0046e210; 2 launches the simulator, 5 a demo.

entries.name: Shell_GetExitCode
entries.description: Returns the int16 exit code at 0046e210 that Shell_SetExitCode stores (the decompile drops the return). Shell_Main and Shell_WinMain read it.

entries.name: Shell_SetBusyCursor
entries.description: SetCursor(LoadCursorA(NULL, busy ? IDC_WAIT : IDC_ARROW)), then ShowCursor(1). Called by MainMenu_OnContinue around its load, Movie_PlayQueue and Avi_Play.

entries.name: Shell_ReadLanguageCfg
entries.description: Opens data\language.cfg with FileRStream_Ctor (asserting at utility.cpp line 0xb7 when that fails), reads one byte, closes it and returns the byte in AL. OnlineManual_Open calls it.

entries.name: WinMouseProducer_Ctor
entries.description: WinMouseProducer constructor (vtable 0046e448 at +4, RTTI name 'WinMouseProducer', 0x574 bytes): (this, owner) runs the base EventProducer_Ctor, constructs +0x10 (DVMouse_Ctor) and 100 13-byte records at +0x5c, sets +0xc = 8 and +0xe = 4, asserts (wsrc\prdwmse.cpp line 0x1c) that the single instance 004823b4 is unset and stores this there, WinMouseProducer_SetCentre(this), vtable slot 0, Mono_Printf's the display's width and height, then MouseDriver_SetBoundsRect(+0x10, {0, 0, width, height}) and MouseListener_Register(+0x10, 00408b03, 0x1f). Shell_Main builds it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00408858; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: WinMouseProducer_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): reinstalls the vtable 0046e448, DVMouse_Dtor(+0x10, 2), the base EventProducer_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Shell_Main runs it with 3.

entries.name: WinMouseProducer_SetCentre
entries.description: (producer): stores half the current display's width (GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0) at +0x4a and half its height (attribute 1) at +0x4e. WinMouseProducer_Ctor calls it.

entries.name: WinMouseProducer_Reset
entries.description: WinMouseProducer vtable 0046e448 slot 0 (producer): zeroes +0x52, +0x56 and +0x5a and empties the 100-entry mouse ring by zeroing its read index +0x570 and write index +0x572. WinMouseProducer_Ctor calls it through the vtable. WinKeyboardProducer_Reset fills the same slot for the keyboard; EventProducer's own is Rtl_PureError.

entries.name: Mouse_QueueRecord
entries.description: (mouse, a, b, code): appends a 13-byte {a, b, code byte, GetTickCount()} record to the 100-entry ring at mouse+0x5c (tail +0x572, head +0x570), Mono_Printf'ing the tick; when the tail catches the head the oldest record is dropped. Mouse_OnButtonState queues through it.

entries.name: Mouse_OnButtonState
entries.description: Turns a change of mouse button state into queued mouse records: sub-code 0 for a move, 2/1 for the left button going down/up, 4/3 for the right.

entries.name: WinMouseProducer_PostEvents
entries.description: WinMouseProducer vtable 0046e448 slot +4 (producer): drains the mouse ring from +0x570 to +0x572, the 13-byte records at +0x5c ({x +0, y +4, sub-code byte +8, time +9}), wrapping at 100: each becomes a WinMouseEvent (MouseEvent_Ctor) with +6 = 4, no target (+0x20 = 0), the time at +8, the sub-code at +0x24 and, for sub-code 0 (a move) only, the position at +0x10/+0x14 (0, 0 otherwise), appended to the producer's event vector +8 (PtrVector_Append_Thunk). The mouse twin of Keyboard_PostEvents, which fills the keyboard producer's same slot.

entries.name: WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor
entries.description: WinKeyboardProducer constructor (vtable 0046e6c0 at +4, RTTI name 'WinKeyboardProducer', 0x54 bytes): (this, owner) runs the base EventProducer_Ctor, constructs +0x10 (DVKeyboard_Ctor), stores this at 004823b8, sets +0xc = 8 and +0xe = 4, vtable slot 0, KeyListener_Register(+0x10, 00408f3e, 0046e450), and KeyListener_RegisterCopy(+0x10, 00404677, a 255-byte table 1..255). Shell_Main builds it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00408dec; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: WinKeyboardProducer_Dtor
entries.description: (this, flags): reinstalls the vtable 0046e6c0, DVKeyboard_Dtor(+0x10, 2), the base EventProducer_Dtor(this, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Shell_Main runs it with 3.

entries.name: WinKeyboardProducer_Reset
entries.description: WinKeyboardProducer vtable 0046e6c0 slot 0 (producer): zeroes the int16s +0x50 and +0x52. WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor calls it through the vtable.

entries.name: Keyboard_PostEvents
entries.description: Drains the keyboard object's command buffer into command events (0x100, code from 0046e471 at the key code) and its key ring into character events (0x40, from 0046e571 or with Shift 0046e5c5, upper-cased; Ctrl+Q posts its own event). Every event goes out with no target.

entries.name: Shell_ShutdownDevicesAndSound
entries.description: Devices_Shutdown, then ShellSound_Shutdown. Called at the shell main loop's exit and by the switch parser after -v and -?, which runs before Devices_Init and ShellSound_Init, so there it releases nothing.

entries.name: WinConsumer_Ctor
entries.description: WinConsumer constructor (vtable 0046e7d0 at +4, RTTI name 'WinConsumer', 0x10 bytes): (this, owner) runs the base EventConsumer_Ctor, sets +0xe = 6 and +0xc = 8. Shell_Main builds it with the owner 004810f4, as it does the two producers.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004093b4; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: WinConsumer_HandleEvent
entries.description: WinConsumer vtable 0046e7d0 slot 0 (consumer, event): traces the event to the mono debug monitor (Mono_Printf: cursor position, event type, then Mouse/Key/Command type) and turns command events (0x100) into pointer actions by the code at +0x24: 4/5/6/7 move the pointer 8 pixels left, up, right and down (Display_GetCursorPos, then Pointer_MoveTo); 10 posts a left-down mouse event (sub-code 2) and 0x1d a left-up (1) at the pointer state's position (DAT_005ddbd0 +1) through Event_Post; 0x11 runs Pointer_Unlock and Alert_Show(QuitAlert). Then posts the event on with Event_Post.

entries.name: WinButton_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of RTTI class WinButton (vtable 0046e810, 0x4d bytes), one level above ESWindow_Ctor: sets its vtable (slot 0 WinButton_HandleEvent, slot +4 Rtl_PureError), zeroes the lit flag +0x45, ORs 0x60 into the event mask +0x39 -- the 0x20 bit is what lets the widget take mouse events -- sets the enable flag +0x49 = 1, then Window_ShowRecursive. ESRect_Ctor and so every ESRect-derived class (ESButtonFont, ESRegionFill, ESTitle, ESGrid, ESBitmap, ESArm, ESQuad) goes through it; ESMessage_Ctor does not.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: WinButton_HandleEvent
entries.description: WinButton's event handler (vtable 0046e810 slot 0), inherited as slot 0 by ESRect, ESRegionFill, ESTitle, ESGrid and ESQuad. Mouse events (type 0x20) are acted on only while the enable flag +0x49 is set and DAT_00470d70 and DAT_00470e70 are clear. Sub-code 2 or 4 (a press) lights +0x45 and repaints; 1 or 3 (a release) with +0x45 lit calls Window_DispatchCallback, clears +0x45, repaints; the leave event 0x10 clears +0x45. Nothing is passed to the parent, so a widget with no handler, or a disabled one, swallows the click. Type 4 is a repaint, type 2 the hidden event.

entries.name: Input_InitEventTime
entries.description: (obj): Input_EventTime = GetTickCount(). Devices_Init runs it on a 1-byte object.

entries.name: ESWindow_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of RTTI class ESWindow (vtable 0046e828, 0x45 bytes), the lowest widget level: writes its base Window's vtable (004717dc) then its own (slot 0 Window_DispatchCallback) last, zeroes +0x11 and the event mask +0x39, and calls Window_SetRect(widget, parent, rect, handler) -- the 4th argument is the click handler stored at +0x3d. ESMessage_Ctor and ESDialog_Ctor build on this directly rather than on WinButton_Ctor.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: WinButton_Erase
entries.description: WinButton_HandleEvent's and ESArm_HandleEvent's event 2, which hiding a widget posts: Window_BeginPaint, then fills a rect of the widget's own size (+0x2d - +0x25 by +0x31 - +0x29, normalised when negative) at the paint origin with colour {0, 0x10} installed at the drawing context's +0x22c.

entries.name: ESButtonFont_Ctor
entries.description: Plain button widget class, no icon slot (0x5d=93-byte struct, 18 uses -- smaller than ESButtonBitmap_Ctor's 0x69). Same embedded-ESMessage_Ctor-child pattern as ESButtonBitmap_Ctor for its caption, but via ESRect_Ctor's base rather than passing a callback through WinButton_Ctor's base-init call directly.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESButtonFont_HandleEvent
entries.description: The button's mouse handler. Plays the hover/press sound (0042eecf) on mouse sub-events 2 and 4 when the widget is enabled and sound is on, then defers to WinButton_HandleEvent unconditionally. The +0x49 test here gates only the sound, not the dispatch.

entries.name: ESButtonFont_Paint
entries.description: Button's paint: ESRect_FillAndBorder with the fill, a second border one pixel inside in +0x4d, then the caption, one pixel lower while lit and enabled.

entries.name: ESButtonBitmap_Ctor
entries.description: Button-with-icon widget class (0x69=105-byte struct, 17 uses). Passes a click-callback function pointer straight through the widget's base constructor (confirmed at the ServiceBay_BuildScreen call sites: per-weapon-slot handlers FUN_00439f2d/FUN_00439fdc/FUN_0043a0d8/etc, one per weapon-buy button, each ~0xfa/250 bytes apart matching the per-row screen layout). Also constructs an embedded ESMessage_Ctor child sized to the widget's full client rect for the button's caption. Sets the +0x39 flags word's 0x200 bit (likely 'clickable'/'enabled').
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESButtonBitmap_HandleEvent
entries.description: ButtonIcon's event handler (vtable 0046e924 slot 0), the tab strip's class. A left press (sub-code 2) on an enabled widget with neither DAT_00470d70 nor DAT_00470e70 set lights +0x45, plays the press sound (0042eecf) when sound is on, repaints, and -- while the auto-repeat flag +0x61 is clear, as the constructor leaves it -- runs Window_DispatchCallback at once. A left release (1) zeroes +0x45 without repainting. Right-button events fall through to WinButton_HandleEvent, so the right button fires on its release. The leave event clears +0x45 only while +0x5d is 0, and ESButtonBitmap_Ctor sets it to 1. Event 0x200 is the auto-repeat alarm tick, which re-runs the callback while +0x61 is set and the button is lit.

entries.name: ESButtonBitmap_Paint
entries.description: ESButtonBitmap vtable 0046e924 slot +4, the paint (widget): Window_BeginPaint, then draws the face bitmap +0x51 when the lit flag +0x45 is clear and +0x55 when it is set, through the bitmap's vtable +0x1c; then, when the caption Text at +0x4d has a font (+0xb1), ESMessage_Paint on it at the baseline (Font_CellHeight + (+0x31 - +0x29) + 1) / 2, less 1 when idle or disabled (+0x49 clear) and plus 1 when lit and enabled. The face pointer +0x59 is never read. See docs/shell/screen-layout.md, The tab strip.

entries.name: ESRadioButton_Ctor
entries.description: ESRadioButton constructor (vtable 0046e9a0, RTTI name 'ESRadioButton', 0x6d bytes): ESButtonBitmap_Ctor with the same arguments, then its own vtable and +0x69 cleared. PreferencesScreen_Build makes its option buttons with it.

entries.name: ESRadioButton_HandleEvent
entries.description: ESRadioButton vtable 0046e9a0 slot 0, the checkbox's event handler (widget, event). Event 0x10 (leave): clears the lit flag +0x45 and repaints (vtable +4) only while +0x5d is 0. Event 0x20 (mouse) while enabled (+0x49): sub-code 1 (left up) is dropped; sub-code 2 (left down) plays ShellSound_PlayPress when Shell_SoundEnabled, sets +0x45, repaints and fires through Window_DispatchCallback. Anything else goes to WinButton_HandleEvent. Every event it consumes is deleted through its vtable +0x18. See docs/shell/screen-layout.md, The widget that takes a click decides what it does.

entries.name: ESRadioButton_Paint
entries.description: ESRadioButton vtable 0046e9a0 slot +4, the checkbox's paint: ESButtonBitmap_Paint with the face chosen by the tick +0x69 (clear +0x51, set +0x55) instead of the lit flag; the caption placement still follows +0x45 and +0x49.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 0040a26d, compared with 0040a05d; vtable 0046e9a0 (RTTI ESRadioButton)

entries.name: ESQuad_AddColumns
entries.description: Gives a row Panel four Text children at +0x55, +0x59, +0x5d and +0x61, each spanning from the previous column's right edge to its own, the last ending two pixels inside the row. All four are opaque (+0xc1 = 1) so a refresh overwrites cleanly. FUN_0040a4d6 sets one by index and FUN_0040a58b recolours one.

entries.name: ESQuad_SetColumnColor
entries.description: Writes one of a row's four text columns' colour, +0xb5, by column index; does not repaint.

entries.name: ESQuad_Paint
entries.description: Slot 1 of the list-row vtable at 00479bb0, which the repair, squad, arming, build and armory builders each write over ESRect_Ctor's on their rows: clears the interior {1, 1, w-1, h-1} to 0x10, runs ESRect_FillAndBorder (nothing while +0x51 is clear), and paints the four text columns.

entries.name: ESRect_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of RTTI class ESRect (vtable 0046ead0, 0x55 bytes; ESQuad rows reuse it at 0x65 and overwrite the vtable), the simplest visible-chrome widget: calls WinButton_Ctor, sets its vtable, stores a style/colour param at +0x4d, sets +0x51 = 1. Its paint (ESRect_Paint, 0040a959) is ESRect_FillAndBorder(widget, 1) alone: a plain flat-colour rectangle, used raw wherever screens need an unadorned coloured rect.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESRect_FillAndBorder
entries.description: The fill and border under every panel paint, and the whole of ESRect_Paint. Optionally clears the interior to a literal 0x10, then draws a chamfered border in +0x4d: four edges each stopping a pixel short at both ends, with the four pixels one step inside the corners painted instead. Returns immediately when +0x51 is clear.

entries.name: ESRect_Paint
entries.description: ESRect_Ctor's paint override: single flat-fill call, no border/text/children drawing. Confirms ESRect_Ctor is the plain flat-colour rectangle widget class.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESRegionFill_Ctor
entries.description: Smaller bordered sub-panel widget class (0x5d=93-byte struct, 8 uses -- same size class as ESButtonFont_Ctor but a distinct vtable/paint). Calls ESRect_Ctor's base then sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046eae4). Its paint override (ESRegionFill_Paint) is near-identical to ESTitle_Paint's checkerboard-fill+border logic but without the header-divider-line step -- essentially ESTitle_Ctor without the titled header, i.e. a plain framed/bordered box.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESRegionFill_Paint
entries.description: ESRegionFill_Ctor's paint override: checkerboard-dithered fill + border, no header-divider lines (compare ESTitle_Paint). Confirms ESRegionFill_Ctor is a plain bordered box.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESTitle_Ctor
entries.description: Root/tab-panel widget class with title-bar chrome (0x75=117-byte struct, 10 uses). Always the FIRST widget constructed in every one of the six *_BuildScreen functions, sized to near-fullscreen, given a title string (weapon-catalog or hardcoded caption) -- this is each tab screen's own root window. Constructs an embedded ESMessage_Ctor title child, calls Window_ShowRecursive at the end. Its paint override (ESTitle_Paint) draws a header strip with vertical column-divider lines, a checkerboard-dithered body background, and a border -- classic titled-groupbox chrome.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESTitle_Paint
entries.description: ESTitle_Ctor's paint override: fills a header strip (height from +0x59) with vertical divider lines if the header-divider flag is set, else (no title-bar variant) fills the whole body with a checkerboard/dithered pixel pattern; either way finishes with a 4-corner-tick + rectangle border draw. Confirms ESTitle_Ctor is a bordered, optionally-titled groupbox/root-window chrome.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESAlert_Ctor
entries.description: esalert.cpp. ESTitle_Ctor, then its own vtable (0046ebe0), 0x60 ORed into the event mask, and a buffer the size of the rect. Its paint is ESTitle_Paint (via ESAlert_Paint).

entries.name: ESAlert_HandleEvent
entries.description: ESAlert vtable 0046ebe0 slot 0 (alert, event). Event 1 (show): Window_BeginPaint, then Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch reads the screen under the alert into the buffer bitmap at +0x75 (its +4), at {0, 0}. Event 2 (hide): Window_BeginPaint, then Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch puts that bitmap back. Event 4: repaints through vtable +4. Every event is then deleted through its vtable +0x18. ESAlert_Ctor adds 0x60 to the mask, so a click on the alert's body reaches this handler and is dropped; its buttons are child widgets.

entries.name: ESAlert_Paint
entries.description: ESAlert vtable 0046ebe0 slot +4: Window_BeginPaint, then ESTitle_Paint.

entries.name: Alert_Show
entries.description: Window_ShowRecursive on the widget's parent, then on the widget.

entries.name: Alert_Hide
entries.description: Window_HideRecursive on the widget, then on its parent.

entries.name: ESMessage_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of RTTI class ESMessage (vtable 0046ec54, 0xc9 bytes), the text label, the most-constructed widget in VSHELL's screens. Calls ESWindow_Ctor, not WinButton_Ctor, sets its vtable (slot 0 ESMessage_HandleEvent), stores the font handle (+0xb1), alignment (+0x45), ink replacement colour (+0xb5), opaque flag (+0xc1), then ESMessage_SetString; then clears 0x18 from the event mask +0x39, leaving 0x07 -- no mouse bit, so a label never takes a click and one on it is delivered to its parent. 5th argument is the handler at +0x3d. Also the embedded caption child of ESButtonFont_Ctor/ESButtonBitmap_Ctor and ESTitle_Ctor.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESMessage_SetString
entries.description: ESMessage_Ctor's string-setter: stores font/style params, copies the caller's string into the widget's fixed 100-char buffer (asserts 'Message text is too long' if over 100 chars, per the src\esmsg.cpp assert string -- Text shares its overlong-string guard with the message-queue system), or clears/hides the widget if the string is null/empty.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESMessage_HandleEvent
entries.description: The Text class's event handler (vtable 0046ec54 slot 0): event 2 goes to Window_DispatchCallback, event 4 paints (ESMessage_Paint), everything else is discarded. It has no mouse arm, and Text's event mask keeps mouse events from reaching it in the first place.

entries.name: ESMessage_Paint
entries.description: The Text widget's paint, reached by event type 4. Optionally clears its rect to +0xc5 when +0xc1 is set, draws the string at a baseline of H - (H + 1 - cellHeight) / 2 - 2 with the alignment in +0x45, then remaps the font's ink index 0x29 to +0xb5 over the rect.

entries.name: ESBitmap_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of the image panel class (0x61 bytes, vtable 0046ec94): ESRect_Ctor base, the bitmap at +0x5d, the blit offset +0x55/+0x59 cleared, +0x51 cleared so its paint draws no border (the bitmap is blitted regardless), and hidden. Its paint is ESBitmap_Paint (0040b772). The crew screen's portraits and the shell frame's backdrop root are this class.

entries.name: ESBitmap_HandleEvent
entries.description: The image panel's event handler (vtable 0046ec94 slot 0). Repaints on event 4 and runs Window_DispatchCallback on any left release (0x20 sub-code 1) delivered to it -- no press on it needed, no +0x49 test, no DAT_00470d70/DAT_00470e70 test, and the right button ignored.

entries.name: ESBitmap_Paint
entries.description: Image panel paint: blits +0x5d at (+0x55, +0x59) through FUN_00453158, then ESRect_FillAndBorder(widget, 0) -- border over the bitmap, no fill. Vtable 0046ec94 slot +4, read from the raw image.

entries.name: maybe_Grid_InitSingleRow
entries.description: Same zero-init pattern as ESGrid_InitRow but operating on a single standalone row-shaped struct rather than one slot of a ESGrid_Ctor's 30-row array -- used by the part-filling routines, Repair_BuildDiagrams and Build_FillBlueprints (0041579d) among them, to stage a part for ESGrid_SetPart. Plausibly a single detached row/line-item struct reusing the same 10-column layout convention, not confirmed against a distinct constructor.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESGrid_Ctor
entries.description: Multi-column grid/list-view widget class (0x6e8=1768-byte struct, 4 uses -- the biggest widget struct in VSHELL by far). Calls ESRect_Ctor's base, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ecd8), then initializes 30 fixed row slots (56/0x38 bytes each) via ESGrid_InitRow, each row holding a 10-column width/flag array (default {14,16} per column). Used by Squad_BuildRosterList and the wcrewi.cpp/wmissini.cpp list screens -- almost certainly the crew/pilot roster and mission objective/weapon lists (30 rows matches a plausible max-crew-slots count).
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESGrid_InitRow
entries.description: Zeroes one ESGrid_Ctor row slot (icon ptr, x, y fields) and its 10-column width/flag array to the default {14,16} pair per column. Called 30 times by ESGrid_Ctor at construction.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESGrid_SetPart
entries.description: Contains the 'ESGrid::setPart out of range' assert (src/esgrid.cpp). Writes a resolved GLBitmap* plus placement fields into one of up to 29 named part slots (0x38-byte stride) on an ESGrid Herc-display widget -- the 2D icon/portrait-painting layer built on top of the base bitmap-tag mechanism, matching the same 29-part hit-zone indexing used by the mech damage formula. Not needed for base .DTS/.DBA texture rendering, only for VSHELL's per-poly paint-job overlay UI. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: ESGrid_Paint
entries.description: ESGrid_Ctor's paint override: draws 16px gridlines (both axes) if the grid-lines flag (+0x6e5) is set, then for each of the 30 rows with a non-null icon pointer, blits the row's icon (FUN_00453158) and, for each of its 10 columns whose width differs from the default (0x10), performs a byte-remap-based colour-tint fill (FUN_00457364) over that cell. Conclusively confirms ESGrid_Ctor is a per-row-icon, per-column-tinted table/list-view widget.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESGrid_InitAllRows
entries.description: (grid): ESGrid_InitRow for rows 0 to 0x1d. Squad_SetEmptyBayPicture calls it.

entries.name: ESDialog_Ctor
entries.description: The editable text field class (0xc3 struct, esdialog.cpp). String buffer at +0x45, permitted-character set at +0x9f defaulting to the upper-case alphabet, font at +0xa3, length at +0xab, pixel width at +0xaf, caret enable at +0xb3 and text colour at +0xbb. The save screen's ten slot rows are these.

entries.name: ESDialog_IsPermitted
entries.description: Whether a character is in the edit field's permitted-character set at +0x9f; any character when the set is null.

entries.name: ESDialog_SetString
entries.description: Copies a string into an edit field's +0x45 buffer, asserting at 90 characters, then caches its length at +0xab and its summed pixel width at +0xaf.

entries.name: ESDialog_TypeChar
entries.description: Appends a character to the edit field's +0x45 string when ESDialog_IsPermitted, the new length stays below 0x5a, and glyph width + cached width +0xaf + 6 is less than the field's width; updates +0xab and +0xaf and repaints.

entries.name: ESDialog_Erase
entries.description: Takes the last character off the edit field's string while its length +0xab is above the floor at +0xb7; the save screen's rows set the floor to 4, keeping the "%2d. " prefix.

entries.name: ESDialog_HandleEvent
entries.description: The edit field's event handler (vtable 0046edc8 slot 0). Acts on the left press only (sub-code 2), with no +0x49 or DAT_00470d70/DAT_00470e70 test. With the focus flag +0xa7 clear it installs a 500/500 WinTimer alarm, sets the pointer lock (DAT_005ddbd0 +0x1f), sets +0xa7, repaints and runs Window_DispatchCallback. With +0xa7 set it clears it, removes the alarm, releases the lock (Pointer_Unlock), sends a leave, re-hit-tests with Pointer_Enter(0) and re-posts the press (Event_Post) with its target cleared, so the press lands on whatever is under the pointer. Event 0x40 (a key) and 0x100 (a command: 1 backspace, 4 left, 0x0a enter) edit the string; 0x10 removes the alarm.

entries.name: ESDialog_Paint
entries.description: Clears the field to 0x10, draws its string left-aligned one pixel in at a baseline of cellHeight / 2 + (H + 1) / 2, draws a 7x3 caret block at 0x27 past the text when +0xa7 and +0xb3 are both set, then remaps the font's ink index 0x29 to +0xbb.

entries.name: ESArm_Ctor
entries.description: Repeating-horizontal-line fill widget class (0x61=97-byte struct, 3 uses -- same size class as maybe_Widget_InitRect but a distinct vtable/paint). Calls ESRect_Ctor's base, sets its own vtable (&PTR_FUN_0046ee08), sets width/style fields. Its paint override (ESArm_Paint) draws a repeating stack of horizontal lines from a start offset (+0x55) to the bottom edge, plus an optional small corner-bracket shape if a flag (+0x5d) is set -- looks like a hatched section-divider or scrollbar-track background, not a single separator line.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESArm_HandleEvent
entries.description: HatchedDivider's event handler (vtable 0046ee08 slot 0): WinButton_HandleEvent's mouse arm -- press lights +0x45, release with it lit dispatches the +0x3d handler, gated on +0x49 -- without its DAT_00470d70/DAT_00470e70 test, and the leave event repaints recursively.

entries.name: ESArm_Paint
entries.description: ESArm_Ctor's paint override: repeating horizontal-line fill plus an optional corner-bracket shape. Confirms ESArm_Ctor is a hatched/lined fill widget, not a simple 1px separator.
entries.source: project_es2_exe_recon memory, VSHELL widget-class disambiguation pass

entries.name: ESAnim_Ctor
entries.description: ESAnim constructor (esanim.cpp; vtable 0046ee4c at +1, RTTI 'ESAnim', 0x51 bytes): (this, a, b, frames, count, c) ESWindow_Ctor(this, a, b, c), the vtable, the frame set at +0x45 (its +8 is the bitmap array), the current frame +0x49 = 0, the frame count at +0x4d, 0x200 (timer) ORed into the event mask +0x39, then Window_ShowRecursive. ESAnim2_Ctor (esanim2.cpp) is the class the shell builds; tools/scripts/es2_xref.py finds no rel32 branch to 0040c6d0 and no stored pointer of it. Ghidra had no function here: the bytes sat undisassembled after ESArm_Paint.

entries.name: ESAnim_HandleEvent
entries.description: ESAnim vtable 0046ee4c slot 0 (widget, event). Event 1 (show): WinTimer_InstallAlarm(DAT_005ddbd4, widget, 500, 500, 0). Event 2 (hide): WinTimer_RemoveAlarms. Event 4: ESAnim_Paint. Event 0x200 (timer) while not hidden (+0x11 bit 2 clear): advances the frame +0x49, wrapping to 0 at the count +0x4d, and paints. Deletes the event through its vtable +0x18. Unlike ESAnim2_HandleEvent it fires no callback.

entries.name: ESAnim_Paint
entries.description: (widget): Window_BeginPaint, then, when the frame set +0x45 is set, draws bitmap [+0x49] of its array (+8) through the bitmap's vtable +0x1c. ESAnim_HandleEvent calls it; ESAnim's vtable has no paint slot.

entries.name: ESAnim2_Ctor
entries.description: esanim2.cpp. Window subclass (vtable 0046eec4) holding up to ten frame bitmaps at +0x45, the frame count at +0x71 and the current frame at +0x6d; adds 0x200 (timer) to the event mask.

entries.name: ESAnim2_HandleEvent
entries.description: esanim2.cpp. Event 1 (show): 500/500 ms alarm, DAT_0046c098 = 0. Event 2 (hide): alarm removed, frames freed, DAT_0046c098 = 1. Event 4: paints the current frame. Event 0x200 while not hidden: +0x6d advanced modulo the frame count, painted, then Window_DispatchCallback.

entries.name: ESAnim2_AddFrame
entries.description: esanim2.cpp. Appends one bitmap to the widget's frame array and counts it.

entries.name: ESAnim2_Paint
entries.description: esanim2.cpp. Window_BeginPaint, then draws frame +0x6d through the bitmap's vtable slot 0x1c.

entries.name: ESPal_Ctor
entries.description: Window subclass whose +0x45 is a palette index rather than a lit flag; installs vtable PTR_FUN_0046ef04 and zeroes the index. Allocation size 0x47.

entries.name: ESPal_SetIndex
entries.description: Writes +0x45 then installs and commits that palette.

entries.name: ESPal_HandleEvent
entries.description: Event 2 (shown) installs and commits the palette named by +0x45; event 4 goes to 0040cb40. This is why hiding the widget, writing +0x45 and showing it again changes palette.

entries.name: ESPal_Paint
entries.description: The palette scope's event-4 paint: fills its whole rect, {0, 0x1e, 0x27f, 0x1df}, with 0x10. Shell_SetPaletteScope's show posts it, so every tab from WEAPONS to MISSION blacks out the canvas below the strip; nothing repaints the backdrop root afterwards.

entries.name: Str_CountChar
entries.description: (str, ch): the number of times ch occurs in the NUL-terminated str (the decompile drops the return). TextBox_Layout calls it.

entries.name: TextBox_Ctor
entries.description: esreport.cpp's paginated text box (0x36 bytes, not a widget): stores the parent, the rect and the font and zeroes the rest.

entries.name: TextBox_SetText
entries.description: Clears the box, copies the string, lays it out (TextBox_Layout, TextBox_Wrap), computes the page count as lines / perPage + (lines + 1 != perPage), and builds one hidden opaque Text child per line, left-aligned in 0x28.

entries.name: TextBox_Clear
entries.description: Frees the text box's string, rows, line pointers and line texts and zeroes its counters, the shown flag and the page.

entries.name: TextBox_ShowPage
entries.description: Shows the line texts of the current page (+0x1e) while the box is shown (+0x18) and hides every other.

entries.name: TextBox_Layout
entries.description: Estimates the line count, sets lines per page to the rect height over the cell height, and cuts one row rect per line of a page.

entries.name: TextBox_Wrap
entries.description: Splits the text box's string in place into lines: at newlines, and at the last break when the line measured at a space is wider than the box.

entries.name: TextBox_PageUp
entries.description: Back one page while the box is shown and not on page 0.

entries.name: TextBox_PageDown
entries.description: On one page while the box is shown and not on the last.

entries.name: Path_PrefixBaseDir
entries.description: Returns 004823f8, a static buffer holding the directory string at 00482285 followed by the given path with any drive letter ('X:') removed. Game_ExportMissionHandoff, ShellOptions_Load and ShellOptions_SaveAll build their file paths with it.

entries.name: Path_UnderDriveCfg
entries.description: Returns 004822d5 -- the first string in data\drive.cfg plus a backslash, which FUN_0040d327 reads -- followed by the argument with any leading drive letter and colon dropped, in a static buffer at 00482448. Movie_PlayQueue builds each movie's path with it.

entries.name: FileUtil_CopyFile
entries.description: (source, destination), assert file src\fileutil.cpp: opens a FileRStream and a FileWStream (asserting both opened), reads the whole source into a Mem_NewArray buffer of FileRStream_GetSize bytes (asserting the allocation) and writes it out, then closes and destroys both. Career_SaveSlot and Career_LoadSlot copy the slot files with it.

entries.name: ShellOptions_Load_Thunk
entries.description: ShellOptions_Load(). ShellOptions_Init calls it.

entries.name: ShellOptions_Init
entries.description: Clears the 0x36 entries of ShellOptionHandlers, then loads prefs.cfg through ShellOptions_Load_Thunk. Shell_WinMain calls it before reading option 6. DBSIM's Prefs_Init (0045a19c) registers five handlers and applies options here instead.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0040d68c; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0045a19c

entries.name: ShellOptions_Load
entries.description: Zeroes ShellOptions, reads data\prefs.cfg straight over it, then fires every registered handler and re-baselines the shadow.

entries.name: ShellOptions_SaveAll
entries.description: Writes all 54 bytes of ShellOptions back to data\prefs.cfg. Called from nine sites, the practice screen's Begin Mission and InstantAction_SelectDemo among them.

entries.name: ShellOptions_Commit
entries.description: Walks all 54 options, calls the handler of each that differs from the shadow, and re-baselines it.

entries.name: ShellOptions_SetOption
entries.description: Stores one option byte and, when told to apply, calls its handler.

entries.name: ShellOptions_ToggleOption
entries.description: (index, flag): ShellOptions_SetOption(index, ShellOptions[index] ^ 1, flag) and returns the new value.

entries.name: ShellOptions_StepOption
entries.description: value + 1, wrapping to 0 at the caller's modulus.

entries.name: ShellOptions_StepOptionBack
entries.description: value - 1, wrapping to modulus - 1 below zero.

entries.name: ShellOptions_SaveOne
entries.description: (index): ShellOptions_SaveSome(1, &index). Shell_SetCampaignMode saves option 0x2a with it.

entries.name: ShellOptions_SaveSome
entries.description: (count, indices): copies ShellOptions, reads data\prefs.cfg over the copy when it opens, puts the current value of each of the count listed option indices into it, and writes the 0x36 bytes back to data\prefs.cfg. So only the listed options change on disk.

entries.name: Prefs_RegisterOptionHandler
entries.description: (option, handler): ShellOptionHandlers[option] = handler. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Prefs_RegisterOptionHandler (00459c58).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0040db25; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00459c58

entries.name: Devices_Init
entries.description: devices.cpp's setup, called once from Shell_Main: allocates a 1-byte object (constructor 00409958 stores GetTickCount at 0046e818) into 0046f190, Input_SetEventTime(0), then a GLViewport into 0046f194 sized to the screen (00481884 x 00481888, centre at minus half of each), stores the viewport's +4 at +0x44 of the object at 00481868 and, when that object is GL_GetGlobal7's, installs it with Gfx_SetClipBlock, and makes the viewport the current context (Gfx_SetCurrentContext).

entries.name: Devices_Shutdown
entries.description: Destroys the GLViewport at 0046f194 through its virtual destructor and frees the object at 0046f190, clearing each; nothing when they are null. Called only by Shell_ShutdownDevicesAndSound.

entries.name: Input_SetEventTime
