entries.description: (t): stores Input_EventTime (0046e818). Devices_Init calls it with 0.

entries.name: GameFileStr_Read
entries.description: Reads sav\GAMEFILE.STR, the 12-slot directory: a leading length, then two count-prefixed blocks of length-prefixed strings (filenames, then labels with an in-use byte). A label whose 5th byte is NUL is completed with estext.bin string 0x21.

entries.name: GameFileStr_Write
entries.description: Writes sav\GAMEFILE.STR, both blocks with a literal count of 12, then seeks back to patch the leading length with lseek(END)-4 -- which measures the physical file, stale tail included.

entries.name: Game_SetSlotInUse
entries.description: Game_SaveSlot's first step: copies the label over slot param_1's GAMEFILE.STR label when the slot is below 10, sets the slot's in-use byte (00482610 table, +0x5d) for any slot, and rewrites GAMEFILE.STR through GameFileStr_Write.

entries.name: SaveSlot_BuildPath
entries.description: (slot): writes 'sav\' followed by the slot's file name (SaveSlotTable, 0x5e bytes per slot) into the static buffer 004832dc. Used by Game_LoadSlot, Game_SaveSlot and Stats_ScanSlots.

entries.name: Shell_InitGameState
entries.description: Startup: clears the game-in-progress flag, reads GAMEFILE.STR, loads herc_inf.dat and damage.dat, scans the slots' summaries, and seeds CampaignModeFlag from prefs option 42.

entries.name: ShellMap_Build
entries.description: Destroys the map in DAT_0046f26c, constructs a new one (0x3c5 bytes) over the canvas rect {0x123,0x43,0x249,0x124} and builds its relief (ShellMap_BuildRelief). Called from Game_LoadSlot, Career_LoadCurrentMission and Msn_BuildPath.

entries.name: Game_NewCareer
entries.description: game.cpp. Starts a career: loads weapons.dat, generates the pilot roster, loads hercs.dat, sets the career position and seeds the salvage pool to rand(0..10)*1000 + 100000.

entries.name: Game_SaveSlot
entries.description: game.cpp. Writes sav\GAME_?.SAV for the given slot: armory stock, career block, 3x12 pilot roster, the player, the hangar, 9 shorts, the salvage pool, the 2000-byte campaign flag array, game state and a 20-byte tail. Slot 10 becomes 11 when DAT_0048260c is 0 (training). Validated by parsing all nine retail saves.

entries.name: Game_LoadSlot
entries.description: game.cpp. Field-for-field mirror of Game_SaveSlot. Refuses a slot whose in-use byte (00482610 table, +0x5d) is clear.

entries.name: Shell_SetCampaignMode
entries.description: (mode): CampaignModeFlag = mode, prefs option 0x2a = mode without its handler, then that option alone saved (ShellOptions_SaveOne(0x2a)).

entries.name: Player_SetBay
entries.description: (bay): stores bay in 00482a9e, the player pilot record's +0x22.

entries.name: Squad_SetMemberBay
entries.description: (member, bay): writes squad member's +0x22. Bay -1 clears its on-strength byte through Squad_SetOnStrength; any other bay calls Squad_UpdateOnStrength with the member index in the position argument.

entries.name: Hangar_ScrapSelected
entries.description: The scrap dialog's ACCEPT action: CareerSalvage += HercList_ScrapSelected(00482ac3); the pilot Squad_PilotForBay finds for the selected bay gets bay -1, and the squad member at that pilot's +0x27 position is set off strength.

entries.name: Armory_ScrapWeapons
entries.description: The weapon scrap dialog's ACCEPT action: CareerSalvage += Armory_ScrapStock(id).

entries.name: Hangar_WithdrawChassis
entries.description: (chassisType) HercList_RemoveFirstOfType, then the pilot Squad_PilotForBay finds for the returned index gets bay -1; the on-strength byte is left alone. Career_Advance's stage 1 mission 6 event, with 8, the Razor.

entries.name: Game_AutoRepairSquad
entries.description: (budget) The debrief's repair billing by ShellOption_RepairMode: Repair_Auto on the player's machine in mode 0 only, and on each on-strength squad member's at positions 1 up to 00482a78 in any mode but 2, each against the same unsigned budget (the caller passes CareerSalvage / 00482a7a), each cost taken off CareerSalvage.

entries.name: Hangar_BuySelected
entries.description: BUILD's order: HercList_OrderIntoSelected(00482ac3, chassis) and CareerSalvage minus the price Herc_Order returns (EAX passes through 00410982).

entries.name: CampaignFlags_Clear
entries.description: memset of the 2000-byte campaign flag array.

entries.name: MsnGen_SeedCampaignFlags
entries.description: Before a mission load: training clears the flag array, campaign writes flags 1-2 as the career position; both write flag 3 from 00482606 and flags 4-6 a draw below 12 each.

entries.name: MissionVar_Write
entries.description: game.cpp. Writes the 2000-byte campaign flag array to data\mission.var before a mission launches.

entries.name: MissionVar_Read
entries.description: game.cpp. Reads data\mission.var back into the campaign flag array at debrief -- the reader for the block DBSIM's FUN_0042412c dumps at mission end.

entries.name: Game_ProcessMissionResults
entries.description: game.cpp. The post-mission debrief: reads data\mission.var back, then data\results.dat (outcome, a salvage award, salvage pairs, per-HERC damage and per-pilot counters), bills repairs, advances the campaign via Career_Advance and sets the next screen in 0048260e.

entries.name: Game_ExportMissionHandoff
entries.description: game.cpp. Pre-launch export: writes data\mission.var, removes the stale export file, then writes the player's HERC record plus every on-strength squad member's name index, skill tier and HERC. The output path is referenced as a bare address (0046f521) so its text is not in the decompile; data\player.mec is the reading.

entries.name: Game_DeliverWeaponQueue
entries.description: In a campaign, CareerSalvage -= Armory_DeliverQueue(). The debrief's first campaign-only step.

entries.name: Debrief_WriteReport
entries.description: (results header by value, salvageItems) Formats the mission tab's debrief report texts: the outcome's estext.bin string (0x146 + outcome), the salvage award in tons, the salvage item count, the player's Herc, Base and Flyer kills for the mission (+0x2d, +0x31, +0x2f) and the same three summed over the player and each on-strength squad member at positions 1 up to 00482a78, and the pilots-lost count Squad_ProgressAll returned. Writes widget text only.

entries.name: Squad_AllArmed
entries.description: Every squad member on strength in positions 1..SquadPositionsInPlay-1 has an armed machine. Rock & Roll code 3.

entries.name: Campaign_LoadStageText
entries.description: game.cpp. Reads eng\campaign.str in the .STR layout and returns a new copy of string N (its argument, stage - 1) of the first group, freeing the previous one (DAT_0046f3e8); null when there is no such string. Mission_Show's map view fills text box 0 with it.

entries.name: Util_Shuffle
entries.description: Fills an int16 array of the given length with a random permutation of 0..n-1 (fill with -1, then place each value into the k-th still-empty slot).

entries.name: Pilot_DrawSkill
entries.description: A draw below 100 against the thresholds 70/85/95/100 at 0046f5ec: skill 0-3.

entries.name: Pilot_RankForSkill
entries.description: (skill): returns int16 {0, 1, 2, 2}[skill] from 0046f5f4. Squad_GenerateRoster passes it to Pilot_Init as the rank (+0x29) of a pilot whose skill Pilot_DrawSkill drew.

entries.name: Squad_GenerateRoster
entries.description: Generates 3 squads x 12 pilots at new-career time. Per squad it draws a 4- and a 3-element shuffle, giving each pilot a roster id (0-11) and an esnames.bin name index (0-35); the name string is copied out of esnames.bin.

entries.name: Squad_TakeMember
entries.description: (squad) -> the squad's record at its cursor, which then steps mod 12, reset to the pilot defaults. Player_Create takes each squad's record 0.

entries.name: Squads_Write
entries.description: Save block 4: (stream) Pilot_Write on each of the 3 squads x 12 pilot records at 004832fc (squad stride 0x2c4, record stride 0x3b), then the 3 int16 current members at 00483b48 and the 3 int16 next members at 00483b4e through the write slot (vtable +0x14). Game_SaveSlot calls it.

entries.name: Squads_Read
entries.description: Save block 4 reader, the mirror of Squads_Write: Pilot_Read into the same 3 x 12 records, then the 6 bytes at 00483b48 and at 00483b4e through the read slot (vtable +0x18). Game_LoadSlot calls it.

entries.name: Pilot_Init
entries.description: Writes a pilot record: roster id, name index, name, skill at +0x25 and rank at +0x29, then the per-record defaults.

entries.name: Pilot_SetDefaults
entries.description: A pilot record's defaults: bay -1, off strength, position (+0x27) -1, +0x2b 100, then +0x2d, +0x2f, +0x31 and the fields after them 0. Called by Pilot_Init.

entries.name: Pilot_Write
entries.description: Serializes one 59-byte pilot record; FUN_0040fefc is the reader. Name is length-prefixed, so the on-disk size varies.

entries.name: Pilot_Read
entries.description: (pilot, stream): reads one pilot record, the mirror of Pilot_Write: int16 at +0 and +2, an int16 name length and that many name bytes into +4, int16 +0x22, byte +0x24, then eleven int16 from +0x25 to +0x39. Player_Read and Stats_ScanSlots read pilots with it. See docs/formats/save-games.md.

entries.name: Pilot_AccumulateMissionStats
entries.description: Reads a pilot's three per-mission counters from results.dat in the order +0x2d, +0x31, +0x2f, adds them into the career totals at +0x33/+0x35/+0x37 and increments the missions-flown count at +0x39.

entries.name: Pilot_Progress
entries.description: Advances one pilot's skill (+0x25) and rank (+0x29), both capped at 3. Skill steps when career Herc + Flyer kills hit a multiple of the divisor and only for non-player pilots; rank steps on missions flown. +0x27 selects the divisor pair: 0 gives 20 kills / 10 missions, non-zero gives 10 / 15. Confirmed in raw disassembly: the jnz at 0041009f skips the whole skill block for the player, and the skill test examines only the idiv remainder (test edx,edx at 004100b3) with no guard on the kill sum -- so a zero total satisfies it.

entries.name: Player_Clear
entries.description: Zeroes the player structure's two leading shorts and its three squad-member pointers.

entries.name: Player_Create
entries.description: Builds the player structure at 00482a78 for a new career (Game_NewCareer): Pilot_Init of the embedded record with the given name and skill, then bay 0, position (+0x27) 0 and on strength, and the three squad-member pointers at +0x3f.

entries.name: Player_Write
entries.description: Save block 5: (player, stream) writes the int16s at player+0 and +2 and then the pilot record at +4 with Pilot_Write. Game_SaveSlot passes SquadPositionsInPlay (00482a78). The mirror of Player_Read.

entries.name: Player_Read
entries.description: Reads save block 5 -- two int16 and the player's pilot record -- then points the three squad pointers at +0x3f at record DAT_00483b48[k] of squad k.

entries.name: Squad_PilotForBay
entries.description: The pilot record assigned to a hangar bay, or null: the player's own (embedded at +0x04, bay at +0x26) and then the three squad members the player structure points at from +0x3f. -1 finds nothing.

entries.name: Squad_PilotNameForBay
entries.description: Squad_PilotForBay's name field (+0x04), or estext.bin entry 0, the empty string.

entries.name: Squad_SetMemberPosition
entries.description: (player, member, position): writes the squad member's position, pilot record +0x27, through the player structure's pointer at +0x3f.

entries.name: Squad_MemberAtPosition
entries.description: (player, position) -> index 0-2 of the first of the three squad pointers at player+0x3f whose pilot record +0x27 equals position, or -1.

entries.name: Squad_SetPositionsInPlay
entries.description: (player, n): the positions in play, then Squad_UpdateOnStrength for positions 1-3.

entries.name: Squad_SetOnStrength
entries.description: (player, member, flag): writes the squad member's on-strength byte (+0x24), incrementing or decrementing the player structure's +2 (00482a7a, machines on strength) when the byte changes.

entries.name: Squad_UpdateOnStrength
entries.description: (player, position): sets the on-strength byte of the squad member at that position when the position is below the player structure's leading short (00482a78) and the member has a bay, clears it otherwise (via Squad_SetOnStrength, 00410327). Matches every retail save's on-strength bytes.

entries.name: Squad_ProgressAll
entries.description: Post-mission progression pass over the player and every on-strength squad member: Pilot_Progress for survivors, replacement from the roster for a pilot at zero condition.

entries.name: HercsDat_Clear
entries.description: Empties the hercs.dat record table: clears +0x20 and +0x22, then for each of the eight record pointers at +0 frees the record (HercRecord_ClearMounts, Mem_Delete) and zeroes the slot, and clears +0x24. LoadHercsDat calls it before loading.

entries.name: LoadHercsDat
entries.description: Loads gam\hercs.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: Hangar_Write
entries.description: Save block 6: the hangar's occupied count (+0x20 of the eight-pointer array at 00482ac3), then each occupied bay in order as its index and Herc_Write.

entries.name: PlayerMec_WriteEntry
entries.description: One player.mec entry past its pilot fields: type, capacity, weapon ids (0 empty), ammunition types (5 empty), a 0, the 66-byte status block.

entries.name: Hangar_Read
entries.description: Save block 6 reader, the mirror of Hangar_Write (herclist.cpp asserts at lines 0x77 and 0x79): HercsDat_Clear, the int16 count into +0x20, then per entry an int16 bay, asserting the bay is empty, a new 0x7a-byte HercRecord_Ctor record stored there and filled by Herc_Read.

entries.name: HercList_ScrapSelected
entries.description: herclist.cpp. For the hangar's +0x22 slot, when occupied: Herc_Scrap, ClearMounts, free, slot to null, count at +0x20 minus one. Returns the value, 0 for an empty slot.

entries.name: HercList_OrderIntoSelected
entries.description: herclist.cpp. Allocates a 0x7a-byte HERC record (HercRecord_Ctor), stores it in the slot the hangar's +0x22 (selected bay) names without testing it, increments the count at +0x20, and runs Herc_Order on it.

entries.name: HercList_BuildTickAll
entries.description: (hangar) Herc_BuildTick on every occupied bay whose machine HercList_IsBuilt says is not built. The debrief's construction step.

entries.name: HercList_IsBuilt
entries.description: (hangar, bay) Whether the bay holds a machine whose +0x4a build percentage is 100; false for an empty bay.

entries.name: Herc_IsDeployable
entries.description: Bay pointer non-null, built to 100 (HercList_IsBuilt (00410a64)) and Herc_IsFlightworthy. Rock & Roll code 0.

entries.name: Herc_HasSingleDeployable
entries.description: True when exactly one of the eight bays holds a machine that is occupied, fully built and flightworthy (Herc_IsDeployable, 00410a9d). The repair and build screens' SCRAP buttons are dead while it holds, whichever bay that machine is in.

entries.name: Herc_IsArmed
entries.description: Bay pointer non-null and Herc_HasWeapon. Rock & Roll code 1.

entries.name: HercList_ChassisAt
entries.description: (hangar, bay) The chassis type (+0x00) of the machine in the bay, or -1 for a negative bay or an empty one.

entries.name: HercList_Deliver
entries.description: (hangar, bay, herc): asserts the bay empty, stores the machine and counts it.

entries.name: HercList_RemoveFirstOfType
entries.description: (hangar, chassisType) The first bay whose machine is that chassis: Herc_StripMounts, the record freed, the bay emptied and the count at +0x20 decremented, and the bay index returned. With no match it returns its last probe, HercList_ChassisAt(hangar, 7). No salvage is paid.

entries.name: Herc_FirstBuiltBay
entries.description: The first of the eight bays holding a machine whose +0x4a is 100, or -1. What Repair_Enter falls back to when the selected bay holds nothing workable.

entries.name: Herc_SettleAfterMission
entries.description: Scraps or keeps a machine after a mission. Below 30 overall condition it is valued, freed and removed from the hangar; at 30 or above only the overall-condition slot is reset to 100. Returns the salvage credited.

entries.name: Herc_TypeToIndex
entries.description: Searches the nine-entry table at 0046f728 for a chassis type and returns its position. Retail contents are 0-8 in order, so the map is identity.

entries.name: Herc_CapacityForType
entries.description: Hardpoint capacity for a chassis type: Herc_TypeToIndex then 0046f73a[index]. This, not herc_inf.dat +0x06, is the figure every hardpoint loop uses.

entries.name: HercRecord_Ctor
entries.description: Zero-state HERC record: type and +0x02 to -1, capacity and occupancy 0, +0x4a build percent 100, +0x78 0, all three status-block condition arrays to 100 via HercStatus_InitAll.

entries.name: HercRecord_ClearMounts
entries.description: Frees every mounted weapon unit, zeroes the occupied count and resets each per-hardpoint condition to 100.

entries.name: HercRecord_ResolveName
entries.description: Sets the record's +0x04 name pointer to estext.bin string 0x6e + record +0x02, which is what fixes the chassis type order (0 Outlaw through 8 Razor). Type -1 resolves to string 0.

entries.name: HercRecord_ReadCatalogForm
entries.description: Reads the gam\*.dat form of a HERC record (type, build percent, build missions remaining, occupied hardpoint count, then sparse 6-byte mounts). Capacity, the +0x02 index and the name pointer are derived after the read, and the status block is left at the ctor's uniform 100.

entries.name: Herc_SetType
entries.description: Re-types an existing HERC record in place: clears mounts, sets +0x00, derives capacity, +0x02 and the name.

entries.name: Herc_Order
entries.description: Buys a chassis. Clears mounts, sets the type and capacity, build percent 0 and occupancy 0, copies herc_inf.dat +0x0c into +0x78 as the build time, and returns herc_inf.dat +0x08 * 1000 as the price to charge.

entries.name: Herc_BuildTick
entries.description: One mission of construction: decrements +0x78 and recomputes +0x4a as ((buildTime - remaining) * 100) / buildTime, the "% Complete" figure.

entries.name: Herc_Read
entries.description: Herc_Write's reader (asserts in src\herc.cpp): (herc, stream). HercRecord_ClearMounts, then reads the int16s +0 and +2, 0x42 bytes at +8, and the int16s +0x4a, +0x78, +0x4c and +0x4e; then, for each of the +0x4e occupied mounts, an int16 slot index (asserting the slot +0x50[index] is empty, line 0x9a), a 10-byte WeaponUnit_Ctor (asserting the allocation, line 0x9c) and WeaponUnit_ReadSaveForm into it. Ends with HercRecord_ResolveName. Hangar_Read calls it per HERC.

entries.name: Herc_Write
entries.description: herc.cpp. Serializes one 122-byte HERC record and its occupied mounts, each preceded by its slot index; Herc_Read is the reader. The writer loops to the mount capacity at +0x4c but the reader loops the occupied count at +0x4e.

entries.name: Repair_Auto
entries.description: The Auto Repair mode. Steps down repair levels while the cost exceeds the budget, stopping once the machine's own average condition reaches the level under test, then applies through Repair_Apply. Repairs and charges nothing when no level is affordable.

entries.name: Repair_Apply
entries.description: Writes a target condition across all three status-block arrays, leaving an empty hardpoint at 100.

entries.name: Herc_ScrapValueTons
entries.description: Herc_ScrapValue / 1000 -- the figure the herc scrap dialog quotes.

entries.name: Herc_Scrap
entries.description: Herc_ScrapValue then Herc_StripMounts; returns the value. Called by HercList_ScrapSelected and Herc_SettleAfterMission.

entries.name: Repair_SelectionCost
entries.description: Returns the repair cost of one component given (herc, category, index): reads the condition through HercStatus_Get, then Repair_UnitValueCost (00413968) to pick the unit value and price it. It is not Repair_ItemCost's wrapper -- it goes through Repair_LevelStepCost instead, so it prices one level up rather than a rebuild to 100. A hardpoint keys the weapon value table by the fitted weapon's id at herc + 0x50 + slot*4, not by the slot number.

entries.name: Herc_FitMount
entries.description: (herc, slot, weapon): Armory_AddUnit of the slot's unit and +0x4e minus one; weapon 0 empties the slot at condition 100 through HercStatus_Set; otherwise Armory_PopUnit of the weapon becomes the mount, its +0x04 the hardpoint condition, +0x4e plus one, and its +0x08 guidance 1 for ids 0xd-0xf and 5 for any other (0x10 included). An empty stock list leaves the slot empty and its condition unwritten. es2_xref.py finds one caller, Arming_FitSelected (0043dc8a).

entries.name: Herc_FitNewUnit
entries.description: (herc, slot, weapon, ammo): a new weapon unit of the weapon and ammunition type into the slot, the hardpoint at 100, occupancy up one.

entries.name: Herc_IsFlightworthy
entries.description: True when internals 0, 1, 5 and 8 -- both leg servos, the engine and life support -- are all above 50.

entries.name: Herc_HasWeapon
entries.description: True when one of the ten mounts holds a weapon id below 0x1d (the four pods do not count).

entries.name: Herc_ReadStatusBlock
entries.description: Reads a machine's 66-byte status block from results.dat straight over the record's +0x08 span, then destroys any mount whose per-hardpoint condition arrived at 0, decrementing the occupied count at +0x4e.

entries.name: Herc_StripMounts
entries.description: Empties a chassis's hardpoints when it is scrapped: a mount at 80 condition or better is returned to armory stock via Armory_AddUnit, anything below is destroyed.

entries.name: LoadHercInfDat
entries.description: Loads gam\herc_inf.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: Herc_GrantUnlocks
entries.description: Grants chassis availability from campaign progress. For each locked herc_inf.dat record, tests one campaign-flag slot against an expected value and sets +0x0e on a match, clearing the slot either way: Raptor II 0x3c/2, Maverick 0x3d/2, Ogre 0x3e/2, Razor 0x3f/1.

entries.name: ChassisAvailability_Write
entries.description: Save block 7: writes the 9 int16 chassis availability flags at 00483b62, stride 16 (herc_inf.dat record +0x0e), through the write slot. Game_SaveSlot calls it.

entries.name: ChassisAvailability_Read
entries.description: Save block 7 reader: reads the 9 int16 flags back to 00483b62, stride 16. Game_LoadSlot calls it.

entries.name: Weapon_ClassIndexForId
entries.description: Searches the thirty-entry table at 0046f868 for a weapon catalog id and returns its position. The table holds ids 0-18 and 22-32, so the three Bull weapons resolve to -1.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_Ctor
entries.description: Zero-state weapon unit: { -1, -1, 100, 100, 5 }. The trailing 5 is the "nothing guided" ammo type that reaches data\player.mec as the empty-hardpoint filler.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_Init
entries.description: Fills a weapon unit from an id and three values, deriving the class index at +0x02 via Weapon_ClassIndexForId.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_ReadCatalogForm
entries.description: Reads the 6-byte gam\*.dat form of a weapon unit: id, condition, ammo type. The class index is derived and +0x04 stays at the ctor's 100.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_SetWeaponAndAmmo
entries.description: (unit, weapon, ammo): unit+0 = weapon id, unit+2 = Weapon_ClassIndexForId(weapon), unit+8 = ammo, leaving +4 and +6 as they are (WeaponUnit_Init sets all of them). Herc_FitNewUnit calls it on the slot's unit.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_ReadSaveForm
entries.description: Reads all five int16 of a weapon unit, the form the save file and the armory stock use.

entries.name: WeaponUnit_WriteSaveForm
entries.description: Writes all five int16 of a weapon unit. Mirror of WeaponUnit_ReadSaveForm.

entries.name: HercStatus_InitAll
entries.description: Initializes all three status-block condition arrays to 100: 13 external at +0x00, 10 at +0x1a (9 internals plus the overall slot), 10 per-hardpoint at +0x2e.

entries.name: HercStatus_OverallCondition
entries.description: Mean condition over 13 external entries, the first 9 internal entries and one per occupied hardpoint, divided by hardpoints + 0x16. The divisor is what proves the 13/9 split and that internal index 9 is excluded from its own average.

entries.name: HercStatus_GroupMean
entries.description: Mean of one external component group, read through the -1-terminated group table at 0046f8a4. This is accessor mode 0.

entries.name: HercStatus_SetGroup
entries.description: Writes one value into every external facet an external group covers, walking the group's -1-terminated row of HercComponentGroupTable (0046f8a4).

entries.name: HercStatus_Set
entries.description: HercStatus_Get's setter: (block, mode, index, value). Mode 0 writes an external group through HercStatus_SetGroup (00411c78), mode 1 block+0x1a+index*2, mode 2 block+0x2e+index*2.

entries.name: HercStatus_Get
entries.description: Indexed accessor into a HERC's 66-byte status block (record +0x08): mode 1 reads block+0x1a+index*2 (10 condition values, index 9 being the machine's overall condition), mode 2 reads block+0x2e+index*2 (10 per-hardpoint conditions). NOT an average -- (block,1,9) is one element, not a mean over 9 sections. HercStatus_Set (00411cbd) is the matching setter.

entries.name: WeaponsDat_ReadRecord
entries.description: Per-record body reader for WEAPONS.DAT (29-byte stride, blockLen-prefixed front block, price field at 0x14 scaled x1000). Called from LoadWeaponsDat.

entries.name: Armory_ReadWeaponStock
entries.description: (record, stream): Armory_ClearStock(record), reads one byte into record+0x16 and an int16 count, then that many units, each a new 10-byte WeaponUnit_Ctor filled by WeaponUnit_ReadSaveForm and handed to Armory_AddUnit. Armory_Read runs it on each of the 0x21 weapons.dat records.

entries.name: Armory_WriteStock
entries.description: Armory_Write's per-weapon writer: the record's +0x16 unlock byte, the +0x17 count and that many units from the +0x19 list, head first, so each save and load reverses a weapon's units.

entries.name: Armory_PopUnit
entries.description: Unlinks the head of a weapons.dat record's +0x19 unit list, frees the list node, decrements +0x17 and returns the unit; 0 when 00411f87 reports the list empty.

entries.name: Armory_AddUnit
entries.description: armory.cpp: pushes a weapon unit onto its catalog record's +0x19 owned-unit list and increments the +0x17 owned count.

entries.name: Armory_UnitListEmpty
entries.description: (record): true when the weapons.dat record's owned-unit count (+0x17) is 0. Armory_PopUnit tests it.

entries.name: Armory_ClearStock
entries.description: Pops and frees every unit on a weapons.dat record's +0x19 owned-unit list through Armory_PopUnit, one off the +0x17 count each.

entries.name: LoadWeaponsDat
entries.description: File-level parser for gam\weapons.dat (SHELL0/GAM weapon catalog, 33 entries). Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: Armory_ResetQueue
entries.description: Resets the weapon build queue: five free workspace slots at 0046f8d4, all five slot ids at 0046f8d6 cleared.

entries.name: Armory_Read
entries.description: Save blocks 1-2 reader, the mirror of Armory_Write: 00411dbb on each of the 0x21 weapons.dat records (WeaponsDat_RecordArray, stride 0x1d), Armory_ResetQueue, then the int16 ArmoryQueueFreeSlots and five {int16 slot, int16 weapon} pairs, each weapon stored at ArmoryQueueSlots[slot]. Game_LoadSlot calls it.

entries.name: Armory_Write
entries.description: armory.cpp. Writes all 33 weapons.dat catalog records' armory state: the +0x16 byte, the owned-unit count at +0x17, and that many 10-byte units from the +0x19 list. Armory_Read is the reader.

entries.name: PlayerMec_WriteUnlockTable
entries.description: Closes the data\player.mec export with int16 33 then 33 bytes, each weapon catalog record's +0x16 unlock flag at the 29-byte stride. Present in all ten retail player.mec files. Nothing traced reads it back.

entries.name: Armory_AddNewUnit
entries.description: (id, fitCondition) Allocates a ten-byte weapon unit, WeaponUnit_Init(unit, id, fitCondition, 100, 5), and appends it to the id's catalog record through Armory_AddUnit. The debrief's results.dat salvage pairs (campaign only) and Armory_GrantCampaignWeapons' unit grants (fitCondition 100) both come through it.

entries.name: WeaponsDat_IdAtRank
entries.description: Weapon catalog id holding the given rank in WeaponsDat_RankTable, skipping rank 99; -1 when no id has it. This is the rank table only established use -- catalog ordering.

entries.name: Armory_AutoFillQueue
entries.description: Resets the build queue then walks the catalog in rank order via WeaponsDat_IdAtRank, enqueueing each weapon that is unlocked (record +0x16), that the player owns fewer than two of (record +0x17), and that the cumulative total leaves affordable.

entries.name: Armory_TrimQueueToBudget
entries.description: Clears build-queue slots from the front while the queued total exceeds the salvage pool, restoring one workspace slot per entry cleared.

entries.name: Armory_RefreshQueue
entries.description: Armory_AutoFillQueue while ShellOption_WeaponsBuildMode is 0 (built automatically), Armory_TrimQueueToBudget otherwise. Run by the weapon scrap's ACCEPT.

entries.name: Armory_DeliverQueue
entries.description: Delivers the whole weapon build queue: per occupied slot allocates a ten-byte weapon unit, initializes it with ammo type 1 for the missile racks (ids 13-16) and 5 otherwise, appends it to that catalog record via Armory_AddUnit, and accumulates the price. Returns the total to charge -- it is a delivery with a running total, not a pure cost calculation.

entries.name: Armory_ScrapStock
entries.description: (short)Armory_ScrapValueTons(id) * 1000, after Armory_ClearStock has emptied the weapon's stock (the value is taken first).

entries.name: Armory_QueuedTotal
entries.description: Sums weapons.dat +0x14 over the occupied build-queue slots. This is the "Allocated:" figure, and purchases are gated on the pool covering it plus the new item.

entries.name: Armory_FirstFreeSlot
entries.description: Index of the first empty build-queue slot, or -1 when the workspace count is 0 or all five are taken.

entries.name: Armory_Enqueue
entries.description: Puts a weapon catalog id in the first free build-queue slot and decrements the workspace count. No-op when the queue is full.

entries.name: Armory_Dequeue
entries.description: Clears every build-queue slot holding the given weapon catalog id, incrementing the workspace count once per slot cleared.

entries.name: Armory_QueuedCount
entries.description: How many of the five queue slots hold the given weapon id.

entries.name: Armory_ScrapValueTons
entries.description: What scrapping the armory's whole stock of a weapon yields, in tons: (weapons.dat +0x14 / 1000) * the +0x17 count held / 10, raised to 1 when that is below 1 and the count is not 0; 0 for an empty stock. The weapon scrap dialog quotes it.

entries.name: Armory_GrantCampaignWeapons
entries.description: Debrief-side weapon grants, campaign only, called by Game_ProcessMissionResults right after Herc_GrantUnlocks. Loop 1: for each still-locked weapon id with a flag slot in WeaponGrant_UnlockSlots, sets weapons.dat +0x16 when the flag equals WeaponGrant_UnlockValues[id], and zeroes the slot either way. Loop 2: for flag slots 0x15-0x31, adds flag[s] units of WeaponGrant_UnitIds[s-0x15] at condition 100 via Armory_AddNewUnit (0041229d), without clearing the slot; returns the number of units added.

entries.name: CareerDat_ReadStage
entries.description: career.cpp. Reads one gam\career.dat stage: an int16 campaign index, an int16 mission count, then that many int16 name indices, each resolved through missions.bin at load. Verified byte-exact against the retail 148-byte file: 6 stages, stage 0 the 11 training missions and stages 1-5 the ten missions of each campaign chapter.

entries.name: LoadCareerDat
entries.description: Loads gam\career.dat. Confirmed via direct string reference to the literal path.

entries.name: Career_SeedPosition
entries.description: Seeds a new career's (stage, mission) by mode: campaign (1) -> (1, 0); training (0) -> (0, PracticeScreen_SelectedRow), the practice row. Called by Game_NewCareer with CampaignModeFlag.

entries.name: Career_SaveSlot
entries.description: career.cpp. Writes the 152-byte career block (stage, mission-in-stage, and the three mission.str line-index arrays) to the save stream, then copies data\script.dat, data\mission.str and data\player.mec out to sav\script%d.dat, sav\missn%d.str and sav\player%d.mec. The save direction; Career_LoadSlot is the reverse.

entries.name: Career_LoadSlot
entries.description: career.cpp. Reads the 152-byte career block back and copies sav\script%d.dat, sav\missn%d.str and sav\player%d.mec in to data\. Its third parameter, when set, also rebuilds the assembled briefing text from the restored data\mission.str (FUN_00412f97). The load direction; Career_SaveSlot is the reverse.

entries.name: Career_StartMissionLoad
entries.description: Shows the mission-name dialog with the career position's name and, unless 00482284 is set, posts a press and a release to its Use Default button.

entries.name: Career_Advance
entries.description: career.cpp. Loads the mission named by the current (stage, mission) position, then advances the position -- unconditionally, whatever the outcome. Returns 1 past the last stage (campaign complete), 0 on a failed mission at a stage boundary, else 2. Fires the hard-coded squad events at stage 1 mission 3 and stage 1 mission 6.

entries.name: Career_SetBriefing
entries.description: Copies a loaded mission's 10 objective, 30 briefing and 30 intelligence mission.str line indices into the career block, counting the non-(-1) ones, and its briefing movie id into 004840b8, all from a by-value argument.

entries.name: Career_BuildBriefingText
entries.description: career.cpp. Loads data\mission.str and concatenates the lines named by the career block's 10- and 30-entry index arrays into single strings (-1 skips a slot).

entries.name: Career_FreeBriefingText
entries.description: Mem_DeleteArray and clears each of the three text buffers 0046fb1c, 0046fb20 and 0046fb24 that are non-null. Career_BuildBriefingText calls it.

entries.name: Career_SetDebriefLines
entries.description: Copies thirty mission.str line indices into 0048407c and a movie id into 004840ba from its stack; reached from Career_Advance through Msn_LoadDebrief (0041d2c3) for the mission just flown.

entries.name: Career_BuildDebriefText
entries.description: Loads data\mission.str and concatenates the lines 0048407c names into DAT_0046fb28; Career_Advance calls it.

entries.name: Career_FreeDebriefText
entries.description: Mem_DeleteArray and clears the debrief text buffer 0046fb28 when non-null. Career_BuildDebriefText calls it.

entries.name: Career_ObjectivesText
entries.description: Returns DAT_0046fb20, the objectives Career_BuildBriefingText assembles from the 10-entry array at 00483fea.

entries.name: Career_BriefingText
entries.description: Returns DAT_0046fb1c, the briefing Career_BuildBriefingText assembles from the 30-entry array at 00484000.

entries.name: Career_IntelligenceText
entries.description: Returns DAT_0046fb24, the intelligence report Career_BuildBriefingText assembles from the 30-entry array at 0048403e.

entries.name: Career_DebriefText
entries.description: Returns DAT_0046fb28, the debrief Career_BuildDebriefText assembles from the array at 0048407c.

entries.name: Career_BriefingMovie
entries.description: Returns DAT_004840b8, the movie id Mission_Show enqueues in the briefing view.

entries.name: Career_DebriefMovie
entries.description: Returns DAT_004840ba, the movie id Mission_Show enqueues in the debrief view.

entries.name: LoadDamageDat_Shell
entries.description: Loads gam\damage.dat -- VSHELL/UI-facing summary table (fixed 9x{6,9} shorts + 0x21 shorts), distinct from DBSIM's variable per-Herc hit-zone table loaded by HercPiece_LoadTable. Confirmed via direct string reference.

entries.name: Repair_LevelForCondition
entries.description: First level 0-5 whose band floor in 0046fd84 is at or below the given condition; 0 when none matches.

entries.name: Repair_TargetForLevel
entries.description: Target condition for a repair level: 0046fd78[0] for level 0, else 0046fd78[level] + 1.

entries.name: Repair_LevelStepCost
entries.description: Prices one component up a single repair level: (target - condition) * unitValue / 100, where the target is RepairTargetTable[0] = 100 at level 0 and otherwise the band floor of the level above, read as 0046fd82 + level*2. The repair screen's per-item figure, as against Repair_HercCost's rebuild to 100. param_3 == 0 selects the opposite direction, which the shell does not use.

entries.name: Repair_ItemCost
entries.description: Cost to bring one component from its current condition to a target: zero when already at or above it, else (levelTarget - current) * unitValue / 100.

entries.name: Repair_UnitValueCost
entries.description: Picks the unit value by accessor mode -- HercExternalGroupValues and HercInternalValues at chassisType*0x21 + index, WeaponScrapValues at the weapon id -- and calls Repair_LevelStepCost (00413871) on it. It formats nothing and draws nothing; it returns a cost.

entries.name: Repair_HercCost
entries.description: Total repair cost for a machine to a target condition: Repair_ItemCost over the six external groups, the nine internals, and each occupied hardpoint at its weapon's scrap value.

entries.name: Herc_ScrapValue
entries.description: Salvage yield for scrapping a machine: sum of condition * unitValue / 100 over the six external groups and nine internals, plus each mount under 80 condition (the complement of what Herc_StripMounts returns to stock). The under-construction branch divides before multiplying and yields 0 for every progress figure from 1 to 99 -- confirmed in raw disassembly, idiv ecx at 00413b8d preceding imul ecx at 00413b9d and imul edi,eax,1000 at 00413b9f.

entries.name: RepairLayout_FindWeaponPart
entries.description: Looks one weapon's part up in a chassis's rpr_*.dat weapon groups: the record in group weaponId whose part id is the third argument (slot + 6 at both callers), or null.

entries.name: LoadRepairLayouts
entries.description: hercdisp.cpp: loads all nine gam\rpr_*.dat repair-bay layouts into a per-chassis structure of 33 counts followed by 33 record pointers, 0xc6 bytes per chassis.

entries.name: Repair_BuildDiagrams
entries.description: Fills both per-bay damage pictures for all eight bays. Externals: one grid part per gam\rpr_*.dat component record at its (+0x02, +0x06) from frame +0x12 of dba\rpr_<chassis>.dba, plus one per occupied hardpoint found by FUN_00413ccc on the per-weapon groups. Internals: the single trailing record at 00484534, from dba\<chassis>_int.dba, with a second part for the Razor. Bank path tables at 0046fedc and 0046ff04, handles cached in 0046fdc4 and 0046fdec.

entries.name: Repair_WeaponPartRect
entries.description: The inclusive rect {x, y, x + width, y + height} of the weapon part fitted in one mount, from its rpr_*.dat record and its rpr_wpns.dba frame; the repair tab's hotspot for that mount. Asserts with a Data Error message when the chassis has no record for the weapon in that socket.

entries.name: Squad_FreeRepairPictures
entries.description: Frees the bank at 0046fde8 and, for the chassis in each of the eight bays (HercList_ChassisAt(00482ac3, bay)), the banks at 0046fdc4[chassis] and 0046fdec[chassis], with GLBitmapArray_Dtor(_, 3), clearing each pointer; ESGrid_InitAllRows on SquadSlotPictureWidgets[bay] and 0048d118[bay]. Squad_FreeTabPictures' tab 3 (REPAIR) arm.

entries.name: Repair_ColorDiagram
entries.description: Colours the selected bay's damage picture for the selection's column: on the external picture each body part's 0xe remap target to its group's band colour and each mount part's 0xf target to its hardpoint's; on the internals picture the nine 0046fe80 indices of slot 0 to the internals' band colours. Called by Repair_BuildDiagrams and on every Repair_RefreshDetail.

entries.name: Arming_RowLive
entries.description: Whether an inventory row is live: always with no hardpoint selected; with one, only when the chassis's armory layout has a part for the weapon at slot+2 and the weapon is unlocked.

entries.name: LoadArmoryLayouts
entries.description: hercdisp.cpp: loads all nine gam\arm_*.dat armory layouts. Two leading records per chassis instead of a counted list, and two 8-byte rect blocks per record instead of one.

entries.name: Squad_BuildBayPictures
entries.description: Fills the squad panel's eight bay pictures and the empty picture (DAT_0048d4dc) for WEAPONS, BUILD and CREW: moves each to {5, 0x2b} at 0xe7 x 0x105, grid lines off, then the arm_*.dat top and bottom records from dba\<stem>_bod.dba (mt_3qtr.dba at 0% built, body frames 2/3 or 4/5 while building) and each fitted weapon's group record (id slot + 2) from <stem>_wep.dba.

entries.name: Squad_FreeChassisPictures
entries.description: Frees the bitmap bank at 0046fe34, clears the grid 0048d4dc, and for each of the eight squad slots frees the banks at 0046fe10, 0046fe38 and 0046fe5c indexed by that slot's chassis (HercList_ChassisAt) and clears the slot's SquadSlotPictureWidgets grid. Squad_FreeTabPictures runs it from three of its branches, tabs 2 and 4 among them.

entries.name: Squad_SetEmptyBayPicture
entries.description: Puts dba\mt_3qtr.dba frames 0 and 1 at (1,1) and (1,0x8c) into the selected bay's squad-panel picture, after clearing it.

entries.name: Arming_MarkHardpoint
entries.description: Redraws a socket's weapon part (slot hardpoint+2) on the bay picture from the fitted weapon, and puts the socket's outline in part slot 12 from a second per-chassis bank, remapping 0xba to 99.

entries.name: Build_FillBlueprints
entries.description: Fills the build screen's nine blueprint Grids from the rpr_*.dat body records (DAT_00484d28/DAT_00484d14) and the dba rpr_<chassis> banks, remap pair 0xe -> 0xe, no weapons.

entries.name: Build_FreeBitmapsAndGrids
entries.description: For each of nine slots: GLBitmapArray_Dtor(_, 3) on the non-null array at 0046fdc4[i] and clears it, then ESGrid_InitAllRows on 0048d88c[i]. Build_Leave calls it.

entries.name: Msn_ConditionParentValue
entries.description: (guid, count) -> the first of the first count row-1 records with the GUID: a type-1 record's draw, or -99 for a type-3 record; -1 for none. A type-2 record survives on its parent's value.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveTextRef
entries.description: The .ENG-record member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family: a text id to its data\mission.str line.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow3Ref
entries.description: The row-3 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow6Ref
entries.description: (guid, count, exported) -> a row-6 GUID's position among the first count records: with exported set, records whose GUID is -1 are not counted, giving the script.dat index; otherwise the array index. -1 for none. One of a family, one per row.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow7Ref
entries.description: The row-7 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow8Ref
entries.description: The row-8 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow9Ref
entries.description: The row-9 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow10Ref
entries.description: The row-10 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow11Ref
entries.description: The row-11 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow16Ref
entries.description: The row-16 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow12Ref
entries.description: The row-12 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow13Ref
entries.description: The row-13 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow14Ref
entries.description: The row-14 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_ResolveRow15Ref
entries.description: The row-15 member of Msn_ResolveRow6Ref's family.

entries.name: Msn_PickVariant
entries.description: (key) -> the row-1 index of a variant: the type-3 record whose +0x06 is key draws below its +0x0a into +0x0c, and the type-2 child whose range holds the draw is returned. Draws again on every call.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow6
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-6 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-6 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow7
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-7 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-7 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow8
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-8 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-8 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow12
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-12 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-12 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow13
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-13 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-13 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow14
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-14 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-14 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_VariantSourceRow15
entries.description: (key, count) -> the first of the first count row-15 records whose condition is Msn_PickVariant(key)'s GUID: the record a row-15 record with that variant key copies from.

entries.name: Msn_ApplyHeaderPatch
entries.description: Row 2: writes each of the patch buffer's ten header words that is not its unset value (1 for the first, 0 for the rest) into DAT_00485446 upward, and each flag index that is not -1 into the clear list at DAT_0048545a.

entries.name: Msn_MergeText
entries.description: A repeated .ENG id: moves the new record's text onto the earlier entry.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow10
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-10 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow11
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-11 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow12
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-12 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow13
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-13 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow14
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-14 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow15
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-15 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_MergeRow16
entries.description: (source, target) -> a repeated row-16 GUID: copies each field of the new record that is not its unset value onto the earlier one.

entries.name: Msn_ConditionFilterGate
entries.description: msn_gen.cpp. (condition, count) -> 1 when the condition is -1 or names one of the first count surviving row-1 records, else 0. Every .MSN record passes through it; the row-1 comparisons themselves are MsnGen_ParseMsnFile's.

entries.name: Msn_ClearPatchedFlags
entries.description: Zeroes every campaign flag the row-2 clear list at DAT_0048545a names.

entries.name: Msn_LoadEngText
entries.description: Loads the mission's .eng (.fre/.ger by 0048227a) between rows 2 and 3: condition-filtered, a repeated id replacing the text. DAT_00470664 is the count kept.

entries.name: MissionStr_Write
entries.description: Writes data\mission.str from the loaded .ENG records: size, count, then length/text/NUL/attribute-count 0 per line. Opened without O_TRUNC.

entries.name: MsnGen_ParseMsnFile
entries.description: The raw .MSN byte parser (msn_gen.cpp). Revision-field check, scratch/patch pass, then 17 record-array rows with a condition-filter/template-inheritance system. Macro-structure confirmed byte-exact against 61/62 real retail .MSN files.

entries.name: WriteScriptDatFile
entries.description: Fully traced: the WRITER of data\script.dat. Serializes directly from the same in-memory .msn row-array globals FUN_00417b67 populates (DAT_0047064e/0x16=row6, DAT_00470650/10=row7, DAT_00470656=row8, DAT_0047065e/0xc=row9, DAT_00470660/0x52=row10, DAT_00470662/0x1e=row11, DAT_00470652/0x90=row12, DAT_00470654/0x66=row13, DAT_0047065c/0x3e=row14, DAT_00470658/0x16=row15, DAT_0047065a/0xa4=row16, DAT_0047064a/0x3a=row17, DAT_00470640=row4), filtering out GUID==-1 (deleted/inactive) records per row and exporting only a field subset of each. See docs/formats/script-dat.md for the full block table.

entries.name: MsnGen_HercArrayIndex
entries.description: (exported) -> the row-12 array index of the exported-th record whose GUID is set; a negative argument gives the first. Its return is in AX, which the decompiler drops.

entries.name: MsnGen_FreeRows
entries.description: Frees the mission loader's row arrays (conditions, .ENG strings and their texts, row 4, row 5, and the rest) and nulls each pointer. Msn_LoadDebrief calls it after handing row 5 on.

entries.name: MsnGen_BuildPlayerHerc
entries.description: Training: the player's machine into bay 0 -- group 0's first member while the practice row is below 4 or DAT_0047363c is set, else gam\ini_*.dat for prefs option 0x28.

entries.name: MsnGen_LoadMission
entries.description: msn_gen.cpp. Calls MsnGen_ParseMsnFile (00417b67) first with the .msn path, then WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54) -- confirmed to be data\script.dat's writer, serializing a GUID-filtered field-subset re-export of the same in-memory row arrays MsnGen_ParseMsnFile just populated. See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: Msn_LoadDebriefRows
entries.description: The debrief's reload of the mission just flown: row 1 against the flags (drawing ShellRandom for type-1 conditions, as the main load does), row 2 skipped so no flag is cleared, the .ENG text, row 3, row 4 skipped, and row 5 kept -- the debrief text records MsnGen_ParseMsnFile skips. Writes data\mission.str. Called only from Msn_LoadDebrief.

entries.name: Msn_LoadDebrief
entries.description: (missionPath) Msn_LoadDebriefRows, then row 5's first slot handed by value to Career_SetDebriefLines -- its thirty mission.str lines and its row-3 value, the debrief movie -- and the load's arrays freed (MsnGen_FreeRows (0041c28f)). Called only from Career_Advance, for the mission at the career position before it advances.

entries.name: PtrVector_Append
entries.description: (vector, value): PtrVector_Grow, then stores value in the new last slot of the dword array at +10; returns 0 when the grow fails.

entries.name: PtrVector_RemoveAt
entries.description: (vector, index): returns 0 for an index outside 0..count-1; otherwise shifts the later elements of the dword array at +10 down one and PtrVector_DropLast's. PtrVector_PopFront calls it with 0.

entries.name: PtrVector_Grow
entries.description: (vector): adds one to the count at +0, in place when the data pointer at +10 is set and the capacity at +4 allows it, otherwise through PtrVector_Resize with the new count. Returns whether it succeeded.

entries.name: PtrVector_DropLast
entries.description: (vector): decrements the count (+0) when it is positive. Returns 1.

entries.name: PtrVector_Resize
entries.description: PtrArray::resize (assert 'PtrArray:resize: Could not allocate memory' in wsrc\ptrarray.cpp line 0x94): (vector, count). A count below 1 frees the data (+10) and zeroes count (+0), capacity (+4) and data; otherwise rounds the capacity up to a multiple of the int16 grow step (+8), Mem_HeapAlloc's or reallocs the data to it, and stores count and capacity. Returns 1. PtrVector_Grow calls it when the capacity is exhausted.

entries.name: EventConsumer_Ctor
entries.description: EventConsumer constructor (vtable 00470c58 at +4, RTTI name 'EventConsumer', 0x10 bytes): (this, owner) EventProducer_Ctor's shape, appending this to the owner's consumer list with Dispatcher_AddConsumer. WinConsumer_Ctor runs it first.

entries.name: EventConsumer_Dtor
entries.description: EventConsumer destructor (vtable 00470c58 at +4, RTTI name 'EventConsumer', 0x10 bytes): (obj, flags) reinstalls the vtable, calls 0041dd79(+8, obj) when +8 is non-null, then Mem_Delete(obj) when flags bit 0 is set.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0041d644; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: EventProducer_Ctor
entries.description: EventProducer constructor (vtable 00470c44 at +4, RTTI name 'EventProducer', 0x10 bytes): (this, owner) SListNode_Init(this), installs the vtable, clears the int16s +0xc and +0xe, appends this to the owner's producer list with Dispatcher_AddProducer when owner is non-null, and stores owner at +8. WinKeyboardProducer_Ctor and WinMouseProducer_Ctor run it first.

entries.name: EventProducer_Dtor
entries.description: EventProducer destructor: (this, flags) reinstalls vtable 00470c44, EventProducer_UnlinkFromOwner(+8, this) when +8 is non-null, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. WinKeyboardProducer_Dtor and WinMouseProducer_Dtor end with it.

entries.name: EventBase_Ctor
entries.description: EventBase constructor (vtable 00470c18, RTTI name 'EventBase', 0xc bytes, over ClassItem): clears the word at +6. WinEvent_Ctor runs it first.

entries.name: EventBase_Dtor
entries.description: EventBase vtable 00470c18 slot +0x18 (event, flags): decrements the live-object counter at *005ddec0, restores the vtable, then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The event handlers delete every event they consume through this slot.

entries.name: EventBase_Clone
entries.description: EventBase vtable 00470c18 slot +0x1c (event): Mem_New's a 0xc-byte EventBase (EventBase_Ctor), copies +4, +6 and +8 into it and returns it. Each event class overrides it with a copy of its own size and fields.

entries.name: EventBase_GetClassTag
entries.description: EventBase vtable 00470c18 slot 0: returns 0x500000.

entries.name: EventBase_GetStreamSize
entries.description: EventBase slot +4: returns 8, what EventBase_ReadFromStream reads. WinEvent_GetStreamSize adds to it.

entries.name: EventBase_GetMemorySize
entries.description: EventBase slot +8: returns 0xc, the object's size.

entries.name: EventBase_ReadFromStream
entries.description: EventBase slot +0xc (event, stream): reads the int16 +4, the int16 +6 (through a local) and the int32 time +8 through the stream's read slot. The labels are EventBase_DebugPrint's: Event, Attr, Time.

entries.name: EventBase_WriteToStream
entries.description: EventBase slot +0x10 (event, stream): writes +4, +6 and +8 as EventBase_ReadFromStream reads them.

entries.name: EventBase_DebugPrint
entries.description: EventBase slot +0x14 (event, verbose, indent): prints '%sEvent: %u Attr: %X Time: %d' with +4, +6 and +8 to stdout, indented by indent spaces (at most 99).

entries.name: PtrVector_Append_Thunk
entries.description: Forwards (vector, value) to PtrVector_Append. Keyboard_PostEvents and WinMouseProducer_PostEvents append each event to the vector at the input object's +8 through it.

entries.name: Dispatcher_RunQueue
entries.description: (dispatcher, typeMask, subMask): calls slot +4 of every idle handler on the list at +0x1c whose masks (+0xc, +0xe) match; then pops each queued item (PtrArray at +0, asserting 'PtrArray::operator[]: Index out of range'), passes it through the filter functions at +0x18 (count +0xe), delivers it to every listener on the list at +0x20 whose masks match the item's type words (+4, +6), and deletes it.

entries.name: Dispatcher_AddProducer
entries.description: (dispatcher, producer): SList_Append(dispatcher+0x1c, producer), the producer list.

entries.name: Dispatcher_AddConsumer
entries.description: (dispatcher, consumer): SList_Append(dispatcher+0x20, consumer), the consumer list.

entries.name: EventProducer_UnlinkFromOwner
entries.description: (owner, producer): EventConsumer_UnlinkFromOwner's twin for the producer list: when the owner's cursor +0x28 is producer, steps it to producer's next (+0); then SList_Remove(owner+0x1c, producer).

entries.name: EventConsumer_UnlinkFromOwner
entries.description: (owner, consumer): when the owner's cursor +0x24 is consumer, steps it to consumer's next (+0); then SList_Remove(owner+0x20, consumer). EventConsumer_Dtor runs it on its +8 owner.

entries.name: SListNode_Init
entries.description: (node): clears the next link at +0.

entries.name: SList_LinkAfter
entries.description: (link, node): node->next = *link; *link = node.

entries.name: SList_Append
entries.description: (head, node): follows the next links (+0) from head to the last one and SList_LinkAfter's node there.

entries.name: SList_Remove
entries.description: (head, node): follows the next links (+0) from head to the one holding node, links around it and clears node's next; returns 1, or 0 when node is not on the list.

entries.name: Avi_BuildPalette
entries.description: CreatePalette of 236 entries from entries 10-245 of the palette installed, into Avi_PaletteHandle, which Avi_Play hands the movie with 'setvideo mov palette handle to %d'.

entries.name: Avi_OpenDevice
entries.description: Opens MCI's avivideo device for one movie; with its argument 1 first builds the movie palette (Avi_BuildPalette). Movie_PlayQueue passes its own argument through.

entries.name: Avi_CloseMovie
entries.description: 'close mov', with a message box on an MCI error. Called by Avi_Play as playback ends.

entries.name: Avi_CloseDevice
entries.description: 'close avivideo', with a message box on an MCI error. Called by Movie_PlayQueue after each movie.

entries.name: Avi_MoveWindow
entries.description: Moves the MCI movie window to a {left, top, width, height} rect through MoveWindow; Avi_Play's only use of it.

entries.name: Avi_Play
entries.description: Plays one AVI through MCI ('open %s alias mov style child', 'play mov window notify'; src\avi.cpp). Sets the palette, SetCapture on the main window and DAT_00470d70 = 1, then loops until DAT_00470d60 is set -- a mouse button down in the window procedure, or Esc or Space (scan codes 1 and 0x39) -- then ReleaseCapture and DAT_00470d70 = 0. Returns 1, or 0 when the open fails. Its one caller is Movie_PlayQueue.

entries.name: MovieQueue_Contains
entries.description: Whether any of the ten MovieQueue_Entries carries the id; Movie_Enqueue adds nothing when it does.

entries.name: Movie_Enqueue
entries.description: Adds a movie to the ten-entry ring at 00485668 at write index DAT_00470e6c, when movies are on (DAT_00482275) and the id is not already queued: the id, a rect, a palette index (0xffff for none), a flag that ends the run on the campaign map's location tab, and a callback run after it. Movie_PlayQueue plays the ring.

entries.name: Movie_PlayQueue
entries.description: Plays every queued movie from read index DAT_00470e6e, each through Avi_Play with its palette and rect, lighting the MISSION tab around it while the frame is up, then runs the entry's callback and frees it. Sets DAT_00470e70 = 1 for the whole run and clears it only when it finds the ring empty -- the shell's main loop (FUN_00401525) calls it with 1 once a pass -- or while it waits on the insert-CD panel (DAT_0048d108). Also called directly after enqueuing by the startup (FUN_004012b0), Game_ProcessMissionResults and FUN_004315ec.

entries.name: Window_SetRect
entries.description: Stores a constructor's rect verbatim into +0x25/+0x29/+0x2d/+0x31 -- left, top, right, bottom, parent-relative -- has FUN_0041ef45 derive the absolute rect into +0x15/+0x19/+0x1d/+0x21, attaches to the parent with Window_AttachChild (0041f134), ORs 0x1f into the event mask +0x39, and stores its 4th argument, the click handler, at +0x3d.

entries.name: Window_MoveRect
entries.description: Moves a widget after construction: rewrites the parent-relative rect at +0x25, rederives the absolute one and repaints. Called on one widget (0048d7dc). Window_SetPosition (0041ee1d) also moves widgets (the repair diagrams and bay pictures), and Window_SetWidth resizes them.

entries.name: Window_SetWidth
entries.description: (widget, width): sets the right edge +0x2d to left + width - 1 and the screen right +0x1d to match, when width is positive, the widget has a parent, the new width fits inside the parent, and no child's screen right edge (+0x1d) would fall outside. Moves the pointer off and back on (Pointer_Leave, Pointer_Enter) when it is over this widget and now past its edge.

entries.name: Window_SetHeight
entries.description: (widget, height): Window_SetWidth's vertical twin: sets the bottom edge +0x31 and the screen bottom +0x21 under the same conditions, with the children's screen bottoms (+0x21) checked.

entries.name: Window_RepaintRecursive
entries.description: Posts a repaint event (type 4 at event+0xc, target widget at +0x20; a 0x24-byte event from the global operator new at 00408107) to a widget, then recurses over its children (first child +0xd, next sibling +5). A hidden widget (+0x11 bit 2) and its whole subtree are skipped. The shell's usual 'redraw this panel' call.
entries.source: docs/shell/screen-layout.md#showing-and-hiding-a-widget (the +0x11 hidden bit and child links); WinButton_HandleEvent's type-4 repaint

entries.name: Window_SetPosition
entries.description: Window::setPosition (assert 'Window::setPosition > can't move...' in wsrc\window.cpp when the widget has no parent): (widget, {x, y}). Clamps the position to be non-negative and to keep the widget inside its parent, moves the rect +0x25..+0x31 there keeping its size, then Window_ResolveRect and Window_RepaintRecursive. Repair_BuildDiagrams and Squad_BuildBayPictures place their pictures with it.

entries.name: Window_ResolveRect
entries.description: (widget, parent): derives the absolute rect (+0x15..+0x21) from the parent-relative one (+0x25..+0x31) by adding the parent's absolute left/top (the widget's own parent when none is passed; the relative rect as is at the root), then recurses over the children (first child +0xd, next sibling +5). Window_SetRect and Window_MoveRect call it.

entries.name: Window_AssertFit
entries.description: Window::fit's checks (src: wsrc\window.cpp lines 199, 0xcd, 0xd3, 0xd9, severity 4, each after Mono_Printf'ing four values at 0,0): (window, parent). Asserts the window's screen rect (min +0x15/+0x19, max +0x1d/+0x21) and parent-relative rect (min +0x25/+0x29, max +0x2d/+0x31) are not inverted, that its screen min is not below its parent min, and that the parent's screen max (+0x1d/+0x21) is not below the window's parent max. Window_SetRect runs it when a parent is given, between Window_ResolveRect and Window_AttachChild.

entries.name: Window_AttachChild
entries.description: Window_AttachChild(parent, child): pushes the child onto the HEAD of the parent's child list (+0xd head, +5 next sibling, +9 previous sibling or, on the head with +0x11 bit 1 set, the parent). Only caller Window_SetRect, so every child list runs newest first -- which is why the later-built of two overlapping siblings wins a click.

entries.name: Window_LastSibling
entries.description: (unused, widget): follows the next-sibling link at +5 (a parent's children run from its +0xd through +5) until it is null and returns the last widget of the chain, in EAX (the decompile drops it); 0 for a null widget. Window_Detach and Window_ShowRecursive call it.

entries.name: Window_Detach
entries.description: Unlinks a widget from its parent's child list and clears its links. Called by two teardowns (0040ce2b, 0043c7ea) that delete what they unlink; nothing re-attaches, so no child list is reordered.

entries.name: Window_Parent
entries.description: Returns a widget's parent: walks +9 (previous sibling) while +0x11 bit 1 is clear, then returns +9 of the list head, which is the parent.

entries.name: Window_GetRoot
entries.description: Follows a widget's parent link (+9) to the top and returns that widget in EAX (the decompile drops the return).

entries.name: Window_ContainsPoint
entries.description: Window_ContainsPoint(widget, point): 1 when the point is inside the widget's absolute rect +0x15..+0x21, edges included.

entries.name: Window_ShowRecursive
entries.description: Shows a widget subtree: clears bits 2 and 4 of the +0x11 flags word, refusing to run while the effective parent is still hidden, posts type=1 (self) and type=4 (parent-directed) events, then walks the +9 chain. Type 4 is what reaches ESMessage_Paint. VSHELL_FULL.txt names this Window_HideRecursive; the two are swapped there. Mirror of Window_HideRecursive (0041f469).

entries.name: Window_HideRecursive
entries.description: Hides a widget subtree: sets bit 2 of the +0x11 flags word, which is a HIDDEN bit, sets bit 4 when the effective parent is hidden too, recurses into every child that is not already hidden (+0xd child-list head, +5 sibling-next), then posts a type=2 event via FUN_00468440. VSHELL_FULL.txt names this Window_ShowRecursive; the two are swapped there. ESMessage_Paint (0040b439) draws only when bit 2 is clear, and the repair tab's entry (004332ec) calls the other one on its own panels while its teardown (004333eb) calls this. Mirror of Window_ShowRecursive (0041f2e6).

entries.name: Window_BeginPaint
entries.description: The first call in all five widget paints: binds the drawing context to the widget and clips to it. The paints depend on that clip rather than measuring -- the titled panel's hatch is drawn over 700 pixels wide whatever the widget's size.

entries.name: Window_DispatchCallback
entries.description: Calls the widget's own handler at +0x3d if it has one. This is what a click actually reaches, and what the palette scope's on-shown hook goes through.

entries.name: ShellCursor_Ctor
entries.description: Cursor object: vtable 00471844, the HCURSOR at +4. Built twice at startup around GetCursor() into DAT_004810e8 and DAT_004810ec.
WinWin95Cursor vtable 00471844 slot 0, the class's only virtual: returns at once. WinCursor's own slot is Rtl_PureError. What calls the slot is Open.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_Ctor
entries.description: WinWin95Display constructor (vtable 004717ec at +1, RTTI 'WinWin95Display', 0x65d bytes): installs the WinDisplay vtable 00471818 and registers the display with WinBase_AddDisplay, then its own vtable; builds the 100-entry {left, top, right, bottom} rect array at +0x19 (RectI_Ctor); a root Window (0x45 bytes, vtable 004717dc) at +5 sized to the display (GLDisplay_GetAttribute 0 and 1 of DAT_0048e17c); a GLViewport at +0x15; shows the root; +9 = +0xd = 0x100; zeroes the rects and the rect count +0x659.

entries.name: DirtyList_PresentOne
entries.description: Display_PresentRect(rect, rect) and decrements the dirty count at +0x659.

entries.name: DirtyList_Flush
entries.description: Presents every dirty rectangle queued on a screen object (16-byte rects from +0x19, count at +0x659) with DirtyList_PresentOne and zeroes the count.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_BeginPaint
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot 0 (display, widget), what Window_BeginPaint calls: sets the viewport +0x15's clip rect (+0x210..+0x21c) to the widget's absolute rect (+0x15..+0x21), clip mode +0x20c and translation flag +0x208 to 1, makes the viewport current, then records the rect in the dirty list (+0x19, count +0x659): drops every listed rect strictly inside it and appends it unless a listed rect already contains it, asserting (winwin95.cpp line 99) fewer than 100.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_BeginPaintRect
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +4 (display, rect): WinWin95Display_BeginPaint for a bare rect: the viewport's clip rect is the rect and its clip mode +0x20c 1 (the translation flag is left alone), and the rect is appended to the dirty list without the containment test (assert at winwin95.cpp line 0x6d).

entries.name: WinWin95Display_GetCursor
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +8: returns the cursor Display_SetCursor caches at +0x11.

entries.name: Display_SetCursor
entries.description: Slot 3 of the shell display's vtable 004717ec: SetCursor(arg) unless it equals the one cached at display +0x11. Pointer_Enter passes a widget's +0x35, a cursor object's address rather than its handle.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_SetCursorPos
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +0x10 (display, point): ClientToScreen on the main window (DAT_00481e54), then SetCursorPos. Pointer_MoveTo calls it.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_GetCursorPos
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +0x14 (display, point): GetCursorPos, ScreenToClient on the main window (DAT_00481e54), stored to point. Display_GetCursorPos calls it.

entries.name: WinWin95Display_ShowCursor
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +0x18: ShowCursor(1).

entries.name: WinWin95Display_HideCursor
entries.description: WinWin95Display vtable 004717ec slot +0x1c: ShowCursor(0).

entries.name: Map_Ctor
entries.description: Constructor of RTTI class Map (vtable 0047195e, 0x4e bytes), the base ShellMap (004721b0) derives from: rect width/height at +0x46/+0x4a, own drawing context at +4 centred on the rect, 3Space camera at +0xc (focal shift 7 at +0x10, no rotation), position +0x12/+0x16, altitude +0x1a = 200000 (DAT_00471870), pan +0x3a/+0x3e zeroed, pan step via Map_PanStepFor.

entries.name: Map_Dtor
entries.description: Map destructor (camera, flags): decrements the live-object counter at *005ddec0, restores the Map vtable 0047195e, deletes the drawing context at +4 through its vtable +0x18 and the 3Space camera at +0xc through its slot 0 (each when set), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Dtor ends with it.

entries.name: Map_Project
entries.description: World point to canvas through the map camera: FUN_0045e2d0, FUN_0045e350 ((view << 7) / depth) and FUN_0045e424 (centre offset, y flipped) -- a plan view about the viewport centre.

entries.name: Map_PushContext
entries.description: (camera): saves the current drawing context (0048e184) at +8 and makes the camera's own context at +4 current (Gfx_SetCurrentContext); returns it. ShellMap_Paint brackets its drawing with this and Map_PopContext.

entries.name: Map_PopContext
entries.description: (camera): makes the drawing context Map_PushContext saved at +8 current again and returns it.

entries.name: ShellMap_InstallCamera
entries.description: (map): places the map's view (+0xc) at x = +0x12 + +0x3a, y = +0x16 + +0x3e and +0xc = +0x1a, installs it (Raster_InstallViewProjection) and clears the model transform (Raster_SetModelTransform(0)). ShellMap_Paint calls it.

entries.name: Map_ZoomOut
entries.description: Map vtable 0047195e slot +8: altitude +0x1a += 50000 (DAT_00471864) while the result stays at or below 1000000 (DAT_0047186c), then Map_PanStepFor. ShellMap overrides it with ShellMap_ZoomOut.

entries.name: Map_ZoomIn
entries.description: Map vtable +4: altitude -= 50000 while the result stays >= 50000, then Map_PanStepFor.

entries.name: Map_PanWest
entries.description: Map vtable 0047195e slot +0x14: pan x +0x3a -= the step +0x42 when position x +0x12 less the step stays at or above -5000000. ShellMap overrides it with ShellMap_PanWest.

entries.name: Map_PanEast
entries.description: Map vtable 0047195e slot +0x18: pan x +0x3a += the step +0x42 when position x +0x12 plus the step stays at or below 5000000. ShellMap overrides it with ShellMap_PanEast.

entries.name: Map_PanNorth
entries.description: Map vtable 0047195e slot +0xc: pan y +0x3e += the step +0x42 when position y +0x16 plus the step stays at or below 5000000 (DAT_00471860). ShellMap overrides it with ShellMap_PanNorth.

entries.name: Map_PanSouth
entries.description: Map vtable 0047195e slot +0x10: pan y +0x3e -= the step +0x42 when position y +0x16 less the step stays at or above -5000000. ShellMap overrides it with ShellMap_PanSouth.

entries.name: Map_ResetPan
entries.description: Map vtable +0x1c: zeroes the pan +0x3a/+0x3e.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA
entries.description: (positions, uvCorners, count, atlasPage, shadePtr, mode, preTransformed): VSHELL's affine textured-polygon fill, one function doing what DBSIM splits into Raster_SetupTexturedSpan and Raster_DrawPolygon. Per vertex: model-to-view unless preTransformed, project, u and v << 8, the view depth into +8 when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled is set, and in mode 2 a ramp row from shadePtr[i]; near-plane clip; Raster_ClipPolygonX, Raster_ClipPolygonY and Raster_BuildEdgeTables with flags 1 (|4 in mode 2, |8 with the depth buffer). Then per row u and v are stepped linearly across the span by the span routine the mode selects: 0 Raster_SpanTextured, 1 Raster_SpanTexturedShaded (with *shadePtr turned into one ramp row in place), 2 Raster_SpanTexturedGouraud, or their ...Clipped twins when the clip-span table DAT_0047e92c is set and the context clip mode is 2 or the depth buffer is on. TSTexture4Poly_Render dispatches between it and TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB on g_TexturedPolyPerspective.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB
entries.description: (positions, uvCorners, count, atlasPage, shadePtr, mode, preTransformed): the perspective-correct twin of TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA, and VSHELL's copy of DBSIM's Raster_DrawTexturedPolyNear. Per vertex it stores 1/z (1 << DAT_005d7fd4 over the view depth) at +0x14, u and v << 16 times 1/z, and the view depth at +8; clips and builds edges with flags 0xb (0xf in mode 2). Each row is drawn in runs of 2^k pixels: k = 10 when the row's ends have equal 1/z, else 4, 5, 6 or 7 as |delta 1/z| >> 12 is over DAT_00471980, over DAT_00471984, over DAT_00471988 or none. At each run's end u and v are recovered with Int64Pair_Q16Divide (per-run steps from Raster_ScaleRunStep) and the run is filled affinely by Raster_SpanTexturedShaded, or Raster_SpanTexturedShadedClipped under RasterizeA's conditions. With DAT_0047188c set, the row's start and its last partial run's end take Raster_BuildEdgeTables' quadratic fit instead of a divide. Every mode draws with the shaded span: mode 1 sets its ramp row from *shadePtr, and mode 2 interpolates a per-vertex row along the edges that no span reads.

entries.name: ShapeRender_BindNodeTransforms
entries.description: (shape, worldTransforms): stores worldTransforms at 004869d0, the array ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform indexes by transform id (stride 0x20); the first argument is not read. When it is not null, clears the 50 per-node composed flags at 0048a118, runs Raster_SaveState on 004869d8, marks flag 0 and clears the current id 0048a14c. TSShape_Render and TSShapeInstance_Render pass the shape's +0x18 before drawing.

entries.name: TSGroup_BindNodeTransform
entries.description: One-line forwarder: ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform(group, out, (short)*(group + 4)), +4 being the part's transform id. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's TSGroup_BindNodeTransform.

entries.name: ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform
entries.description: (part, out, transformId), assert file src\ts_part.cpp. A negative id returns to the base state: when a node is current it restores slot 0 (0045f528 on 004869d8), records that node's id in out+0x20 and clears the current id 0048a14c; with none current it sets out+0x20 to -1. The id that is already current sets out+0x20 to -1 and nothing else. Otherwise it pushes: saves the previous id in out+0x20, sets 0048a14c = id + 1 (asserting it stays under 0x32), and the first time an id is seen since the flags at 0048a118 were cleared composes the node's world transform (id * 0x20 into the array at [004869d0]) with the object-to-view transform [004869f8] into out (Transform_Concat), installs it with Raster_SetModelTransform and saves the resulting state in the 0x110-byte slot 004869d8 + id*0x110 (Raster_SaveState); a repeat restores that slot. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's ShapeNode_ComposeToViewTransform.

entries.name: TSRender_NoOp
entries.description: Empty function (a bare RET). The four shape and poly renderers that call it get no effect from the call.

entries.name: TSPartBase_FindPart
entries.description: TSPartBase vtable 0047f0f8 slot +0x20 (part, id): returns the part when its id (+6) is id, else 0. TSGroup, TSBSPGroup and TSBitmapPart inherit it; TSPartList_FindPart overrides it to search children. DBSIM's copy is 00476120.

entries.name: TSPartBase_FindPartSlot
entries.description: TSPartBase vtable 0047f0f8 slot +0x24 (part, id): returns 0; a leaf part holds no child slots. TSPartList_FindPartSlot overrides it.

entries.name: TSBounds_ScreenVisibility
entries.description: (bounds{+8 radius, +0xa/+0xc/+0xe centre int16}): Raster_ModelToView on the centre; 0 when the sphere lies wholly nearer than 005d7fd8. Otherwise projects the centre (Raster_Project, Raster_ToScreen), scales the radius to screen by a cached factor built from the view's width (Math_Atan2Bam, 004509c4, FixedMulQ10), and tests a box of that half-size plus 3 around the screen centre against the drawing context's rect +0x210..+0x21c: 0 when they do not overlap, 2 when the box is wholly inside when the clip mode +0x208 is 1, else 1. TSShape_Render and TSShapeInstance_Render call it.

entries.name: TSBitmapPart_Render
entries.description: Contains the 'TSBase::getBitmapPtr() : index out of range' assert. Reads poly+0x10 (the part's bitmap tag) as a frame index, bounds-checks against g_ActiveBitmapArray's count, looks up g_ActiveBitmapArray.Frames[frameIndex], and if non-null draws a textured quad using poly+0x12/+0x13 (the x and y offset bytes) for placement. This is the bitmap-tag-to-bitmap resolution path. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSPartList_Ctor
entries.description: TSPartList constructor (vtable 00471ab8, RTTI 'TSPartList', 0x16 bytes): stamps ClassItem, TSBase, TSPartBase and its own vtable in turn, counting each level at *005ddec0, and clears the child count +0x10 and the child array +0x12. TSPartList_Construct, TSCellAnimPart_Construct, TSShape_Ctor, TSDetailPart_Ctor and TSBSPPart_Ctor run it. DBSIM's is TSPartList_Ctor (00476604).

entries.name: TSPartList_Dtor
entries.description: TSPartList vtable 00471ab8 slot +0x18 (list, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, deletes each child of the array +0x12 (count +0x10) through its vtable +0x18 with 3, frees the array, decrements once more for TSPartBase, TSBase_Dtor(list, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The derived parts' destructors chain to it.

entries.name: TSPartList_Render
entries.description: TSPartList vtable 00471ab8 slot +0x1c (list): TSGroup_BindNodeTransform into a local, then each child of the array +0x12 (count +0x10) in order through its own vtable +0x1c, then TSRender_NoOp.
