TSShape inherits it, and TSShape_Render and TSShapeInstance_Render call it with g_ActiveBitmapArray bound to the shape's DBA.

entries.name: TSPartList_FindPart
entries.description: TSPartList vtable 00471ab8 slot +0x20 (list, id): returns the list itself when its id (+6) is id; otherwise asks each child of the array +0x12 (count +0x10) through its own slot +0x20, in order, and returns the first non-null answer. TSShape, TSDetailPart, TSBSPPart, TSCellAnimPart and ANShape inherit it. Identical after normalisation to DBSIM 00476744.

entries.name: TSPartList_FindPartSlot
entries.description: TSPartList vtable 00471ab8 slot +0x24 (list, id): returns the address of the entry of the child array +0x12 (count +0x10) whose part's id (+6) is id; when no direct child matches, asks each child through its own slot +0x24 and returns the first non-null answer. The address of the slot, not the part, is what lets a caller replace the part; see docs/formats/mech-shape-drawing.md. DBSIM's copy is 00476784.

entries.name: TSCellAnimPart_Render
entries.description: TSCellAnimPart vtable 0047f12c slot +0x1c: TSGroup_BindNodeTransform into a local, then renders child [frame % count] through its vtable +0x1c, frame being the entry for its sequence +0x16 in the cell-frame array ShapeRender_BindCellFrames bound at 004869d4; then TSRender_NoOp. DBSIM's is TSCellAnimPart_Render (004767e4).

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Ctor
entries.description: TSDetailPart constructor (vtable 00471a84, RTTI 'TSDetailPart', 0x1a bytes): TSPartList_Ctor, its own vtable, and clears the size list +0x16. TSDetailPart_Construct runs it.

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Dtor
entries.description: TSDetailPart vtable 00471a84 slot +0x18 (part, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the size list +0x16, TSPartList_Dtor(part, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSDetailPart_Render
entries.description: TSDetailPart vtable 00471a84 slot +0x1c, the LOD selection: size = (radius +8 << the focal shift 005d7fd4) / max(Math_FastMagnitude3D(eye) - radius, 1), at least 1; t = FixedMulQ10(004719c8, size); i starts at the bias 004719cc and advances while the threshold [i] of +0x16 is below t and i is below the last; renders child [min(i - bias, count - 1)] through its vtable +0x1c, then TSRender_NoOp. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's TSDetailPart_Render (004768bc); 004719c8 is 1024 (Q10 one) and 004719cc 0 in the image, as DBSIM's g_TSDetailPartSizeScaleQ10 and g_TSDetailPartBias are.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 004221e7; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 004221e7 DBSIM 004768bc

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Ctor
entries.description: TSBSPPart constructor (vtable 00471a50, RTTI 'TSBSPPart', 0x20 bytes): TSPartList_Ctor, its own vtable, and clears the node count +0x16, the nodes +0x18 and the per-node transform ids +0x1c. TSBSPPart_Construct runs it.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Dtor
entries.description: TSBSPPart vtable 00471a50 slot +0x18 (part, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees +0x18 and +0x1c, TSPartList_Dtor(part, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSBSPPart_RenderNode
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's TSBSPPart_RenderNode (00476a1c): (part, node) walks the part's BSP tree back to front from one node, testing the eye against the node plane (through the node's transform when its id at +0x1c is not -1) and drawing children through their vtable +0x1c. It has a block DBSIM's lacks, ahead of the walk: while the byte 0047e9a4 is set it composes the node's view transform and draws the node's plane as a gizmo, three lines in colour 0x77 and one in 0x7f, through Gfx_DrawLine. 0047e9a4 is 0 in the image, and es2_xref.py finds this read as its only absolute reference (Open).

entries.name: TSBSPPart_Render
entries.description: TSBSPPart vtable 00471a50 slot +0x1c: TSGroup_BindNodeTransform into a local, copies the eye position (g_EyeInModelSpace, 005d7fcc, 005d7fd0) to 0048a150..0048a158, TSBSPPart_RenderNode(part, 0), then TSRender_NoOp. Matches DBSIM's 00476b0c.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 0042286d; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 0042286d DBSIM 00476b0c

entries.name: TSNullObj_Render
entries.description: TSNullObj slot +0x1c: does nothing.

entries.name: TSPoly_Render
entries.description: TSPoly vtable 0047ee90 slot +0x1c: does nothing. The derived polys override it (TSSolidPoly_Render and its siblings).

entries.name: TSSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real vtable-slot-0x1c render method (see g_TSSolidPolyVtable). Resolves the surface record via (surfaceField*4 + g_ActiveSurfaceRecords) -- the same *4 stride as TSTexture4Poly_Render, consistent with the poly's surface field holding surfaceIndex*4. Runs TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest against poly+4/+6 (normal/centre point indices, each *6 into the three-short point array) to pick front (piVar3[0]/[1] = Front/FrontLine) or back (piVar3[2]/[3] = Back/BackLine) color pair -- confirms the surface entry's 4-slot Front/FrontLine/Back/BackLine layout applies to flat polys too, not just textured ones. Skips drawing if both resolved color dwords have top byte 0x18-shift == 0x14 (looks like an uninitialized/sentinel guard, not chased further). Otherwise projects and clips via Poly_ProjectShapeVertices/FUN_0045ec54 and fills via PolyFill_FillThenOutline -- the chain TSTexture4Poly_Render's g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush branch also uses, there with a bitmap brush installed in place of the default colour brush. No dithering/lighting-ramp math visible anywhere in this chain -- VSHELL (a shell/viewer app) passes the front/back colours straight through to the fill routines, unlike DBSIM's in-mission renderer.

entries.name: TSTexture4Poly_Render
entries.description: TSTexture4Poly's vtable-slot-0x1c render method (see g_TSTexture4PolyVtable). Reads poly+0xc (the surface field) as MOVZX (unsigned short), SHL 2 (x4) to a byte offset into g_ActiveSurfaceRecords (DAT_005d88a2), then reads front=*(int32*)(base+offset) and back=*(int32*)(base+offset+8), i.e. two int32 slots on -- read from ES2DumpAsm raw disassembly, not just the decompiler. A TSGroup's on-disk surface count is stored as surfaceCount*4 and each surface entry is four slots (Front, FrontLine, Back, BackLine), so the surface field holds surfaceIndex*4: the front value is surface[field/4].Front and the back value surface[field/4].Back. Front/back is chosen by TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest against poly+4/+6; when the ramp row count DAT_0047e9ac is non-zero the face's shade comes from Light_ComputeShadeForFace, with the normal negated for a back face. g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush (00471890) chooses between two textured fills: this descriptor-and-rasterizer path (flag == 0) and a 2D bitmap-brush fill of the frame's bitmap (flag != 0; see the flag's entry). Only the flag == 0 path reaches TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA/B. In that path the resolved frame index indexes the 20-byte-stride per-frame descriptor table at g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] (a pointer distinct from the DBA object itself): int32 fields F0..F3 (bytes 0-15) and F4 at byte 16, passed to the rasterizer as param_4 (a pixel-data handle). The quad's UV corners are [V0=(F0,F1), V1=(F2,F1), V2=(F2,F3), V3=(F0,F3)] (decompiled assignment sequence _DAT_0048a190.._0048a1ac = F0,F1,F2,F1,F2,F3,F0,F3): an axis-aligned rect, top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, with F0/F1 the frame's texture-space left/top and F2/F3 its right/bottom. The function that builds that descriptor table, which decides whether F0/F1 can be nonzero, is open. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: TSShadedPoly_Render
entries.description: TSShadedPoly vtable 0047ede0 slot +0x1c: TSSolidPoly_Render's front/back surface-pair selection (g_ActiveSurfaceRecords + colour*4, TSPoly_FrontBackVisibilityTest on the normal +4 and centre +6) and its skip when both colours carry 0x14 in the top byte; then shade = Light_ComputeShadeForFace(normal, centre), the normal negated for a back face, and the shade's low byte ORed into bits 16-23 of both the fill (005d8004) and line (005d7ffc) colour words; then projects the +8 vertices from list +0xa (Poly_ProjectShapeVertices), clips to the near plane when that returns 1, and PolyFill_FillThenOutline(backFacing). DBSIM's TSShadedPoly_Render (0047542c) differs at the shade step: it resolves the final palette bytes itself through Palette_ShadeRampLookup and Raster_ShadeRampRow(0x80) instead of packing the shade into the words.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00423024; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00423024 DBSIM 0047542c

entries.name: TSGouraudPoly_Render
entries.description: TSGouraudPoly vtable 0047edb4 slot +0x1c: the surface-pair selection and skip of TSSolidPoly_Render, then one shade per vertex: Light_ComputeShadeForFace(the vertex's normal from the list +0xe, the vertex from the list +0xa), the normal negated for a back face, low byte into a local array; then projects the +8 vertices. When the projection reports 1 (a near-plane crossing) 0045f0d4 builds the clipped ring's shade array from it and the fill uses that one; either way 005d8000 = 1, the shade array goes to 005d800c and PolyFill_FillThenOutline(backFacing) draws. Matches DBSIM's 004755c8.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00423193; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00423193 DBSIM 004755c8

entries.name: TSGroup_Ctor
entries.description: TSGroup constructor (vtable 00471bf4, RTTI 'TSGroup', 0x28 bytes): stamps ClassItem, TSBase, TSPartBase and its own vtable, counting each level at *005ddec0, and clears the index list +0x10, the point list +0x14, the colour list +0x18 and the item list +0x1c. TSGroup_Construct and TSBSPGroup_Ctor run it.

entries.name: TSGroup_Dtor
entries.description: TSGroup vtable 00471bf4 slot +0x18 (group, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the index, point and colour lists, deletes each item of +0x1c (count +0x26) through its vtable +0x18 with 3, frees that list, decrements for TSPartBase, TSBase_Dtor(group, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSGroup_RenderPolys
entries.description: TSGroup's render method: slot +0x1c of the vtable at 00471bf4, whose RTTI names TSGroup (0x28 bytes). Calls TSGroup_BindNodeTransform into a local transform, saves the render context's (0048e184) +0x228, +0x22c and +0x20c, installs the default brushes 005d7ff8 and 005d8000 at +0x228 and +0x22c and clears +0x20c. Publishes the group's colour list (+0x18) as g_ActiveSurfaceRecords, its points (+0x14, three int16 each) at 005d8894 and its indexes (+0x10, or 005d8014 when null) at 005d889e. Copies the point count +0x22 to 005d889c, asserts it is at most 1000 (severity 4, ts_base.h line 0x2e7) and zeroes that many bytes of the per-point scratch at 005d88a6. Then draws the +0x26 items of the +0x1c pointer array in order, each through its own vtable slot +0x1c, restores the three context fields and calls TSRender_NoOp. TSBSPGroup_Render is the TSBSPGroup counterpart, drawing the polys in BSP order instead. Field names from TSGroup_DebugPrint; see docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 00423497; tools/scripts/es2_naming.py rtti VSHELL 00471bf4; VSHELL_vtables_full.txt

entries.name: TSBSPGroup_Ctor
entries.description: TSBSPGroup constructor (vtable 00471bc0, RTTI 'TSBSPGroup', 0x2e bytes): TSGroup_Ctor, its own vtable, and clears the node count +0x28 and node array +0x2a. TSBSPGroup_Construct runs it.

entries.name: TSBSPGroup_Dtor
entries.description: TSBSPGroup vtable 00471bc0 slot +0x18 (group, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the nodes +0x2a, TSGroup_Dtor(group, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: TSBSPGroup_RenderNode
entries.description: (group, node): draws a TSBSPGroup's polys by its BSP tree from one node. Nodes are 10 bytes at group+0x2a: int32 plane constant, uint16 poly index (into the polys at +0x1c), and two int16 children at +6 and +8. The plane is the node poly's own stored normal (poly+4, a point index into +0x14): d = dot(normal, g_EyeInModelSpace) - constant. For d < 0 it draws the +6 child, then the node's poly, then the +8 child; otherwise the +8 child first. A child below zero is nothing, one with bit 0x4000 the poly [value & 0x3fff], and anything else a node to recurse into; polys draw through their vtable slot +0x1c. TSBSPGroup_Render starts it at node 0.

entries.name: TSBSPGroup_Render
entries.description: TSBSPGroup's render method: slot +0x1c of the vtable at 00471bc0, whose RTTI names TSBSPGroup (0x2e bytes). Sets up like TSGroup's render: TSGroup_BindNodeTransform, the default brushes 005d7ff8 and 005d8000 installed at the context's +0x228 and +0x22c with +0x20c cleared, the group's surfaces (+0x18), points (+0x14) and indexes (+0x10, defaulted when null), and a zeroed scratch of +0x22 bytes, asserting that count is at most 1000. Then draws the polys by the group's BSP tree through TSBSPGroup_RenderNode from node 0 rather than in order, and restores the three context fields. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00423709; tools/scripts/es2_naming.py rtti VSHELL 00471bc0; VSHELL_vtables_full.txt

entries.name: TSAliasSolidPoly_Render
entries.description: TSAliasSolidPoly vtable 0047ed88 slot +0x1c: the surface-pair selection, skip, projection and near-plane clip of the solid poly, then 005d8000 = 0 and the fill 0045f448(backFacing) where the non-alias polys call PolyFill_FillThenOutline. Matches DBSIM's 00475bc4.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00423816; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00423816 DBSIM 00475bc4

entries.name: TSAliasShadedPoly_Render
entries.description: TSAliasShadedPoly vtable 0047ed5c slot +0x1c: TSShadedPoly_Render with the fill 0045f448 in place of PolyFill_FillThenOutline, the shade packed into bits 16-23 of both colour words. Matches DBSIM's 00475c80, which packs the shade the same way.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 004238d9; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 004238d9 DBSIM 00475c80

entries.name: TSAliasGouraudPoly_Render
entries.description: TSAliasGouraudPoly vtable 0047ed30 slot +0x1c: TSGouraudPoly_Render with the fill 0045f448 in place of PolyFill_FillThenOutline. Matches DBSIM's 00475de0.

entries.name: Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper
entries.description: Identical in shape to Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper but for .DBA bitmap-array resources (e.g. "dba\mis_icon.dba"). Confirms both file kinds funnel into the same generic VshellClassItem_LoadItem loader.

entries.name: Vshell_PanelLoadWrapper
entries.description: (path): opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserting (src\shellmap.cpp line 0x5f) that it opened, loads one class item from it with VshellClassItem_LoadItem(stream, 0), asserting (line 0x62) that one loaded, destroys the stream and returns the item. Any class item: ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded loads dfn\map.dfn, a GLFont, with it. Vshell_DbaLoadWrapper is its sibling for .DBA files.

entries.name: ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. Lazy-loads mis_icon.dba, mapshp.dba, and map.dfn into globals (guarded by null-checks), asserts on failure, sets a screen-state byte to 0. Confirmed via direct string references to the three literal filenames.

entries.name: ShellMap_ReleaseResources
entries.description: shellmap.cpp teardown counterpart to ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded -- destroys the 3 loaded resources (calls each object's vtable+0x18 destructor) and nulls the globals. Confirmed the only other reference to ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr in VSHELL.EXE besides the loader -- the loaded DFN panel object's contents are never read, only destroyed.

entries.name: ShellMap_Constructor
entries.description: ShellMap::ctor (vtable &PTR_FUN_004721b0). Opens data\mission.str and data\maplabel.str as independent string tables, then calls ShellMap_LoadScriptDat. Confirmed via assert string. The object is the briefing's map; see docs/shell/mission-map.md.

entries.name: ShellMap_Dtor
entries.description: (map, flags): ShellMap's destructor (vtable 004721b0, RTTI ShellMap, 0x3c5 bytes): restamps the vtable, passes the object at +0x4e to 0045dbf0 and then runs its virtual destructor, frees the arrays at +0x52, +0x56, +0x5e, +0x62, +0x6e and the +0x72 six-byte records' buffers at +0x5a and the array itself, deletes +0x66, runs 00427ea4 on +0x219 and +0x1b7 and Map_Dtor, and Mem_Delete's the map when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Build destroys the previous map with it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042424a; tools/scripts/es2_naming.py rtti VSHELL 004721b0

entries.name: ShellMap_LoadScriptDat
entries.description: shellmap.cpp. The briefing map's reader for data\script.dat -- a SECOND, independent reader of the same 13-block structure WriteScriptDatFile (0041ac54, VSHELL) writes and DBSim_LoadScriptDat (00424308, DBSIM) also reads. Confirmed byte-for-byte identical block order/strides to both, differing only in which fields it keeps vs seeks past (e.g. keeps row12/row14/row15 blocks in full for UI display, where DBSIM keeps only 1 field or discards entirely). Not an independent or map-rendering-only format. See docs/formats/script-dat.md.

entries.name: ShellMap_LoadZone
entries.description: Loads dat\zone%d.dat (keeps int32[2] cell shift at +0x104, int32[3] height scale) and dba\zone%d.dba through HeightGrid_Load into the map's HeightGrid (DAT_00472258).

entries.name: ShellMap_ReadSquadHeader
entries.description: shellmap.cpp (source line 0x1f5). The only VSHELL function found that parses data\player.mec (Career_SaveSlot and Career_LoadSlot copy it whole); it takes just the two leading int16 -- the player entry index and the squad size -- before closing it and opening data\mforms.dat for formation layout. No VSHELL reader of the rest of player.mec, including the trailing weapon-unlock table, was found by a literal-reference sweep.

entries.name: ShellMap_FitBounds
entries.description: Full view: centre of the widened block-1 bounds and the altitude fitting both halves in the viewport; also the altitude limit +0x3bd.

entries.name: ShellMap_FitSquad
entries.description: Squad view +0x193/+0x197/+0x19b: the same fit over the squad's positions widened by 250000.

entries.name: ShellMap_SkipIntro
entries.description: Moves the intro state +0x172 to 0x11 (the closing zoom) when it is below 0x12.

entries.name: ShellMap_Paint
entries.description: Map vtable slot 0: camera clamp, then clear, relief, grid and bounds, path, bases, nav markers, squad.

entries.name: ShellMap_Clear
entries.description: Fills the viewport with 0x10; busy-waits 10 ticks during the intro's first paint.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintRelief
entries.description: Stretches the relief bitmap (+0x3c1) over the bounds widened by 100000 through GLBitmap_DrawStretched.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintGrid
entries.description: Grid lines in 0x0f every 200000 through the projected origin; outside the first paint, the bounds outlined in colour 10 (Gfx_FillRect mode 4).

entries.name: ShellMap_IntroStep
entries.description: The intro state machine (+0x172, 20 states): hold, zoom to the squad, reveal the squad, pan along the nav path, zoom back. Timer is GetTickCount()>>4.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintPath
entries.description: Nav path in 0x0e; part-way through the intro only the line to the camera centre and a radius-3 pen.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintBases
entries.description: Bases shown by +0x1a (friendly non-zero, hostile == 1), mis_icon frame by type.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintIcon
entries.description: Icon at a world point: projected size below a threshold plots a pixel, below the frame height a scaled blit, else the frame.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintNavMarkers
entries.description: mis_icon frames 14+ at path points after the first, up to nine.

entries.name: ShellMap_PaintSquad
entries.description: Squad icons, frame 3 for block-7 record 0 else 5, as many as the intro has revealed.

entries.name: ShellMap_CurrentLine
entries.description: Picks the mission.str line the intro has reached into +0x17e; the rest of its body is empty branches, so it draws nothing.

entries.name: ShellMap_BuildRelief
entries.description: Banded relief of the cells under the widened bounds: min(h,0x7f)/5 + 0xd1, two Gfx_BandedTriangle per cell, min(640/cols, 400/rows) pixels a cell.

entries.name: ShellMap_ClampCamera
entries.description: Caps the altitude at +0x3bd and keeps the centre half a viewport inside the bounds widened by 100000.

entries.name: ShellMap_ZoomOut
entries.description: Map vtable +8: altitude += 50000 when the clamp leaves it; then ShellMap_PanStepFor.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanWest
entries.description: Map vtable +0x14: pan x -= step when the clamp leaves the moved centre alone.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanEast
entries.description: Map vtable +0x18: pan x += step, same test.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanNorth
entries.description: Map vtable +0xc: pan y += step, same test.

entries.name: ShellMap_PanSouth
entries.description: Map vtable +0x10: pan y -= step, same test.

entries.name: TSLight_Dtor
entries.description: TSLight vtable 00472188 slot 0, the destructor (light, flags): decrements *005ddec0, destroys the member at +0x1e with TSContext_Dtor(+0x1e, 2) and the light itself with TSContext_Dtor(light, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: TSSunLight_Dtor
entries.description: TSSunLight vtable 0047219c slot 0 (light, flags): when light is set, decrements *005ddec0 twice (its own level and TSLight's), destroys the TSContext member at +0x1e with TSContext_Dtor(+0x1e, 2) and the light with TSContext_Dtor(light, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_Constructor builds the map's sun as one, with +0x16 = 1.

entries.name: StringTable_Ctor
entries.description: Clears a string table: buffer +0, cursor +4, length +8 and the group counters +0xc and +0xe. ShellMap_Constructor builds its table with it.

entries.name: StringTable_Load
entries.description: (table, path), assert file src\strings.cpp: opens path with VolRStream_CtorFromPath, asserts it opened, reads it with StringTable_LoadFromStream, destroys the stream and returns that result. String-table reader: +0 content buffer, +4 cursor, +8 content length, +0xc int16 strings in the current group, +0xe int16 index within it. Layout of the file in docs/formats/str-strings.md.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadFromStream
entries.description: (table, stream): reads the int32 content length into +8, allocates that many bytes (Mem_NewArray, asserting in src\strings.cpp on failure) at +0, reads the content into it and sets the cursor +4 to the start. Returns 1.

entries.name: StringTable_Free
entries.description: Frees a string table's buffer (Mem_DeleteArray) and zeroes the buffer, cursor, length and group counters.

entries.name: StringTable_PeekGroupCount
entries.description: Returns the byte at the cursor, the low byte of the next group's int16 count, sign-extended; 0 when nothing is loaded.

entries.name: StringTable_ReadNext
entries.description: (table, &text, &attributes): reads the next string. At the start of a group it takes the int16 count first. Stores a pointer to the text (after its int16 length) and, when attributes is non-null, to the attribute bytes after the count byte, then advances past both. At the end of a group it resets the group counters and returns 0; also 0 past the end of the content.

entries.name: StringTable_LoadGroup
entries.description: (table, texts, capacity, attributes): reads the next group's count, asserts in src\strings.cpp when capacity is positive but smaller than it, and fills texts[i] (and attributes[i] when that array is given) with StringTable_ReadNext, asserting on a short group. Resets the group counter and returns the count. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's StringTable_LoadGroup.

entries.name: Driver3_Slot8ReturnsZero
entries.description: Slot 8 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600): returns 0, so RasterDriver_OpenDisplay's slot-8 check of the bitmap header always passes. DBSIM's slot 8 is the same (0048a0c0).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004281f4; table dump at 0047e600

entries.name: Driver3_OpenDisplay
entries.description: Slot 11 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600), which RasterDriver_OpenDisplay calls with (bitmapHeader, info): keeps the header at 00481834, allocates a row-offset table (base, then one offset per row) into info+0 (freeing the previous one, 0046d73c), takes the width and height from GLDisplay_OpenWithSize's one-shot overrides (0046d734, 0046d738, reset to -1) or else from the header, fills the rest of info (+0x24/+0x28 the header's own size, 8 bits, 256 colours) and sets the screen rect and origin globals. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0048a0c8.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004281fb; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a0c8

entries.name: Driver3_Slot7NoOp
entries.description: Slot 7 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600): returns at once. RasterDriver_OpenDisplay and GLDisplay_SetAttribute call slot 7. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Driver3_Slot7NoOp (0048a218).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042837a; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a218

entries.name: Driver3_CloseDisplay
entries.description: Slot 12 of raster driver 3's routine table (0047e600), which RasterDriver_CloseDisplay calls: (info) frees the row-offset table at info+0 that Driver3_OpenDisplay allocated. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Driver3_CloseDisplay (0048a220).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042837f; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0048a220

entries.name: GLDisplay_OpenWithSize
entries.description: (display, bitmapHeader, width, height): stores width at 0046d734 and height at 0046d738 when not negative, GLDisplay_Open, then on success selects the display as the render target, sets its attributes +0x88 = 0 and +0x8c = 1 (publishing them when it is the current target), and sets its page offsets (0, 200, 400, 600 for kind 'VGA 8', zero otherwise). Driver 3's open routine (004281fb) takes the stored width and height once, in place of the header's, then resets them to -1. Display_Init and ShellMap_BuildRelief call it.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Ctor
entries.description: HeightGrid constructor (vtable 00472470 after the ClassItem 0047f834 and TSBase 0047f858 base vtables; RTTI name 'HeightGrid', 0x125 bytes): Rtl_VectorNew of 0x14 8-byte elements at +0x28, 00467ee4(+0xd0, 0x100) for the height offset table, zeroes +0xf0/+0xf4/+0xf8 and sets +0x104 = 10, +0x108 = 8. ShellMap_LoadZone calls it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042870b; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: HeightGrid_Dtor
entries.description: HeightGrid vtable 00472470 slot +0x18 (grid, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the array at +0xec when set, decrements once more and runs TSBase_Dtor on the height offset table at +0xd0 (the VectorTable HeightGrid_Ctor builds there), then TSBase_Dtor(grid, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: HeightGrid_FromBitmap
entries.description: hgrid.cpp: the shell's copy of the zone loader's bitmap path -- one height byte per pixel, rows north to south, material rolls.

entries.name: HeightGrid_Load
entries.description: hgrid.cpp: loads data\mat0.dat, then a .dba through HeightGrid_FromBitmap or any other extension as the ASCII debug format.

entries.name: HGrid_RenderAround
entries.description: (grid, position): hgrid.cpp's cell renderer, while grid +0x118 is set. Clears the model transform, installs a mode-0 brush at the context's +0x22c for the walk, takes the cell of position (+4, +8, shifted down by grid +0x104) and its byte +0x17, and walks the polygon at grid +0xc8 around it with CellWalk_Polygon, callback 00429dac. When that byte was set it calls 0042afd7(grid, cellX, cellY) after the walk. Restores the brush. See docs/polygon-fill.md.

entries.name: Sfx_Init
entries.description: (sfx, cacheLimit, fileCount, sampleCount): stores the cache limit at +0x18 (the bytes Sfx_Cache may hold, 0 for none) and the counts at +0x10 and +0x14, allocates the 0x21c-byte file table (+0x34) and the 0x28-byte sample table (+0x38) with every slot's +0 at -1, then opens the drivers through 0042d7f0(+0x44, the format at +0x24). Returns 1; 0 with SetLastError(14) when an allocation fails (both tables freed) or SetLastError(0x3eb) when 0042d7f0 does. ShellSound_Init calls it with sampleCount = fileCount + 10.

entries.name: Sfx_Construct
entries.description: (sfx): clears the file and sample tables (+0x34, +0x38), the voice counts (+0x3c, +0x40) and the bytes cached (+0x1c), sets defaults, and reads [Sound] from data\sound.cfg: Driver (read, then +0x2a set to 1 regardless), Buffers into +0x30 (1-64, else 5), Rate 11 giving +0x24 = 0x10 and anything else 0x20, and Width 'Mono' giving +0x28 = 4 and anything else 8. Increments the count at *005ddec0. ShellSound_Init constructs the shell's SFX with it before Sfx_Init.

entries.name: ShellSoundManager_Dtor
entries.description: (manager, flags): Sos_Shutdown (which ends with Sos_UnbindLibrary), Mem_Delete on the arrays at +0x34 and +0x38 (clearing both), then Mem_Delete(manager) when flags bit 0 is set. ShellSound_Shutdown runs it on ShellSound_Manager with 3. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SfxManager_Dtor.

entries.name: ShellSound_ReleaseDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver. ShellSound_Stop calls it between its two Mono_Printf marks.

entries.name: ShellSound_AcquireDriver
entries.description: Returns Sos_AcquireDigiDriver's answer. ShellSound_Start calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Open
entries.description: SFX::open (asserts 'SFX::open: Can not allocate a ...' in inc\sfx_fix.h, with SetLastError(14)): (sfx, name, mode, a, b). Takes a free 0x28-byte handle slot from the table at +0x38 (count +0x14), numbering it (serial +0x20 << 16) | index, and fills its defaults (flags +8 = 0, +0xc = 5, +0x14 = 100, +0x18 = 1, +0x1c = 0x8000, +0x20 = 0x10000); its +4 takes the data entry's handle. Reuses a loaded 0x21c-byte data entry with the same name from the table at +0x34 (count +0x10), bumping its reference count at +0x208, or takes a free one and fills it: +4 the name, +0x204 a, +0x208 reference count 1, +0x20c loaded 0, +0x210 b (the size Sfx_Cache uses when non-zero), +0x214 the backend object, null. Mode 0 sets flag 1 at +8, and mode 2 sets 0x1000 there for a new data entry only. Returns the handle, or -1 when either table is full. ShellSound_Init calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Cache
entries.description: SFX::cache (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, sampleHandle, load). Asserts the handle and its file handle are valid and current. A sample flagged 0x1000 returns 1 at once. Otherwise brings its file's loaded state (+0x20c) to load: unloading (only while the file's reference count +0x208 is below 2, else SetLastError(0x20)) frees it through 0042d906 and takes its size (+0x210) off the bytes cached (+0x1c); loading opens the file as a VolRStream (assert 'Unable to open file' otherwise), takes its size once (assert 'Bogus file size' for 0), makes room through 0042ce58 when the cache limit (+0x18) would be exceeded, and loads it through 0042d906. Returns the resulting loaded state. Sfx_Play calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_Play
entries.description: SFX::play (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle). Asserts on an invalid (-1) or stale handle, and on a sample whose file index is invalid or stale. Sample slots are 0x28 bytes at sfx+0x38 (the handle's low 16 bits index them; +4 the file index, +8 flags), sound files 0x21c bytes at sfx+0x34 (+4 the file name, +0x20c loaded). Loads the file when needed (Sfx_Cache), starts it (Sfx_StartVoice), counts it as a playing song (+0x40; flag bit 0, Sfx_StartVoice's MIDI path) or sample (+0x3c), sets the playing bit 0x100 and returns 1; returns 0 when loading or starting fails.

entries.name: Sfx_Service
entries.description: Sos_Service(0, 0, 0, 0): the library service call with no window message. 00404895 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sfx_Service (0046415c).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042cce0; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0046415c

entries.name: Sfx_EvictForSpace
entries.description: (sfx, bytesNeeded): frees cached sound files until bytesNeeded are released. Scores each loaded file reference count * 10 + 1, plus for each of its sample slots the slot's +0xc, 1000 when it is playing (0x100) and 10000 more when it is also flagged 0x80; a file with a 0x1000 sample scores 0 and is never evicted. Then repeatedly takes the lowest non-zero score, stops every sample of the file through 0042ca95 when the score is 1000 or more, frees it through Sos_LoadOrFreeSample and takes its size off the bytes cached (+0x1c). The free's MIDI flag comes from the last sample slot the scoring pass visited, not from the evicted file. Returns whether enough was freed. Sfx_Cache calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_SetVolume
entries.description: SFX::setVolume (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, volume). Asserts 'Can not setVolume an invalid handle' for handle -1 and 'Sample handle is old and no longer valid' when the handle does not match the one stored in its slot (the low 16 bits index 0x28-byte slots at sfx+0x38). Stores the volume at slot +0x14 and applies it now (Sos_ApplyVolume) when the slot is playing (+9 bit 0).

entries.name: Sfx_SetLooping
entries.description: SFX::setLooping (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx, handle, loops). Validates the handle like Sfx_Play, clears flag 0x80 for a count of 1 and sets it otherwise, stores the count at slot +0x18 and applies it now (0042dc6e) when the slot is playing.

entries.name: Sfx_PlayMusicTrack
entries.description: SFX-level thunk to Music_PlayTrack (0042dcef), the copy of DBSIM's. No reference found by es2_xref.

entries.name: Sfx_StopAll
entries.description: SFX::stopAll (assert file .\inc\sfx_fix.h): (sfx). For each sample slot with the playing bit 0x100, asserts its file handle is valid and current, stops it through 0042da8c and, when that succeeds, decrements the playing-song (+0x40, flag bit 0) or playing-sample (+0x3c) count and clears the playing bit. The loop runs over the first +0x10 slots of the sample table, +0x10 being the file count. ShellSound_Stop calls it.

entries.name: Str_FormatToStatic
entries.description: (format, ...): vsprintf into the static buffer 0048a840 and returns it. Sfx_Cache formats its assert messages with it.

entries.name: Sos_InitBackend
entries.description: (window, format): the VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sos_InitBackend: keeps window at 0048a940, Sos_BindLibrary, copies the format words (from the SFX's +0x24) into 00473174-0047317c, and opens the drivers through 0042df68 with the configured driver id, then with id 1, unbinding the library when both fail. Returns true on success. Sfx_Init calls it.

entries.name: Sos_Shutdown
entries.description: Sos_ShutdownDrivers, then Sos_UnbindLibrary. ShellSoundManager_Dtor's first call. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_Shutdown.

entries.name: Sos_AcquireDigiDriver
entries.description: Returns whether Sos_AcquireDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle()) returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_AcquireDigiDriver.

entries.name: Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver
entries.description: Sos_ReleaseDriver(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), 0x1000). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ReleaseDigiDriver.

entries.name: Sos_Service
entries.description: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): Sos_UserService(Sos_GetDriverHandle()), then Sos_HandleWindowMessage with the message when hwnd is non-null. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_Service (004736cc).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042d8b9; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 004736cc

entries.name: Sos_LoadOrFreeSample
entries.description: (file + 4, unused, load, isMidiSong): the VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sos_LoadOrFreeSample: loads (0042e47d digital, 0042e76c MIDI) or frees (0042e625, 0042e816) the file's backend object at file +0x214, nulling it on a free. Returns true on success. Sfx_Cache and Sfx_EvictForSpace call it.

entries.name: Sfx_StartVoice
entries.description: (file + 4, sample + 4): starts a cached sample. Flag bit 0 (sample +8) is a MIDI song: Sos_MidiInitSong on the file's loaded object (file +0x214), then Sos_MidiStartSong, uninitialising it on failure. Flag 0x1000 goes to 0042e846. Otherwise a digital sample: both channels' volume = volume (+0x14) * Sos_MasterVolume * 0x7fff / 10000, the loop count (+0x18) less 1 (-1, forever, for 0), and two further fields copied into the SOS sample header, then Sos_StartSample on Sos_GetDriverHandle() with the voice handle out at sample +0x24. Returns true on success. Sfx_Play calls it.

entries.name: Sfx_StopVoice
entries.description: (file + 4, sample + 4): stops a playing sample by its flags (sample +8): bit 0, a MIDI song, Sos_MidiStopSong and Sos_MidiUnInitSong; 0x1000, a stream, 0042eb13; otherwise Sos_StopSample on Sos_GetDriverHandle(). The voice handle is sample +0x24. Returns 1. Sfx_StopAll calls it.

entries.name: Sos_VoiceIsDone
entries.description: (voice): Sos_MidiSongDone(+0x20) for a MIDI song (flags +4 bit 0), otherwise Sos_SampleDone(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20). 0042cc1e asks it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_VoiceIsDone (00473950).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042db36; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00473950

entries.name: Sos_SetMasterVolume
entries.description: (voice): writes Sos_MasterVolume from the record's +0x10. es2_xref.py finds no branch, stored pointer or vtable slot referencing it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_SetMasterVolume.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVolume
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear) Sos_SetSampleVolume(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20, v) with v = +0x10 * Sos_MasterVolume * 0x7fff / 10000 in both 16-bit halves; for a MIDI song Sos_MidiSetMasterVolume(+0x10 * 0x7f / 100). Sfx_SetVolume calls it for a live voice. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ApplyVolume.

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVoicePitch
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear), Sos_SetSampleRate(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20, (+0x1c * 11025) >> 16); nothing for a MIDI song. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ApplyVoicePitch (00473a48).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042dc1e; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00473a48

entries.name: Sos_ApplyVoicePan
entries.description: (voice): for a digital sample (flags +4 bit 0 clear), Sos_SetPanLocation(Sos_GetDriverHandle(), +0x20, +0x18); nothing for a MIDI song. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ApplyVoicePan (00473a74).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042dc49; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00473a74

entries.name: Sfx_ApplyLoopingNoOp
entries.description: Empty body. Sfx_SetLooping calls it when the voice is playing.

entries.name: Music_PlayTrack
entries.description: The copy of DBSIM's Music_PlayTrack: plays one Red Book CD track through MCI (cdaudio, TMSF, MCI_PLAY with MCI_NOTIFY). Reached only through Sfx_PlayMusicTrack.

entries.name: Sos_ShutdownDrivers
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_ShutdownDrivers: closes the digital driver when 00473184 is set and the MIDI driver when 00473186 is set, Sos_FreePreparedMemory twice for MIDI driver ids 0xa002/0xa009 with 0048a9ba bit 1, error results into 00473180 (returning 1); Sos_TimerUnInitSystem on the MIDI side unless 00473188. Returns 0.

entries.name: Sos_GetLastError
entries.description: MOV EAX,[00473180]; RET -- returns Sos_LastError. Sfx_StartVoice reads it when Sos_StartSample fails.

entries.name: Sos_AnyDriverActive
entries.description: Returns (00473184 & 00473188) | (00473186 & 0047318a): whether the digital driver is open and was requested, or the MIDI driver is. Sos_HandleWindowMessage asks it on WM_TIMER. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_AnyDriverActive (00474220).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042e44d; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00474220

entries.name: Sos_GetDriverHandle
entries.description: Returns the int16 at 0048aa26, the SOS digital driver handle. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_GetDriverHandle.

entries.name: Sos_FreePreparedMemory
entries.description: (memory, prepared): Sos_UnPrepare32Memory(prepared), then GlobalUnlock and GlobalFree of memory's global handle when memory is non-null. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_FreePreparedMemory.

entries.name: Sos_StartFileStream
entries.description: (path, arg, handleOut): plays a file as an SOS stream: Sos_StreamAcquire with a raw 8-bit mono 11025 Hz header, opens the file with _lopen (the plain file system), reads eight 0x8000-byte buffers into GlobalAlloc'd memory, prepares and queues each that read anything (Sos_StreamPrepareBuffer, Sos_StreamAddBuffer) and Sos_StreamStart, storing the stream handle in *handleOut. Returns 0, or 1 when the stream, the file or an allocation fails. Sfx_StartVoice's path for a sample flagged 0x1000.

entries.name: Sos_RefillStreamBuffer
entries.description: (streamId, bufferHeader): _hread's up to 0x8000 bytes from the stream's file into the header's data (+2), stores the count at +0xe and, when it is non-zero, requeues the buffer with Sos_StreamAddBuffer. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_RefillStreamBuffer (00474880).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042ead2; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00474880

entries.name: Sos_StopStream
entries.description: (streamId): Sos_StreamStop and Sos_StreamRelease, _lclose's the stream's file, then for each of its eight buffers Sos_StreamUnPrepareBuffer, Sos_UnPrepare32Memory on both prepared handles and GlobalUnlock/GlobalFree. Returns 0. Sfx_StopVoice and Sos_HandleWindowMessage call it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_StopStream (004748c4).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042eb13; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 004748c4

entries.name: Sos_HandleWindowMessage
entries.description: (hwnd, msg, wParam, lParam): WM_DESTROY kills timer 1; WM_INITDIALOG (0x110) sets timer 1 at 1 ms; WM_TIMER runs Sos_UserService on the driver handle (0048aa26) when Sos_AnyDriverActive says so; message 0xa000 hands wParam 0xa000 to Sos_RefillStreamBuffer and 0xa002 to Sos_StopStream. Returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_HandleWindowMessage (00474994).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0042ebea; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00474994

entries.name: ShellSound_Init
entries.description: Creates the shell's sound manager at 004731f0 unless -s cleared 00482272: loads hmi\gm_69.wav (press), hmi\bptlt2.wav (tab click), hmi\lswitch2.wav (startup switch) and hmi\shell1.wav or shell2.wav by option 5, flips option 5 and saves prefs.cfg, sets the music looping forever at the music volume.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlayTabClick
entries.description: The tab click, hmi\bptlt2.wav at volume 100, gated as ShellSound_PlayPress. The last call of each of the eight tab handlers.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlayPress
entries.description: The press sound, hmi\gm_69.wav at volume 100, while the manager exists, SOUNDS (option 1) is on and the sounds are running. ESButtonFont_HandleEvent, ESButtonBitmap_HandleEvent and ESRadioButton_HandleEvent call it on a press.

entries.name: ShellSound_PlaySwitch
entries.description: hmi\lswitch2.wav at volume 100, gated as the press sound. Called once, by the startup sequence widget's handler 004311b8 on its first tick.

entries.name: ShellSound_Start
entries.description: Unless the sounds are running: raises 00473200, sets the music looping forever, plays the press sound at volume 0 and starts the music at the music volume. Startup, the movie queue's end, and WM_SETFOCUS.

entries.name: ShellSound_Stop
entries.description: While the sounds are running: sets the music to play once, stops every sound, gives up the driver focus and drops 00473200. Before the movie queue, WM_KILLFOCUS, ONLINE MANUAL and the stage-5 location movie.

entries.name: ShellSound_Shutdown
entries.description: ShellSound_Stop, then destroys the sound manager and clears 004731f0. Called by Shell_ShutdownDevicesAndSound and by the insert-CD failure in Movie_PlayQueue.

entries.name: ShellSound_FadeOut
entries.description: While MUSIC (option 0) is on, steps the music volume down one each time more than 10 ms of GetTickCount have passed, pumping messages, until it is below 2.

entries.name: ShellSound_FadeIn
entries.description: While MUSIC (option 0) is on, steps the music volume up one each time more than 10 ms of GetTickCount have passed, pumping messages, until it is past 99.

entries.name: ShellSound_Stop_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to ShellSound_Stop. OnlineManual_Open calls it.

entries.name: CellWalk_SetCallback
entries.description: (ctx, callback, value): stores the cell walk's callback at ctx+0x14 and its value at ctx+0x18.

entries.name: CellWalk_Polygon
entries.description: (ctx, centre, polygon): cuts the polygon into four quadrants around the centre cell with Poly_ClipToHalfPlane, scan-converts each with Poly_BuildSpanList, and calls ctx's callback(ctx, row, xFrom, xTo) per row run, far to near when maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled == 0 && DAT_00471884 != 0 (the image values) and near to far otherwise. hgrid.cpp's cell renderer 00429b4a calls it.

entries.name: Point_RotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: (&x, &y, centre): x' = cx + (y - cy), y' = cy - (x - cx), in place. CellWalk_PolygonByColumn turns its polygon with it.

entries.name: Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout
entries.description: (&x, &y, centre): the inverse of Point_RotateQuarterAbout, x = cx - (y' - cy), y = cy + (x' - cx), in place.

entries.name: CellWalk_PolygonByColumn
entries.description: (ctx, centre, polygon): CellWalk_Polygon's far-to-near walk by column: turns the points a quarter turn about the centre (Point_RotateQuarterAbout), walks, turns each run's end cells back (Point_UnrotateQuarterAbout) and calls callback(ctx, column, yFrom, yTo), then turns the points back. Ghidra's decompile misreads its context as Rtl_VectorNew's return; it is the first argument, held in EDI.

entries.name: CellWalk_Rect
entries.description: (ctx, centre, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): the far-to-near cell walk over a rectangle, no scan conversion, each half running its first quadrant's rows before its second's.

entries.name: Poly_BuildSpanList
entries.description: (poly, spans, header): poly is {count, int32 {x, y} points*}. Translates the points in place so their minimum x and y are 0 (and does not translate them back), scan-converts them into spans with Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding, adds the minimum x back to every span, and fills header = {top row, bottom row, row count, pointer to spans + 8 (the first {x0, x1} pair)} with rows in screen coordinates. CellWalk_Polygon and CellWalk_PolygonByColumn call it on each quadrant Poly_ClipToHalfPlane cuts.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00465e0a and its two entry wrappers; DBSIM copies matched by byte comparison

entries.name: Poly_ClipToHalfPlane
entries.description: (keepHigh, alongX, value, in, out): one Sutherland-Hodgman pass keeping the part of polygon in ({count, points*}) with x (alongX) or y at >= value (keepHigh) or <= value, points on the line kept, into out (whose point pointer the caller sets); crossings computed from the previous point, truncating. Returns the count's low byte. The case bodies sit behind a jump table Ghidra left undisassembled.

entries.name: Stats_ScanSlots
entries.description: stats.cpp. Fills the eleven-entry slot summary table at 0048cddc by opening every save the directory marks in use and seeking block by block to the pilot record, the salvage pool and the career position. Its skip counts are a second independent statement of the whole GAME_?.SAV block order.

entries.name: Stats_StageCurrentGame
entries.description: Writes one slot's summary from the live game rather than from a file: the player's pilot record fields copied one at a time out of 00482a7c, then CareerSalvage, the campaign stage and the mission. This is what binds each summary offset to a named pilot-record offset.

entries.name: MainMenu_BuildScreen
entries.description: wmain.cpp. Builds the main menu once at shell startup: the six-frame bay2a_80..84 startup widget (DAT_0048d0c0), the backdrop root (DAT_0048d0c8), the MAIN MENU TitledPanel {0x90,0xad,0x1e2,0x138} (DAT_0048d0cc) and its ten buttons in two columns.

entries.name: MainMenu_Show
entries.description: Tab 0's entry: shows the main menu's root (DAT_0048d0c8) and panel (DAT_0048d0cc), then writes the greying trio at CONTINUE GAME (DAT_0048d0d4) from 00482a19, slot 10's in-use byte.

entries.name: MainMenu_Hide
entries.description: Hides the main menu's root and panel. Called first by every main-menu button that leaves the menu.

entries.name: StartupAnim_OnTick
entries.description: Handler of the startup sequence widget (DAT_0048d0c0), run on every alarm tick: plays ShellSound_PlaySwitch on its first run (DAT_00473608) and, once the widget's +0x6d reaches 5, hides it and calls MainMenu_Show, once only (DAT_00473604); with DAT_0046c088 set also puts up the Performance Note message box.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnInstantAction
entries.description: INSTANT ACTION's handler: DAT_0047363c = 1, FUN_0040e69e(0), InstantAction_SelectDemo, blank (full screen) or palette scope show/hide, Game_NewCareer("TRAINEE", option 0x27), Game_ExportMissionHandoff, Shell_SetExitCode(2), DAT_0046c074 = 1.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnStartNewGame
entries.description: START NEW GAME's handler: MainMenu_Hide, FUN_0040e69e(1), Registration_Show.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnContinue
entries.description: CONTINUE GAME's handler: Game_LoadSlot(10, 1), selected save slot 10, then the bare frame when DAT_0048260e is 2, otherwise FUN_0044cecf(DAT_0048260e).

entries.name: MainMenu_OnSaveRestore
entries.description: SAVE/RESTORE's handler: MainMenu_Hide, campaign mode 1 (FUN_0040e69e), SaveScreen_ExitTarget = 0, SaveScreen_Enter.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnPreferences
entries.description: PREFERENCES' handler: MainMenu_Hide, PreferencesScreen_Enter.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnViewDemo
entries.description: VIEW DEMO's handler: Shell_BlankScreen when full screen, Shell_SetExitCode(5), DAT_0046c074 = 1.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnCredits
entries.description: CREDITS' handler: shows the bare window DAT_0048d0c4, plays movie 0x54 through Movie_Enqueue and Movie_PlayQueue, hides it.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnQuit
entries.description: QUIT's handler: DAT_0046c074 = 1, Shell_BlankScreen.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnOnlineManual
entries.description: ONLINE MANUAL's handler: OnlineManual_Open.

entries.name: OnlineManual_Open
entries.description: Leaves full screen, option 6 = 0, commit, save all, ShellSound_Stop, then Shell_OpenHelp on <language>\es2guide.hlp by the language letter E/F/G.

entries.name: MainMenu_OnPracticeMissions
entries.description: PRACTICE MISSIONS' handler: MainMenu_Hide, PracticeScreen_Show, FUN_0040e69e(0).

entries.name: QuitAlert_Build
entries.description: Builds the Alt+F4 (key code 0x23e) QUIT alert QuitAlert (0048d0fc): caption estext 0x12 QUIT, buttons 0x11 CANCEL (QuitAlert_OnCancel) and 0x10 ACCEPT (QuitAlert_OnAccept).

entries.name: QuitAlert_OnCancel
entries.description: The QUIT alert's CANCEL button handler.

entries.name: QuitAlert_OnAccept
entries.description: The QUIT alert's ACCEPT handler: sets Shell_QuitFlag.

entries.name: Repair_InstallHotspotHandlers
entries.description: Fills RepairHotspotHandlers' 25 slots with the thunks 004340b5..00434ac8. Repair_BuildScreen's first call.

entries.name: Repair_BuildScreen
entries.description: Builds every widget of tab 3, REPAIR: eight per-bay damage grids over {0x10,0x2f,0xe0,0x12f}, the content TitledPanel {0xf1,0x2b,0x278,0x1d9}, the External and Internal list panels with their 16 and 9 rows, the mode and salvage readouts, three FramedPanel readout panels with REPAIR / REPAIR ALL / SCRAP, and CANCEL. Opens no file; every rect is four immediates on its own stack.

entries.name: Repair_Enter
entries.description: Brings the repair screen up: shows the content panel and both list panels, sets the mode readout from DAT_004824e4, calls Squad_SelectBay(Herc_FirstBuiltBay) when the current bay holds nothing workable -- before TabHandler_Repair stores 3, so that call takes the previous tab's arm, fills both lists (00433caf), snapshots the pool and the machine (Repair_Snapshot, 004338f6) and seeds the selection at (0, 0).

entries.name: Repair_Leave
entries.description: Tab 3's teardown, reached from the dispatcher at 00439ea7: hides the content panel and both list panels. Counterpart of Repair_Enter (004332ec).

entries.name: Repair_HotspotCategory
entries.description: (column, row) to condition-array category: 1 for any non-zero column, 2 for column 0 rows above 5, else 0. These are the same three modes HercStatus_Get takes -- 0 external group, 1 internal, 2 hardpoint.

entries.name: Repair_HotspotIndex
entries.description: Index within the category: row minus 6 for category 2, otherwise row.

entries.name: Repair_RefreshDetail
entries.description: Refills the three readout panels from the selection: the selected component's one-level repair cost (Repair_SelectionCost, 00411454), its condition word and colour, Repair_HercCost(herc, 100), and CareerSalvage minus Armory_QueuedTotal, all suffixed estext 0xc8 'kg'. Then writes the greying trio at REPAIR, REPAIR ALL and SCRAP -- the first two on affordability, SCRAP on there being a machine that is not the last deployable one.

entries.name: Repair_RefreshSalvage
entries.description: The repair screen's salvage readout: CareerSalvage - Armory_QueuedTotal().

entries.name: Repair_Snapshot
entries.description: Copies CareerSalvage into DAT_0048d25c and, with a bay selected, the selected machine's 66-byte status block (HercList_CopySelectedStatus) into DAT_0048d260. Called at the end of Repair_Enter and of Squad_SelectBay's repair arm; Repair_OnCancel restores both.

entries.name: Repair_SwapDiagram
entries.description: Swaps the two per-bay pictures as the selection crosses between columns: the internals diagram (0048d118) is shown while the internals list is selected and the exploded external picture (0048d4bc) while column 0 is.

entries.name: Repair_FillRow
entries.description: Fills one (column, row) of the repair lists: reads the condition through HercStatus_Get, formats it '%d%%' into the row's fourth text child in the damage band's colour, and for a hardpoint row also writes the fitted weapon's name (estext 0x7e + id, or 0x7d --Empty--) and the one-based mount number. A row past the machine's mount capacity is blanked to estext entry 1.

entries.name: Repair_FillAllRows
entries.description: Calls Repair_FillRow over column 0's sixteen rows and column 1's nine, then Repair_RefreshDetail.

entries.name: Repair_SetComponentNames
entries.description: Writes the fifteen component names into the two lists' name columns from one of two fifteen-entry estext index tables, at 00474000 for a walker and 0047401e when the machine's chassis type is 8, the Razor. Called only from Squad_SelectBay's repair arm (0043d753); a bay change on another tab, and Repair_Enter's reselection (which runs under the previous tab's arm), leave the names as they were.

entries.name: Repair_ColorRow
entries.description: Repaints one repair list row in a colour pair -- called as (column, row, 0x10, 0x27) for the outgoing selection and (column, row, 0x29, 0x29) for the incoming. It writes the row Panel's border at +0x4d and its first text child's ink, indexing the sixteen widgets at 0048d140 for column 0 and the nine at 0048d184 for column 1, so this is what maps a (column, row) back to the widget that draws it.

entries.name: Repair_SelectHotspot
entries.description: Takes (column, row), returns early if that pair is already selected, refuses a hardpoint row past the machine's mount capacity (+0x4c) or with nothing fitted, then repaints old and new, stores the pair and its resolved category and index, and refreshes the panel.

entries.name: Repair_OnRepair
entries.description: The repair screen's REPAIR handler: Repair_SelectionCost off CareerSalvage, then HercStatus_Set of the selection to Repair_TargetForLevel(Repair_DamageLevel(condition)); refills the row and Repair_RefreshDetail.

entries.name: Repair_OnRepairAll
entries.description: The repair screen's REPAIR ALL handler: Repair_HercCost(herc, 100) off CareerSalvage, Repair_Apply(herc, 100), Repair_FillAllRows.

entries.name: Repair_OnScrap
entries.description: The repair screen's SCRAP handler: ScrapDialog_Show.

entries.name: Repair_OnCancel
entries.description: The repair screen's CANCEL handler: CareerSalvage back from DAT_0048d25c and the status block at DAT_0048d260 copied over the selected machine, Repair_FillAllRows. Does not leave the screen.

entries.name: HercList_CopySelectedStatus
entries.description: Copies the status block (+0x08, 0x42 bytes) of the machine in the bay list's selected slot (list +0x22) into the caller's buffer; with the slot empty it writes nothing.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_Build
entries.description: Builds VSHELL's PREFERENCES screen (estext.bin 0x103): the Music and Sound Effects checkboxes (prefs options 0 and 1), Repair Options three ways (option 44), Weapons Building two (45), Game Resolution two (4) and Display Mode two (6). It is the one screen that edits the half of prefs.cfg DBSIM shares.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_Enter
entries.description: Seeds the PREFERENCES screen from the option array: options 0 and 1 into the two checkboxes, then 44, 45, 4 and 6 through their setters, each of which writes the option back and relights its radio group.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SyncSoundChecks
entries.description: Sets the tick (+0x69) of the Music checkbox 0048d30c from option 0 (ShellOptions) and of the Sound Effects checkbox 0048d310 from option 1 (ShellOption_Sounds), repainting each through its vtable slot +4. PreferencesScreen_Enter calls it.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SyncDisplayModeRadios
entries.description: Lights one of the pair 0048d2d0 / 0048d2d4 from ShellOption_DisplayMode (0 or 1), clearing the other's tick (+0x69) and repainting both. Any other value changes nothing. PreferencesScreen_SetDisplayMode calls it.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SyncRepairModeRadios
entries.description: Lights one of the Repair Mode three from ShellOption_RepairMode: 0048d324 for 0, 0048d328 for 1, 0048d32c for 2, clearing the other two's tick (+0x69) and repainting all three (vtable +4). Any other value changes nothing. PreferencesScreen_Enter and PreferencesScreen_SetRepairMode call it.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SyncResolutionRadios
entries.description: Lights one of the pair 0048d304 / 0048d308 from ShellOption_GameResolution (0 or 1), clearing the other's tick (+0x69) and repainting both. Any other value changes nothing.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SetRepairMode
entries.description: (value): stores the value at 00474cc4, sets option 0x2c (ShellOption_RepairMode) with its handler, and refreshes the row's buttons (PreferencesScreen_SyncRepairModeRadios).

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SetGameResolution
entries.description: (value): stores the value at 00474cc6, sets option 4 (ShellOption_GameResolution) with its handler, and refreshes the row's buttons (PreferencesScreen_SyncResolutionRadios).

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SyncBuildModeRadios
entries.description: Lights one of the Weapons Building pair from ShellOption_WeaponsBuildMode: 0048d33c for 0 (AutoBuild), 0048d340 for 1 (Manually Build), clearing the other's tick (+0x69) and repainting both. Any other value changes nothing.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SetWeaponsBuildMode
entries.description: (value): stores the value at 00474cc8, sets option 0x2d (ShellOption_WeaponsBuildMode) with its handler, and refreshes the row with PreferencesScreen_SyncBuildModeRadios.

entries.name: PreferencesScreen_SetDisplayMode
entries.description: (value): stores the value at 00474cca, sets option 6 (ShellOption_DisplayMode) with its handler, and refreshes the row's buttons (PreferencesScreen_SyncDisplayModeRadios).

entries.name: SaveScreen_RefreshDetail
entries.description: Rewrites the detail panel's twelve value fields from the selected slot's staging record: name, skill and rank words, six kill counters, salvage in tons, sector word and mission plus one. Writes estext.bin entry 0, the empty string, into all twelve when the slot holds no save.

entries.name: SaveScreen_BeginRename
entries.description: Returns at once when the rename state is 0. Otherwise posts an event at the selected row, moves the pointer onto it (Pointer_SetTarget, 00469cbc) and locks it there (+0x1f of DAT_005ddbd0), sets the row's caret flags +0xbf and +0xb3, rewrites the row as '%2d. ' with the name blanked, lights CANCEL and ACCEPT, and sets the rename state to 2.

entries.name: SaveScreen_SelectSlot
entries.description: Moves the slot selection. Returns early for the slot already selected unless a rename is live, repaints the outgoing row at 0x27 and the incoming at 0x29, regates SAVE and RESTORE, then refreshes the detail panel.

entries.name: SaveScreen_SetRowText
entries.description: Sets one slot row's string: the GAMEFILE.STR label when the second argument is zero, otherwise a formatted '%2d. %s' of the slot number and that argument.

entries.name: SaveScreen_RowText
entries.description: Returns the slot row's own string buffer (+0x45), or an empty string when the row is not built. ACCEPT passes it to Game_SaveSlot as the slot's new label.

entries.name: SaveScreen_OnSave
entries.description: The SAVE button. Writes nothing: sets the rename state to 1, greys SAVE, RESTORE and EXIT, and calls SaveScreen_BeginRename. ACCEPT is what writes the save.

entries.name: SaveScreen_OnRestore
entries.description: The RESTORE button. Game_LoadSlot(selected, 1), Game_SaveSlot(10, NULL) as the current-game autosave, the save screen teardown, clears DAT_004778aa, then Shell_SelectTabPalette(8) and ServiceBay_RefreshTabStrip -- EXIT's tab-strip path whatever SaveScreen_ExitTarget holds.

entries.name: SaveScreen_OnExit
entries.description: The EXIT button. Tears the screen down and then returns to where 0048d344 says: 0 rebuilds the main menu, 8 installs palette case 8 and refreshes the tab strip.

entries.name: SaveScreen_OnCancel
entries.description: The CANCEL button. Restores the row's GAMEFILE.STR label, greys CANCEL and ACCEPT, lights SAVE, RESTORE and EXIT, rename state to 0, then SaveScreen_SelectSlot(10), which deselects the row and regates SAVE and RESTORE off.

entries.name: SaveScreen_OnAccept
entries.description: The ACCEPT button. Game_SaveSlot(selected, the row's typed text), Stats_StageCurrentGame, refreshes the detail panel, greys CANCEL and ACCEPT, lights SAVE, RESTORE and EXIT, rename state to 0.

entries.name: SaveScreen_BuildScreen
entries.description: Builds tab 1, SAVED GAMES: the backdrop root, the titled content panel, the slot list frame, ten editable slot rows, five buttons and the detail panel's 22 text fields. Every rect is four immediates on its own stack; opens no file.

entries.name: SaveScreen_Enter
entries.description: Tab 1's entry routine. Sets all ten row texts from the GAMEFILE.STR labels, gates SAVE on 0048260a and RESTORE on the selected slot's in-use byte, highlights the selected row and refreshes the detail panel. Does not build: FUN_004385b0 does that once.

entries.name: SaveScreen_Teardown
entries.description: Called first by both the EXIT and the RESTORE handlers. SaveScreen_SelectSlot(10), then Window_HideRecursive on the save screen's content panel (0048d34c), root (0048d348) and both detail panels (0048d3b8, 0048d418).

entries.name: Shell_SetPaletteScope
entries.description: Hides PaletteScopeWidget, writes the palette index to its +0x45 and shows it again, which installs that palette.

entries.name: TabStrip_ClearAllLit
entries.description: Clears +0x45 on all nine strip buttons and repaints them. Every tab handler starts here; tabs 2-7 then write their own back to 1 and the main menu's and save's do not, which is why the strip is drawn unlit while either of those is up.

entries.name: Shell_TeardownCurrentTab
entries.description: Tears down whatever tab CurrentTabIndex names, dispatching per tab; the squad panel's hide (Squad_HidePanel) is part of four of the cases.

entries.name: TabHandler_MenuButton
entries.description: The square button's click handler; calls into wmain.cpp at 004317ea.

entries.name: TabHandler_MainMenu
entries.description: Tab 0. Tears down, installs palette 1, autosaves through Game_SaveSlot(10, NULL), then builds the main menu. Does not latch its own plate.

entries.name: TabHandler_Save
entries.description: Tab 1. Tears down, installs palette 1, sets 0048d344 to 8 and builds the save screen. Does not latch its own plate.

entries.name: TabHandler_Weapons
entries.description: Tab 2. Latches its plate, shows the squad panel and builds the arming screen.

entries.name: TabHandler_Repair
entries.description: Tab 3. Latches its plate, shows the squad panel and builds the repair screen.

entries.name: TabHandler_Build
entries.description: Tab 4. Latches its plate, shows the squad panel and builds the build screen.

entries.name: TabHandler_Armory
entries.description: Tab 5. Latches its plate and builds the armory screen; the only latching tab with no squad panel.

entries.name: TabHandler_Crew
entries.description: Tab 6. Latches its plate, shows the squad panel and builds the crew screen.

entries.name: TabHandler_Mission
entries.description: Tab 7. Picks the mission sub-mode -- 0 (campaign map) when 004778aa and CampaignMissionInStage are both zero, else 1 (briefing) -- and calls Mission_ShowView.

entries.name: Mission_ShowView
entries.description: Stores the mission sub-mode in MissionScreenView, installs that view's palette and builds the mission screen. Also called by the campaign layer with the debrief mode.

entries.name: ServiceBay_BuildScreen
entries.description: wsrvbayi.cpp (service/repair bay tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref. Every widget's {x,y,w,h} rect is a plain immediate literal in this function (e.g. local_5c=0x27f, local_58=0x1df); no fopen/Volume/ClassIO/fread call anywhere in the function. Confirms VSHELL's tab-screen layouts are hardcoded pixel constants compiled into the EXE, not driven by any data file.

entries.name: ServiceBay_RefreshTabStrip
entries.description: The tab gate. Shows the shell panel (and with it the strip), then writes +0x49 on tabs 2-6 from CampaignModeFlag -- REPAIR, BUILD and ARMORY off in training, all five on in the campaign -- and parks CurrentTabIndex at 0xffff.

entries.name: Shell_SelectTabPalette
entries.description: Picks a tab's palette index and hands it to Shell_SetPaletteScope. Tab 3 takes 1, tabs 2 and 4-6 take 2, tab 7 takes stage+4 (briefing), stage+9 (debrief) or 3/4 (map). Case 8 is not a tab: it shows the shell root (ShellRootWidget), undoing ServiceBay_Show.

entries.name: ServiceBay_Show
entries.description: Despite the name, HIDES the shell panel and root -- and with the panel every tab-strip button -- then installs palette 1 (dpl\palette.dpl). Called by tabs 0 and 1, so the main menu and the save screen stand alone with no strip. The name predates the Widget_Show/HideRecursive swap; Shell_SelectTabPalette(8) plus ServiceBay_RefreshTabStrip undo it.

entries.name: SaveRegistration_BuildPanel
entries.description: Builds a second registration panel into the save screen's stub panel DAT_0048d418 at startup (FUN_004012b0 at 004012f2): FramedPanel DAT_0048d470, prompt, name box DAT_0048d47c and field DAT_0048d480, Text readout DAT_0048d484, SKILL LEVEL (0043bd15), CANCEL (0043bd90) and ACCEPT (0043bf1b). No show of DAT_0048d418 or DAT_0048d470 found by an absolute-operand search.

entries.name: SaveRegistration_ShowDetailPanel
entries.description: Window_HideRecursive on 0048d470 and 0048d418, then Window_ShowRecursive on the detail panel 0048d3b8. SaveRegistration_OnAccept and 0043bd90 call it.

entries.name: Registration_BuildScreen
entries.description: Builds the registration screen once at startup (FUN_004012b0 at 004012f7): the backdrop root DAT_0048d494, the TitledPanel DAT_0048d498 {0xce,0xc6,0x1b2,0x144} (REGISTRATION), the FramedPanel DAT_0048d49c, the prompt, the disabled name box DAT_0048d4a4 and its edit field DAT_0048d4a8 (set 00476169, handler 0043bdee), the skill readout DAT_0048d4ac, SKILL LEVEL (0043c01d), CANCEL (0043c098) and ACCEPT DAT_0048d4b8 (0043c0fb), built greyed. Verified: estext 0x30-0x34 captions, and the three widgets Registration_Show and Registration_Hide name.

entries.name: Registration_Show
entries.description: START NEW GAME's screen up: shows DAT_0048d494, DAT_0048d498 and DAT_0048d49c (Registration_BuildScreen's root, panel and box), posts a left press at the name field DAT_0048d4a8, sets the pointer's target to it (Pointer_SetTarget) and locks it.

entries.name: Registration_Hide
entries.description: Hides the registration screen's root, panel and box (DAT_0048d494, DAT_0048d498, DAT_0048d49c). Called by CANCEL (0043c098) and ACCEPT (0043c0fb).

entries.name: SaveRegistration_ShowSkillText
entries.description: Sets the text widget 0048d484 to the ES text string RegistrationSkillChoice + 0x35 (WeaponsBin_LookupName on EsTextBinHandle), colour 2, 0x29, 1. SaveRegistration_BuildPanel and SaveRegistration_StepSkill call it.

entries.name: SaveRegistration_StepSkill
entries.description: SKILL LEVEL on the save screen's second registration panel (FUN_0043b260): steps RegistrationSkillChoice modulo 4 and rewrites that panel's readout DAT_0048d484 from estext.bin 0x35 + skill (FUN_0043bce0). Not the registration screen's; that is 0043c01d.

entries.name: Registration_OnNameEvent
entries.description: The registration name field's handler (+0x3d, written by Registration_BuildScreen): on an event 0x40 (character) or 0x100 (command) writes the greying trio at ACCEPT (DAT_0048d4b8) from the field's first character -- 0x26/0x26/disabled while empty, 0x29/0x22/enabled otherwise.

entries.name: SaveRegistration_OnAccept
entries.description: ACCEPT on the save screen's second registration panel (FUN_0043b260): Game_NewCareer(DAT_0048d480's string, RegistrationSkillChoice), Stats_StageCurrentGame(10), SaveRegistration_ShowDetailPanel (hides DAT_0048d470 and DAT_0048d418, shows the detail panel DAT_0048d3b8), then lights SAVE (DAT_0048d3ac). Not the registration screen's; that is 0043c0fb.

entries.name: Registration_ShowSkillText
entries.description: Sets the text widget at +0x55 of 0048d4ac to the ES text string RegistrationSkillChoice + 0x35, keeping its colour +0x45 and +0xb5. Registration_BuildScreen and Registration_StepSkill call it.

entries.name: Registration_StepSkill
entries.description: SKILL LEVEL's handler on the registration screen: steps RegistrationSkillChoice modulo 4 and rewrites the readout DAT_0048d4ac from estext.bin 0x35 + skill (FUN_0043bfe1). Reads no button sub-code, so either button's release steps forward.

entries.name: Registration_OnCancel
entries.description: CANCEL's handler on the registration screen: Registration_Hide, then MainMenu_Show.

entries.name: Registration_OnAccept
entries.description: ACCEPT's handler on the registration screen: LoadHercInfDat, Registration_Hide, DAT_004778aa = 0, Game_NewCareer(name field's string, RegistrationSkillChoice), then MissionScreenView = (CampaignMissionInStage != 0) -- 0, the map view, before the posted Use Default click loads the mission.

entries.name: Hotspots_BuildOverlay
entries.description: wsquadi.cpp. Builds the clickable-region overlay for the arming tab (mode 2, gam\arm_hots.dat) or the repair tab (mode 3, gam\rpr_hots.dat), one Panel per area over each of the eight bay slots' chassis pictures. Not the squad roster list: the name it carried before described the module, not the function.

entries.name: Squad_FreeTabWidgets
entries.description: Frees the nine arrays at 00476328 (Mem_DeleteArray), then for each of the eight squad slots at 00482ac3 that has a chassis (HercList_ChassisAt) and a widget array at 00476308: detaches and deletes that slot's widgets -- the member's +0x4c of them on tab 2, 0048d57c[chassis] plus the member's +0x4e on tab 3, none on any other tab (CurrentTabIndex) -- and frees the array. Squad_FreeTabPictures calls it.

entries.name: Squad_BuildTabPictures
entries.description: Per-tab picture builder the squad panel's show runs: tab 3 builds the repair diagrams and their hotspot overlay, tabs 2, 4 and 6 Squad_BuildBayPictures (00414e5b), tab 2 the arming hotspots as well.

entries.name: Squad_FreeTabPictures
entries.description: The teardown counterpart of Squad_BuildTabPictures, per tab.

entries.name: Squad_BuildRosterList
entries.description: wsquadi.cpp: builds the squad panel -- the eight per-bay picture Grids and the empty one at {5, 0x2b, 0xeb, 0x130}, the Pilot/Skill/Condition label and value Texts, the Squad Inventory TitledPanel and its eight four-column rows on a 14-pixel pitch -- then loads the armory and repair layouts.

entries.name: Squad_ShowPanel
entries.description: Puts up the per-slot panel the WEAPONS, REPAIR, BUILD and CREW tabs share: runs the tab's picture builder (0043c915), refills the readout and the roster, shows the selected bay's picture (or the empty one at 0048d4dc for no bay), the six readout texts and the roster, and colours the eight roster rows -- 0x29 on the selected one, 0x10 on the rest.

entries.name: Squad_HidePanel
entries.description: The mirror of Squad_ShowPanel, run from Shell_TeardownCurrentTab.

entries.name: Squad_RefreshAfterScrap
entries.description: Squad_SetEmptyBayPicture, repaint of the selected bay's picture, the readout, the roster names and crew; on tab 3 the repair salvage figure (004338b3), on tab 4 Build_RefreshSalvage.

entries.name: Squad_RefreshSelectedReadout
entries.description: Squad_RefreshReadout(DAT_00482ae5).

entries.name: Squad_RefreshReadout
entries.description: Fills the squad panel's Pilot/Skill/Condition values for one bay: the pilot's name or Unassigned, 0x35 + skill, and the overall condition's band word in its colour or N% Complete in 0x20 while the machine is being built.

entries.name: Squad_SelectBay
entries.description: A squad roster click: returns for the bay already selected, then takes the bay each tab's own way, by DAT_0047581c. The repair tab refuses an empty or unbuilt bay, swaps the pictures, relights the rows, stores DAT_00482ae5 and resets the repair selection to (0, 0). The crew tab accepts -1 or a finished machine, refusing the Razor unless CrewSelectedRow is 0, and first assigns the bay while Squad_RosterClickFlag is set.

entries.name: Repair_DamageLevel
entries.description: Damage level 0-5 of a 0-100 condition: the first index of DamageLevelBands the condition is strictly greater than, or 5 if none. Hand-decoded from the instruction stream -- the counter lives in EAX (xor eax,eax / inc eax) and the comparison is kept in CX/DX, which is what makes the return the level and not the threshold. Bands match Repair_LevelForCondition's exactly.

entries.name: Repair_DamageLevelColor
entries.description: Calls Repair_DamageLevel and returns DamageLevelColors[level].

entries.name: Squad_RefreshRowNames
entries.description: Writes each roster row's machine name (the HERC record's +0x04 string) in the band colour of its overall condition.

entries.name: Squad_RefreshRowCrew
entries.description: Writes each roster row's last column in 0x27: the assigned pilot's name, or N% Complete for a machine still being built.

entries.name: Arming_SelectHardpoint
entries.description: The arming screen's counterpart to Repair_SelectHotspot: one hardpoint index, a no-op when it is already selected, and it reads the fitted weapon id from the mount pointer at herc+0x50+index*4.

entries.name: Arming_FitSelected
entries.description: With a hardpoint selected: calls Herc_FitMount (004114ec)(herc, hardpoint, weapon) while Arming_FitArmed is set, then Arming_MarkHardpoint and repaints the bay picture.

entries.name: Arming_SetMountGuidance
entries.description: Writes a guidance kind into the selected hardpoint's mount record at +0x08, when a hardpoint is selected and the mount is fitted.

entries.name: Arming_NextHardpoint
entries.description: The > stepper: Arming_SelectHardpoint((hardpoint + 1) % mount capacity).

entries.name: Arming_PreviousHardpoint
entries.description: The < stepper: Arming_SelectHardpoint(hardpoint - 1), wrapping from 0 or none to the last mount.

entries.name: Arming_BuildScreen
entries.description: warmingi.cpp: builds the weapon-fitting screen, reading gam\arm_weap.dat against dba\arm_weap.dba. Its 26 weapon panels are the authoritative set of buyable weapon ids; the four trailing panels are the guidance kinds SARH 0, ARH 1, ARM 2, EO 3. Also opens wpn_desc.bin, three lines per weapon id.

entries.name: Arming_Enter
entries.description: Tab 2's entry, called by TabHandler_Weapons before it stores 2 in CurrentTabIndex: shows the content panel, the inventory and the picture box; when SelectedBaySlot is -1, empty or unfinished calls Squad_SelectBay(Herc_FirstBuiltBay) (which therefore takes the previous tab's arm); clears ArmingSelectedHardpoint and runs Arming_SelectRow(0).

entries.name: Arming_Leave
entries.description: The teardown dispatcher's tab-2 arm: hides the content panel, the inventory and the picture box.

entries.name: Arming_ShowGuidanceButtons
entries.description: Shows the ARM/ARH/SARH/EO buttons and the rack-name button, once, on Arming_GuidanceButtonsUp.

entries.name: Arming_HideGuidanceButtons
entries.description: Puts the four guidance buttons' borders back to 0x22 and hides all five buttons, when Arming_GuidanceButtonsUp is set.

entries.name: Arming_RowOfWeapon
entries.description: The inventory row (0-26) listing a weapon id in Arming_RowWeapons, or -1.

entries.name: Arming_SelectRow
entries.description: An inventory row's handler (27 thunks from 00440300, each setting Arming_FitArmed). No-op for the lit row unless a guidance picture is up or a hardpoint is selected. With a hardpoint, refuses a weapon with none in stock unless fitted (testing the mount's +0x08 guidance kind first) and fits through Arming_FitSelected. Refreshes the rows, relights old and new rows, swaps the picture, fills three wpn_desc.bin lines from id*3, and puts the guidance buttons up for ids 0xd-0x10 or takes them down.

entries.name: Arming_RefreshRows
entries.description: Rewrites all 27 inventory rows: the owned count (weapons.dat +0x17) as %d, two spaces for None; a locked weapon (+0x16 clear) disabled in 0x10; an unlocked one 0x27 and live while Arming_RowLive holds, else 0x25 and disabled.

entries.name: Arming_ShowGuidance
entries.description: Arming_ShowGuidance(kind, show): relights the guidance buttons (0x22 old, 0x20 new); with show set swaps the lit row's picture for the kind's and prints wpn_desc.bin 99+kind*3; stores the kind and writes it to the selected mount through Arming_SetMountGuidance. Kinds: SARH 0, ARH 1, ARM 2, EO 3.

entries.name: Crew_BuildScreen
entries.description: wcrewi.cpp (crew tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref. Same hardcoded-rect-literal pattern; no file I/O.

entries.name: Crew_ColourRows
entries.description: Colours each crew row by whether it is below 00482a78: body +0x59 0x25/0x10, labels 0x19/0x1a, value backing 0x25/0x10. The value colours it writes (0x16/0x17) are overwritten by Crew_FillRows' ESMessage_SetString.

entries.name: Crew_Enter
entries.description: Tab 6's screen entry, run after the handler has stored 6 in DAT_0047581c: Crew_ColourRows, Crew_MatchRowPilots, the three squad portraits, Crew_SelectRow 0-3 then 0, Crew_FillRows, then Squad_SelectBay for every occupied bay -- which leaves the last bay holding a finished machine selected.

entries.name: Crew_Leave
entries.description: The crew tab's teardown: hides the crew content panel (DAT_0048d72c). Called from Shell_TeardownCurrentTab (00439ea7) at 00439f21.
