entries.name: Crew_MatchRowPilots
entries.description: Fills the row pilot pointers at 004776e0 for rows 1-3 with the squad member at that position (Squad_MemberAtPosition), or null.

entries.name: Crew_SelectRow
entries.description: (row): relights the old and new rows' borders and portraits (0x21/0x29), calls Squad_SelectBay with the row pilot's bay (the player's for row 0, -1 for an empty row), then stores the row in CrewSelectedRow -- so the Razor test inside sees the row being left.

entries.name: Crew_FillRows
entries.description: Fills the four crew rows' portraits and Name/Skill/Herc values: the player from 00482a80, PlayerPilotSkill and bay 00482a9e, each squad row from its pilot record, 0x7e None for a pilot with no machine, estext entry 0 for an empty row.

entries.name: Crew_AssignSquadMember
entries.description: (k), the three squad portraits' action. Returns at once on the player's row (CrewSelectedRow 0). Otherwise frees the selected row's position from whoever holds it (Squad_SetMemberPosition -1), gives it to squad member k, clears any row pointer at 004776e0 holding k and points the selected row at k, then Crew_AssignSelectedBay, Squad_RefreshRowCrew, the readout and Crew_FillRows.

entries.name: Crew_ClearRow
entries.description: CLEAR's action. On a squad row holding a member: Squad_SetMemberBay(k, -1), Squad_SetMemberPosition(k, -1), nulls the row pointer, Crew_FillRows, then Squad_SelectBay with the member's now -1 bay while Squad_RosterClickFlag is set. Nothing on the player's row or an empty one.

entries.name: Crew_AssignSelectedBay
entries.description: Gives SelectedBaySlot to the selected row's pilot when the row is the player's or has a pilot: unassigns the player (Player_SetBay -1) and every squad member (Squad_SetMemberBay -1) whose bay equals it, then writes it to the player through Player_SetBay or to the squad member's +0x22 followed by Squad_UpdateOnStrength(row), and Crew_FillRows. With SelectedBaySlot -1 every bayless squad member counts as its holder. Called from Squad_SelectBay's crew arm while Squad_RosterClickFlag is set, and from Crew_AssignSquadMember.

entries.name: Mission_BuildScreen
entries.description: The mission tab's builder (wmissini.cpp): Telecomm, the map panel and its six miss_arw.dba buttons, the map grid, the Mission Summary panel with its five text boxes and two page buttons, the twenty report texts, and the button bar with Mission Briefing / Mission Objectives / Intelligence Report / Rock & Roll >. Every widget it builds is one Mission_Show (004441e3) shows and Mission_Leave (00444a05) hides; it sits inside the address range that reads as wcrewi.cpp's.

entries.name: Mission_LoadPictures
entries.description: wmissini.cpp's first assert string. Loads dba\terradef.dba into the Telecomm picture (DAT_0048d7e4) and, for the map view (arg 0), dba\th_earth.dba below stage 5 or dba\th_moon.dba as the map grid's part 0.

entries.name: Mission_FreePictures
entries.description: ESGrid_InitAllRows(0048d814), then GLBitmapArray_Dtor(_, 3) on the non-null arrays at 00477fc0 and 00477fc4, clearing each. Mission_Leave calls it.

entries.name: maybe_Mission_UpdateLocationTab
entries.description: At stage 5 enqueues movie 0x55 (the lunar drop), installs palette 2 through the scope and fades the music out and stops it; below it, loads frame 0 of MissionLocationDbaTable[stage - 1] into the location picture (DAT_0048d7e0), shows it and installs the theater palette stage + 0xe. Movie_PlayQueue calls it after an entry with the location flag.

entries.name: Mission_HideLocationPicture
entries.description: Hides the mission tab's location picture (DAT_0048d7e0) and frees its bank.

entries.name: Mission_Show
entries.description: Puts the mission tab up in a view: 0 campaign map, 1 briefing, 4 debrief. Retitles the map panel, moves the summary, fills and shows the text boxes, shows or hides the map buttons, bar and page buttons, and enqueues the view's movie once: the map's while its first-show flag DAT_004778aa is clear (RESTORE and a new career clear it), the briefing's and debrief's once per load.

entries.name: Mission_HideReportTexts
entries.description: Hides the mission screen's twenty report texts (DAT_0048d838-DAT_0048d884); Mission_Show calls it in the map and briefing views.

entries.name: Mission_Leave
entries.description: The teardown dispatcher's mission arm (00439ea7 case 7): frees the pictures, hides the report texts, clears the four career text boxes and hides the screen's panels.

entries.name: Career_ObjectivesText_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Career_ObjectivesText and returns its result (the decompile drops it). Mission_Show calls it.

entries.name: Career_IntelligenceText_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Career_IntelligenceText and returns its result. Mission_Show calls it.

entries.name: Career_BriefingText_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Career_BriefingText and returns its result. Mission_Show calls it.

entries.name: Mission_DebriefText
entries.description: Thunk to Career_DebriefText, which Mission_Show(4) fills text box 4 from.

entries.name: Mission_ResetViewButtonBorders
entries.description: Sets the border colour +0x4d of the three mission buttons 0048d804, 0048d808 and 0048d80c to 0x22 and repaints each with Window_RepaintRecursive. Mission_LightViewButton calls it before lighting one.

entries.name: Mission_LightViewButton
entries.description: Puts the first three mission buttons' borders back to 0x22 and writes 0x20 on Mission Briefing for 1 and 4, Mission Objectives for 2, Intelligence Report for 3.

entries.name: Mission_ShowTextBox
entries.description: Marks the text box in DAT_004780a4 not shown and box n shown (+0x18), runs TextBox_ShowPage on both and stores n. Boxes: 0 map, 1 briefing, 2 objectives, 3 intelligence, 4 debrief.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapUp
entries.description: Map button 1: ShellMap vtable +0xc then its paint, 1-4 times by the auto-repeat count +0x65.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapDown
entries.description: Map button 2: vtable +0x10.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapLeft
entries.description: Map button 3: vtable +0x14.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapRight
entries.description: Map button 4: vtable +0x18.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapZoomIn
entries.description: Map button 5 (arrows pointing in): vtable +4.

entries.name: Mission_OnMapZoomOut
entries.description: Map button 6 (arrows pointing out): vtable +8.

entries.name: Mission_OnBriefing
entries.description: Mission Briefing's handler: Mission_LightViewButton and Mission_ShowTextBox with the view (DAT_0048106c).

entries.name: Mission_OnObjectives
entries.description: Mission Objectives' handler: Mission_LightViewButton(2), Mission_ShowTextBox(2).

entries.name: Mission_OnIntelligence
entries.description: Intelligence Report's handler: Mission_LightViewButton(3), Mission_ShowTextBox(3).

entries.name: Mission_OnRockAndRoll
entries.description: Rock & Roll >'s handler: refuses through the dialog FUN_0044d27c with codes 2, 0, 1, 3, otherwise Game_ExportMissionHandoff, FUN_0040876a(2) and DAT_0046c074 = 1.

entries.name: Mission_OnPageUp
entries.description: The summary's up button: TextBox_PageUp on the box in DAT_004780a4.

entries.name: Mission_OnPageDown
entries.description: The summary's down button: TextBox_PageDown on the box in DAT_004780a4.

entries.name: Career_BriefingMovie_Thunk
entries.description: Calls Career_BriefingMovie and returns its result. Mission_Show calls it.

entries.name: Mission_DebriefMovie
entries.description: Thunk to Career_DebriefMovie, which Mission_Show(4) enqueues once per load.

entries.name: Build_BuildScreen
entries.description: The BUILD tab's builder: the Herc Construction titled panel (estext 0xba), nine blueprint Grids, the nine-row chassis list (0x6e + i), the stats box and its four figures, and the lower panel with Salvage Available and the Scrap Herc / Build Herc boxes. Every widget it builds is the one Build_Enter (0044690d) shows and Build_Leave (0044694e) hides. Sits after wmissini.cpp's assert anchor in the image, which is why it was once taken for the mission builder.

entries.name: Build_GateRows
entries.description: Per chassis row: disabled with all four columns 0x10 when (&DAT_00483b62)[type*8] is clear, else all four columns 0x27 and enabled. Rewrites the selected row's name colour too.

entries.name: Build_Enter
entries.description: Tab 4's entry: Build_GateRows, Herc_BuildScreenRefresh, Build_GateButtons, Build_FillBlueprints, shows the content panel, the lower panel and blueprint 0, then Build_SelectChassis(0).

entries.name: Build_Leave
entries.description: The teardown dispatcher's tab-4 arm: frees the blueprint banks, hides the content panel, the lower panel and the selected chassis's blueprint.

entries.name: Build_GateButtons
entries.description: Gates SCRAP and BUILD on the selected bay: empty -> SCRAP dead, BUILD live when CareerSalvage - Armory_QueuedTotal() > price*1000; occupied -> BUILD dead, SCRAP dead when Herc_HasSingleDeployable or the bay's chassis is unavailable.

entries.name: Build_SelectChassis
entries.description: Moves DAT_004786e4 (-1 in the image): old row's name 0x27 and border 0x10 and its blueprint hidden, new row's name and border 0x29 and its blueprint shown, then Build_GateButtons and Herc_BuildScreenRefresh. Returns at once for the chassis already selected.

entries.name: Herc_BuildScreenRefresh
entries.description: Refreshes the Herc Construction stat panel from herc_inf.dat: mass as "%d TONS", speed as "%d KPH", hardpoints bare, price as "%d TONS". This is what names those four fields.

entries.name: Build_RefreshSalvage
entries.description: Writes the lower panel's Salvage Available figure: (CareerSalvage - Armory_QueuedTotal()) / 1000 as %ld %s with estext 0xc6 TONS.

entries.name: Build_OnScrap
entries.description: The build screen's SCRAP handler: ScrapDialog_Show.

entries.name: Build_OnBuild
entries.description: The build screen's BUILD handler: Hangar_BuySelected(DAT_004786e4), then the roster names and crew, the readout, Build_RefreshSalvage and Build_GateButtons.

entries.name: ScrapDialog_Build
entries.description: Builds the herc scrap dialog once at startup: a full-display Window, an ESAlert panel at {0xcb,199,0x1af,0x149} titled estext 0xc9 WARNING, two FramedPanels, caption 0xcc and a figure Text, CANCEL (0xca, 00447c38) and ACCEPT (0xcb, 00447c96).

entries.name: ScrapDialog_Show
entries.description: Writes "%d %s" of Herc_ScrapValueTons(selected bay's machine) and estext 0xcd into the dialog's figure and shows it (Alert_Show). Called by Build_OnScrap and Repair_OnScrap.

entries.name: ScrapDialog_Hide
entries.description: Hides the herc scrap dialog (Alert_Hide).

entries.name: WeaponScrapDialog_Build
entries.description: The armory Scrap dialog's builder: the herc scrap dialog's rects and colours, caption estext 0xce, CANCEL 00447d59, ACCEPT 00447db7.

entries.name: WeaponScrapDialog_Show
entries.description: Stores the weapon id in DAT_0048d970, writes "%d %s" of Armory_ScrapValueTons(id) and estext 0xcd into the figure and shows the dialog.

entries.name: WeaponScrapDialog_Hide
entries.description: Hides the armory's scrap dialog (Alert_Hide).

entries.name: ScrapDialog_OnCancel
entries.description: CANCEL's handler: ScrapDialog_Hide only. The builder passes it as a bare address, so auto-analysis made no function of it; ES2DefineFunctionAt 00447c38 creates it.

entries.name: ScrapDialog_OnAccept
entries.description: ACCEPT's handler: ScrapDialog_Hide, Hangar_ScrapSelected, Squad_RefreshAfterScrap; tab 4 Build_GateButtons; tab 3 Squad_SelectBay(Herc_FirstBuiltBay) and Repair_RefreshDetail; then repaints 0048d13c, 0048d1cc and 0048d4f4.

entries.name: WeaponScrapDialog_OnCancel
entries.description: The weapon scrap dialog's CANCEL: WeaponScrapDialog_Hide only.

entries.name: WeaponScrapDialog_OnAccept
entries.description: The weapon scrap dialog's ACCEPT: WeaponScrapDialog_Hide, Armory_ScrapWeapons(DAT_0048d970), Armory_RefreshQueue, Armory_RefreshRows, Armory_RefreshReadout.

entries.name: Armory_BuildScreen
entries.description: warmoryi.cpp (armory tab) screen builder, located via __FILE__ assert-string xref -- also the largest function in its TU (5365 bytes). Same hardcoded-rect-literal widget-construction pattern; no file I/O. Together with ServiceBay/Squad/Warning/Crew/Mission_BuildScreen, confirms none of VSHELL's tab screens are data-driven -- all layouts are pixel constants compiled into the EXE.

entries.name: Armory_RefreshRows
entries.description: For each of the 26 armory rows: a weapon whose unlock flag (weapons.dat +0x16) is clear has the row disabled and all four columns recoloured 0x10; otherwise the row is enabled, column 0 set to "[ %1d ]" of the queued count or "[   ]", column 2 to "%d" of the owned count, and all four recoloured 0x27.

entries.name: Armory_Enter
entries.description: Tab 5's entry. Writes the greying trio at Clear from ShellOption_WeaponsBuildMode (live only when weapons are built by hand), runs Armory_RefreshRows and Armory_RefreshReadout, shows the content panel and the list, and calls Armory_ClickRow(0). Armory_Leave has put the lit row back to -1, so that call always selects.

entries.name: Armory_Leave
entries.description: The teardown dispatcher's armory arm: hides the lit row's picture, the content panel and the list, and sets the lit row DAT_00479174 back to -1.

entries.name: Armory_DequeueLit
entries.description: Clear's action: with a row lit, Armory_Dequeue of its weapon, column 0 back to "[   ]" in 0x29, and Armory_RefreshReadout.

entries.name: Armory_ClickRow
entries.description: A row's left release. On a row other than the lit one, or with weapons built automatically: recolours the old row 0x27 and hides its picture, lights the new one 0x29, shows its picture and fills the five wpn_info.bin lines from Arming_RowOfWeapon(id) * 5, and stores the row. On the lit row with weapons built by hand: with a queue slot free and the queued total + price < the career salvage, Armory_Enqueue and the row's queued count and the readout refreshed.

entries.name: Armory_RightClickRow
entries.description: A row's right release. Selects exactly as Armory_ClickRow; on the lit row with weapons built by hand, removes one queued unit by dequeuing every one (Armory_DequeueLit) and enqueuing count - 1 again through Armory_ClickRow.

entries.name: Armory_RefreshReadout
entries.description: Writes the armory's four figures, all centred in 0x29: "%ld kg" of CareerSalvage - Armory_QueuedTotal, "%d kg" of Armory_QueuedTotal, the free queue slots and 5 minus them; then the lit row's owned count in 0x29.

entries.name: Armory_OnScrap
entries.description: Scrap's click handler: FUN_00447b97 with the lit row's weapon id, when a row is lit.

entries.name: Armory_OnClear
entries.description: Clear's click handler: Armory_DequeueLit.

entries.name: Armory_OnRow00
entries.description: Armory row 0's click handler, one of 26 identical thunks in ArmoryRowHandlers: Armory_ClickRow(0) when the event's button byte +0x24 is 1 (left), else Armory_RightClickRow(0); then deletes the event (Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount into [005ddec0], virtual dtor +0x18 with 3).

entries.name: PracticeScreen_Build
entries.description: Builds the PRACTICE MISSIONS screen once at startup: backdrop root, TitledPanel {0x4d,0xa2,0x232,0x170} (estext 0xf0), mission list {6,0x1a,0xcf,0xad} with eight ESQuad rows (0xf2-0xf9), parameter box {0xd4,0x1a,0x1df,0xad} with five label buttons (0xfb-0xff), colons and readouts, and Main Menu / Begin Mission.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_Show
entries.description: Shows the practice screen's root and panel and calls PracticeScreen_SelectRow(0). PRACTICE MISSIONS' handler calls it.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_Hide
entries.description: Hides the practice screen's root and panel.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_SelectRow
entries.description: Practice row handler, called by PracticeScreen_OnRow0..PracticeScreen_OnRow7, with row 0 by PracticeScreen_Show, and with rows 8-10 by InstantAction_SelectDemo. No-op for the lit row (PracticeScreen_SelectedRow). Relights the rows through PracticeScreen_Rows, greys Herc Type for rows 0-3, writes the row's chassis from PracticeScreen_RowChassis into prefs option 0x28, refreshes the Herc Type readout, stores the row.

entries.name: InstantAction_SelectDemo
entries.description: INSTANT ACTION's pick: PracticeScreen_SelectRow(8 + option 0x2e), i.e. stage 0's DEMO/DEMO_01/DEMO_02 with the table's chassis, then steps option 0x2e mod 3, commits and saves the options.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_OnMainMenu
entries.description: Main Menu button: PracticeScreen_Hide, MainMenu_Show.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_OnBeginMission
entries.description: Begin Mission button: ShellOptions_Commit(1), ShellOptions_SaveAll, Game_NewCareer("TRAINEE", option 0x27).

entries.name: PracticeScreen_OnRow0
entries.description: Practice row 0's click handler, one of eight identical thunks in PracticeScreen_RowHandlers: PracticeScreen_SelectRow(0), then deletes the event (Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount into [005ddec0], virtual dtor +0x18 with 3).

entries.description: Practice row 1's click handler, one of eight identical thunks in PracticeScreen_RowHandlers: PracticeScreen_SelectRow(1), then deletes the event (Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount into [005ddec0], virtual dtor +0x18 with 3).

entries.name: ReplayDialog_Build
entries.description: Builds REPLAY MISSION?: a full-display ImagePanel of the shell backdrop (DAT_0048dbbc, no border), a TitledPanel {0xce,199,0x1b2,0x145} titled 0x134 (DAT_0048dbc0; face 0x25, dithered body in 0x10, plate 0x37-0xad), two centred lines (DAT_0048dbc4/dbc8) and Yes (0x139, ReplayDialog_OnYes) and No (0x13a, ReplayDialog_OnNo).

entries.name: ReplayDialog_Show
entries.description: (state) Writes the two lines -- 0 0x137/0x138 'The war is lost. Do you / want to replay the mission?', 3 0x135/0x136 'You were killed. ...' -- and shows the backdrop and the panel. Game_ProcessMissionResults calls it for game states 0 and 3.

entries.name: ReplayDialog_Hide
entries.description: Hides REPLAY MISSION?'s backdrop and panel.

entries.name: ReplayDialog_OnYes
entries.description: Yes: ReplayDialog_Hide, Game_LoadSlot(10), Shell_SetExitCode(2) and the quit flag, so the launcher flies data\ as the load left it. Its entry sits in bytes Ghidra left undefined; ESButtonFont_Ctor is passed it as a label.

entries.name: ReplayDialog_OnNo
entries.description: No: Game_SaveSlot(10), ReplayDialog_Hide, MainMenu_Show.

entries.name: EndOfGame_Build
entries.description: Builds CONTINUE GAME's END OF GAME ESAlert {0xcf,0xcb,0x1b4,0x12a} (DAT_0048dbd8), its two text lines and OKAY.

entries.name: EndOfGame_Show
entries.description: (state): first line from the game state (0 0x130, 1 0x131, 3 0x12f; any other left as it was), then Alert_Show.

entries.name: EndOfGame_Hide
entries.description: Alert_Hide on the END OF GAME alert.

entries.name: EndOfGame_OnOkay
entries.description: OKAY's handler: EndOfGame_Hide.

entries.name: LaunchRefusal_Build
entries.description: Builds Rock & Roll's WARNING! ESAlert {0xb1,0x67,0x1d2,0xc6}, its two text lines and OKAY.

entries.name: LaunchRefusal_Show
entries.description: Writes estext 0x13c+2*code and the next into the two lines and shows the alert.

entries.name: LaunchRefusal_HideAlert
entries.description: Alert_Hide(0048dbec). LaunchRefusal_OnOkay calls it.

entries.name: LaunchRefusal_OnOkay
entries.description: OKAY's handler: hides the alert.

entries.name: Career_LoadCurrentMission
entries.description: Loads the career's current mission (MsnGen_LoadMission); in campaign mode rebuilds the map and the briefing text and reshows the mission tab in the view it holds, in training exports the handoff and launches at once.

entries.name: MissionNameDialog_OnUseDefault
entries.description: Use Default: hides the dialog and calls Career_LoadCurrentMission.

entries.name: Msn_BuildPath
entries.description: Builds the msn\<name>.msn path string (format 'msn\\%s.msn', with '^' sanitized to '_') before loading a mission.

entries.name: MissionNameDialog_Show
entries.description: Writes the career position's mission name as the default and shows the dialog.

entries.name: MissionNameDialog_Hide
entries.description: Hides the mission-name dialog.

entries.description: (coder): reads a byte with LZHuffman_GetByte, takes the upper six bits and the extra bit count from the decode tables, reads those bits with LZHuffman_GetBit and returns the 12-bit position. LZHUF's DecodePosition; LZHRStream_Read calls it. The tables are 0047a780/0047a7c0 (encode) and 0047a800/0047a900 (decode). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047bd68.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044f874; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047bd68

entries.name: LZHuffman_EncodeEnd
entries.description: (coder): writes the top byte of the bit buffer (+0x13) when bits are pending (+0x15), then a zero byte. LZHUF's EncodeEnd with a trailing 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047bdbc.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044f8c8; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047bdbc

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetBit
entries.description: (coder): refills the 16-bit input buffer (+0x10, bit count +0x12) a byte at a time with Stream_ReadByte from the source (+0) while it holds fewer than 9 bits (0 at end of data), then shifts out and returns the top bit. LZHUF's GetBit. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047bdec.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044f8f8; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047bdec

entries.name: LZHuffman_GetByte
entries.description: (coder): LZHuffman_GetBit's refill, then shifts out and returns the top 8 bits. LZHUF's GetByte. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047be4c.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044f954; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047be4c

entries.name: LZHuffman_PutCode
entries.description: (coder, len, code): ORs the code's top len bits into the output buffer (+0x13, count +0x15) and writes each completed byte to the stream. LZHUF's Putcode. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047beac.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044f9b0; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047beac

entries.name: LZHuffman_Reconstruct
entries.description: (coder): rebuilds the adaptive Huffman tree: halves the leaf frequencies (+4), rebuilds the internal nodes in frequency order and relinks the parents (+8). LZHUF's reconst; LZHuffman_Update calls it when the root frequency reaches 0x8000. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047bf20.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044fa24; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047bf20

entries.name: LZHuffman_Update
entries.description: (coder, c): LZHuffman_Reconstruct when the root frequency is 0x8000, then increments the frequencies from leaf c to the root, swapping a node past its lower-frequency successors to keep the order. LZHUF's update. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047c054.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0044fb58; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047c054

entries.name: BuffWStream_Ctor
entries.description: BuffWStream constructor (vtable 0047aa0c, RTTI 'BuffWStream', 0x1e bytes): (this, size, buffer) Stream_BaseCtor, the vtable, 0044fcb8(this, size, buffer) to set up the buffer, and status 6 (no target attached).

entries.name: BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget
entries.description: BuffWStream constructor attached to a target stream: (this, target, size, buffer) Stream_BaseCtor, the vtable, 0044fcb8(this, size, buffer), then 0044fd54(this, target). ClassItem_StoreItem wraps a stream in one on its stack.

entries.name: BuffWStream_InitBuffer
entries.description: (stream, size, buffer): clears the target +8; size 0 means a growable 100-byte buffer (+0xc = 1), else size at +0xe with +0xc = 0; +0xd records whether the stream owns the buffer (buffer null), which it then Mem_HeapAlloc's; the buffer goes to +0x12. BuffWStream_Ctor and BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget call it.

entries.name: BuffWStream_Dtor
entries.description: BuffWStream vtable 0047aa0c slot 0 (stream, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, BuffWStream_Close, frees the buffer +0x12 when the stream owns it (+0xd), Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: BuffWStream_SetTarget
entries.description: (stream, target): BuffWStream_Close, stores target at +8, zeroes +0x16 and the buffered count +0x1a, then BuffWStream_SyncStatus. BuffWStream_CtorOnTarget calls it.

entries.name: BuffWStream_Close
entries.description: (stream): when a target is attached (+8), flushes through the stream's own vtable +0x10 (BuffWStream_Flush), clears the target and sets status 6. RLERStream_Close's counterpart for the write side.

entries.name: BuffWStream_GetCapabilities
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +0xc (stream, query): query 0 answers 0xe (the stream type), 1 and 3 answer 1, 2 and 4 answer 0.

entries.name: BuffWStream_GetPosition
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +4: the target's position (its vtable +4) plus the bytes buffered +0x1a; 0 when unattached (status 6).

entries.name: BuffWStream_SetPosition
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +8 (stream, pos), with status 0: moves the buffer cursor +0x1a to pos less the target's position when that lies between 0 and the buffer's high-water mark +0x16; otherwise returns 0.

entries.name: BuffWStream_Flush
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +0x10 (stream), with status 0: writes the buffered bytes (+0x1a of them, from the buffer +0x12) to the target +8 through 0044ffe8 and empties the buffer, returning 1; a failed write goes to 0044ff6c.

entries.name: BuffWStream_Write
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +0x14 (stream, count, src), with status 0: when count does not fit the space left in the buffer (+0xe less +0x1a), a stream whose grow flag +0xc is clear flushes (vtable +0x10) and writes src straight to the target (its vtable +0x14, a failure going to 0044ff6c), and one whose flag is set grows the buffer by the shortfall (0044ff1c) and carries on; otherwise copies src into the buffer at +0x1a, advances it and raises the high-water mark +0x16.

entries.name: BuffWStream_Read
entries.description: BuffWStream slot +0x18: sets status 4 and returns 0; the stream is write-only.

entries.name: BuffWStream_GrowBuffer
entries.description: (stream, extra): adds extra to the buffer size +0xe, rounds it up to a multiple of 100 and reallocs the buffer +0x12. BuffWStream_Write calls it for a growable buffer. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047c414.

entries.name: BuffWStream_SyncStatus
entries.description: (stream): status 6 (no target) when +8 is null, else the target's Stream_GetStatus. Returns 0. BuffRStream_SyncStatus's write-side twin. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047c464.

entries.name: Stream_WriteCopy
entries.description: (stream, count, buffer): calls the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14); a copy of Stream_Write in the BuffWStream unit. BuffWStream_Flush writes through it.

entries.name: BuffRStream_Ctor
entries.description: BuffRStream constructor (vtable 0047aa34, RTTI name 'BuffRStream', 0x21 bytes): (this, source, size, buffer) Stream_BaseCtor, installs the vtable, BuffRStream_InitBuffer(this, size, buffer) and BuffRStream_SetSource(this, source). Volume_LoadVolume builds one with no buffer of its own.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045003c; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: BuffRStream_Dtor
entries.description: BuffRStream vtable 0047aa34 slot 0 (stream, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, BuffRStream_ReleaseSource, frees the buffer +0x14 when the stream owns it (+0x18), Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: BuffRStream_InitBuffer
entries.description: (stream, size, buffer): clears +8, +0x10, +0x19 and +0x1d, stores size at +0xc and whether buffer is null at +0x18 (the stream owns it), and the buffer at +0x14 -- Mem_HeapAlloc(size) when none was passed.

entries.name: BuffRStream_SetSource
entries.description: (stream, source): when source differs from the current one (+8) first runs BuffRStream_ReleaseSource(stream); stores source at +8 and its vtable +4 answer at +0x10, clears +0x19 and +0x1d, then BuffRStream_SyncStatus(stream).

entries.name: BuffRStream_ReleaseSource
entries.description: (stream): when a source is attached (+8): calls the stream's own vtable +0x10, seeks the source (its vtable +8) to the position recorded at attach (+0x10) plus +0x1d, clears +8 and sets status 6. BuffRStream_SetSource runs it before attaching a different source.

entries.name: BuffRStream_GetCapabilities
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +0xc (stream, query): query 0 answers 0xd (the stream type), 2 and 3 answer 1, anything else 0.

entries.name: BuffRStream_GetPosition
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +4: the source position the buffer starts at (+0x10) plus the cursor in it (+0x1d), while attached; else 0.

entries.name: BuffRStream_SetPosition
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +8 (stream, pos): clears an end-of-data status (2); with status 0, a position inside the buffered window (+0x10 to +0x10 plus the filled count +0x19) only moves the cursor +0x1d; any other goes to 004502bc(stream, pos).

entries.name: BuffRStream_Flush
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +0x10: returns whether a source is attached (status other than 6). BuffRStream_ReleaseSource calls it before detaching.

entries.name: BuffRStream_Read
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +0x18 (stream, count, dst), with status 0: copies from the buffer +0x14 at the cursor +0x1d; while the request runs past the filled count +0x19 it copies what is left, moves the window on to its end with 004502bc and carries on, returning 0 when that fails.

entries.name: BuffRStream_Write
entries.description: BuffRStream slot +0x14: sets status 4 and returns 0.

entries.name: BuffRStream_FillAt
entries.description: (stream, pos): seeks the source (+8, its vtable +8) to pos and reads a buffer's worth (+0xc) into the buffer +0x14 with Stream_ReadCopy3; a short read at the source's end of data keeps what came (the count at +0x19), or sets status 2 when nothing did. On success the window starts at pos (+0x10) with the cursor +0x1d at 0 and it returns 1; a failed seek or read returns BuffRStream_SyncStatus. BuffRStream_SetPosition and BuffRStream_Read call it.

entries.name: BuffRStream_SyncStatus
entries.description: (stream): sets the status word +4 to 6 (no source attached) when the source +8 is null, else to the source's Stream_GetStatus. Returns 0. BuffRStream_SetSource ends with it.

entries.name: Stream_GetStatus
entries.description: Returns a stream's status word at +4. Stream status codes at +4 seen in these classes: 0 ok, 1 I/O error, 2 end of data, 3 close failed, 4 write to a read-only stream, 5 no file, 6 filter stream not attached.

entries.name: Stream_ReadCopy3
entries.description: (stream, count, buffer): calls the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a copy of Stream_Read in the BuffRStream unit. BuffRStream_FillAt reads through it.

entries.name: Str_TrimRight
entries.description: (s): cuts s after its last character above a space (code > 0x20), dropping trailing blanks and control characters; returns s. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's 0047d058.

entries.name: Path_Split
entries.description: (path, drive, dir, name, ext): clears each non-null output, then splits path: a leading 'X:' into drive, everything up to and including the last backslash into dir, then the name up to the first '.' into name and the rest, dot included, into ext (all of it into name when there is no dot). Volume_FindEntry splits its lookup path with it.

entries.name: Str_Concat4
entries.description: (a, b, c, d, out): concatenates the non-null strings a to d into out, or into the static buffer 0048e057 when out is null, and returns it. Volume_FindEntry builds its names with it.

entries.name: Math_Atan2Bam
entries.description: VSHELL's copy of DBSIM's Math_Atan2Bam (0047d220): atan2(y=param_2, x=param_1) in BAM.

entries.name: Math_AsinBam
entries.description: Arcsine of a Q14 sine as a binary angle: below 0xe00 * 4 the coarse table at 0047ac5c, above it the fine table at 004793dc, the sign restored at the end. 0042bc4e calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_AsinBam (0047d940).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00450684; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047d940

entries.name: DotProductVec3Short
entries.description: a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y + a.z*b.z of two int16 triples, unscaled. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's DotProductVec3Short.

entries.name: DotProductVec3Int
entries.description: (a, b): the int32 dot product a.x*b.x + a.y*b.y + a.z*b.z. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's DotProductVec3Int.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64
entries.description: (out{quotient, remainder}, int64 *n, d): IDIV of n by d, storing n / d and n % d as two int32s; returns out. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_DivMod64.

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude2D
entries.description: (dx, dy): max(|dx|,|dy|) + min(|dx|,|dy|)/2, the octagonal estimate. TSBSPPart_RenderNode calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_FastMagnitude2D (0047dd40).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045085c; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047dd40

entries.name: Math_FastMagnitude3D
entries.description: VSHELL's copy of DBSIM's Math_FastMagnitude3D: L + M*0.34375 + S*0.25.

entries.name: Transform_TransposeRotation
entries.description: Transposes a transform's rotation in place (swaps +2/+4, +8/+0xc, +0xa/+0xe), which inverts a pure rotation.

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64
entries.description: (out int64, a, b): IMUL into EDX:EAX, stores the 64-bit product a * b and returns out. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_Mul32To64.

entries.name: Math_ISqrt
entries.description: (n) -> floor(sqrt(n)) for unsigned n, bit by bit: BSR for the top bit, then trial additions of halving powers of two against the running square. 0 for 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_ISqrt (0047de90).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00450970; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047de90

entries.name: Math_CosBam
entries.description: Cosine of a 16-bit binary angle in Q14: rounds the angle to a 16-BAM step ((a >> 4) + bit 3), takes its magnitude, and reads the quarter-turn table at 0047b3e4 directly below 0x400 and negated as table[0x800 - i] above. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_CosBam (0047dee4). TSBounds_ScreenVisibility and 0042bc4e call it.

entries.name: FixedDivQ16
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point divide, ((int64)a << 16) / b.

entries.name: FixedMulQ16Copy
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 16: byte-identical to FixedMulQ16, which follows it. 0045add8 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_Q16Multiply2 (0047df71), which sits in the same place before its own Q16, Q8, Q10 and Q14 multiplies.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00450a51; es2_naming.py match against DBSIM

entries.name: FixedMulQ16
entries.description: Q16 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 16. TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB calls it at 59 sites.

entries.name: FixedMulQ8
entries.description: Q8 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 8.

entries.name: FixedMulQ10
entries.description: Q10 fixed-point multiply, (a * b) >> 10 through a 64-bit intermediate. The scale step behind every value damage.dat expands.

entries.name: FixedMulQ14
entries.description: (int a, int16 b): Q14 fixed-point multiply, (int64)a*b >> 14, after FixedMulQ16, FixedMulQ8 and FixedMulQ10. 004657e1 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_Q14Multiply (0047dfb4).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00450a94; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047dfb4

entries.name: Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect (0047e504), the same computation: (plane{nx,ny,nz,d}, segment{start[3],end[3]}, out[3]) -> bool, applying the parameter per component through Math_Mul32To64_Thunk and Math_DivMod64_Thunk.

entries.name: Poly_SplitByPlane
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Poly_SplitByPlane (0047e630), the same code: (plane, poly, front, back) -> bool, through Plane_ClassifyPoint (004514c8) and Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect (00450fe0). Its two callers, 00467920 and 00467ac4, clip against up to six planes chosen by bits 0x02-0x40 of the object's +8 flags, keeping front each time and swapping the in and out lists with Dword_Swap.

entries.name: Math_Mul32To64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_Mul32To64 that returns its out pointer. Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect calls it once per component. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_Mul32To64_Thunk.

entries.name: Math_DivMod64_Thunk
entries.description: Forwarder to Math_DivMod64 that returns its out pointer. Math_PlaneSegmentIntersect calls it once per component. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_DivMod64_Thunk.

entries.name: Point3IPair_Ctor
entries.description: (p): runs maybe_Point3I_Ctor on p and p+0xc -- two int32 triples. Poly_SplitByPlane calls it on a local.

entries.name: Plane_ClassifyPoint
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Plane_ClassifyPoint (0047e9ec): 1, 0 or -1 as dot(n, point) is above, on or below -d, the dot product through DotProductVec3Int_Thunk (0045f71d).

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2D
entries.description: (angle, out): builds a 2x2 Q14 rotation for a binary angle into short[4] {cos, sin, -sin, cos}, looking up the table at 0047b3e4 with the angle >> 4 rounded. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_BuildRotation2D.

entries.name: BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14
entries.description: (euler short[3], out): builds a 3x3 Q14 rotation matrix plus a mode byte from three binary-angle Euler angles through the sine table, with a fast path when angles are zero. TSBSPPart_RenderNode and BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14_Thunk call it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's BuildEulerRotationMatrixQ14 (0047eaac).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00451588; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047eaac

entries.name: Transform_Concat
entries.description: (a, b, out): composes two transforms so that out applies a then b: rotation out = a.rot then b.rot (Q14, rank-byte fast paths), translation out = b.rot(a.t) + b.t. Same routine as DBSIM's Transform_Concat.

entries.name: Math_RotateVec2Q14
entries.description: 2D vector through a Q14 2x2 matrix, each component (sum + 0x2000) >> 14.

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint
entries.description: (point int[2], m short[4], out int[2]): out.x = (x*m0 + y*m2 + 0x2000) >> 14, out.y = (x*m1 + y*m3 + 0x2000) >> 14 with 64-bit intermediates. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_Rotate2DPoint (0047fedc). ShellMap_PaintRelief calls it.

entries.name: Transform2D_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point int[2], xf, out int[2]): out = the point through the 2x2 Q14 matrix at xf (rounded by +0x2000 >> 14) plus the int translation at xf+8/+0xc. 0042b7c7 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Transform2D_ApplyToPoint (0047ff44).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00452058; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 0047ff44

entries.name: RotateVectorByMatrixQ14
entries.description: (v int16[3], transform, out int16[3]): the rotation alone, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding, by the rank byte +0x12: 0 or below copies v, 1 rotates the XY block and passes z through, otherwise the full 3x3. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's RotateVectorByMatrixQ14.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToShortPoint
entries.description: (point int16[3], transform, out int32[3]): Q14 with +0x2000 rounding plus the translation (+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c), by the rank byte +0x12: 0 or below translation only, 1 the XY block with z passed through, otherwise the full 3x3. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Transform_ApplyToShortPoint. Poly_ProjectShapeVerticesPerspective and Transform_ApplyToShortPoint_Thunk call it.

entries.name: Transform_RotatePoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out): Transform_ApplyToPoint without the translation, i.e. the rotation alone, with the same rank-byte fast paths.

entries.name: Transform_ApplyToPoint
entries.description: (point, transform, out): transforms an int32 point, Q14 with +0x2000 rounding and 64-bit intermediates, then adds the translation; the rank byte picks translation-only, Z-rotation or full 3x3 arithmetic. Same routine as DBSIM's Transform_ApplyToPoint. A transform is 0x20 bytes: nine int16 Q14 rotation terms (+0 the XY 2x2 block x->x, x->y, y->x, y->y; +8 x->z, y->z; +0xc z->x, z->y; +0x10 z->z), a rank byte at +0x12 (0 translation only, 1 Z rotation only, 2 full 3x3) and int32 translation x, y, z at +0x14/+0x18/+0x1c.

entries.name: GL_ClaimGlobal
entries.description: (this, index, instance): clears this+0 and stores instance at 0048e160 + index*4 when that GL global is still empty, so the first object constructed for an index becomes GL_GetGlobal(index)'s. GLDisplay_Ctor claims index 7, the current display. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GL_ClaimGlobal (00480484).

entries.name: GL_SetGlobal
entries.description: (index, value): stores value at 0048e160 + index*4 and returns 0, unless value is non-null and the slot already holds one, when it stores nothing and returns 1. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GL_SetGlobal (004804a8).

entries.name: GLViewport_Ctor
entries.description: GLViewport constructor (vtable 0047bc28, RTTI name 'GLViewport', 0x239 bytes, over GLBase 0047e986): initialises its sub-objects at +0x210 (0045fb27) and +0x220, then copies the viewport held at GL_GetGlobal7()+0x40 (0x81 dwords of state from +4, then the fields at +0x208..+0x22c), and clears +0x230, +0x231 and +0x235. Map_Ctor's drawing context at +4 is one.

entries.name: Gfx_SetCurrentContext
entries.description: Makes a drawing context current: stores it at 0048e184 and binds its clip block at +4 (00452993, 00459908).

entries.name: GLViewport_Dtor
entries.description: GLViewport vtable 0047bc28 slot +0x18, the destructor (viewport, flags): decrements the live-object counter at *005ddec0, GLBase_Dtor(viewport, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Map_Dtor deletes the camera's context through this slot. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: GL_GetPtr40
entries.description: Returns the dword at +0x40 of its argument. GLViewport_Ctor calls it on GL_GetGlobal7's object to find the viewport it copies.

entries.name: GLDisplay_SetClipBlock
entries.description: (display, block): stores block at display+0x44 and, when display is GLDisplay_GetCurrent's current one, installs it with Gfx_SetClipBlock. Gfx_SetCurrentContext calls it.

entries.name: GL_RegisterClassItems
entries.description: Static initialiser: ClassItem_RegisterBucket(0047bcd0, [0047bd3c]), the GL class-item table. Display_Init calls it first. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GL_RegisterClassItems (00480de8).

entries.name: GLBase_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLBase vtable 0047e986 slot 0, the class-item tag getter's default: returns -1. GLPrimitive, GLRegion and GLViewport keep it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 004529cc; identical after normalisation to DBSIM 00480dfc

entries.name: GLBase_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLBase vtable 0047e986 slot +4, default: returns 0.

entries.name: GLBase_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLBase vtable 0047e986 slot +8, default: returns 0.

entries.name: GLBase_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLBase vtable 0047e986 slot +0xc, default: does nothing.

entries.name: GLBase_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLBase vtable 0047e986 slot +0x10, default: does nothing.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Ctor
entries.description: (display, kindName): GL_ClaimGlobal(display, 7, display), so the first display built becomes the current one; registers an assert hook and an atexit handler, clears flags +0 and stores GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName(kindName) at +0x30. Does not open the display. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_Ctor; the shell map builds its 'BMP_8' displays with it.

entries.name: GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen
entries.description: (display, kindName, bitmapHeader): GLDisplay_Ctor's body followed by GLDisplay_Open(display, bitmapHeader). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_CtorAndOpen.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Dtor
entries.description: (display, flags): GLDisplay_Close(display), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_Dtor.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Open
entries.description: (display, bitmapHeader): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_Open: once ever GLDisplay_FirstOpenNoOp (counter 0047bc44), then RasterDriver_OpenDisplay with the driver id +0x30, bitmapHeader and display+4; on success two 0x22c-byte clip blocks at +0x40 and +0x44 initialised for the display's size by ClipBlock_Init, +0x34..+0x3c zeroed, flags bit 0 set, returns 1; 0 when already open or on failure.

entries.name: GLDisplay_Close
entries.description: (display): GLDisplay_Open's inverse, the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_Close: when open, frees the clip block +0x40, clears the flags, RasterDriver_CloseDisplay(driver id +0x30, display+4), and decrements the open count 0047bc44, running GLDisplay_LastCloseNoOp when it reaches 0. Returns 0.

entries.name: Gfx_SelectRenderTarget
entries.description: (display): returns 1 when 00452fb9 reports a current display and 00452fe8 returns nonzero; otherwise 00452ff5(display) and 00459756, copies display +4..+0x2c to 0047c3e6.., calls the three page routines at 0047e588, 0047e580 and 0047e584 with +0x34, +0x38 and +0x3c, 00459878(+0x40) and Gfx_SetClipBlock(+0x44), and returns 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_SelectRenderTarget. ShellMap_BuildRelief calls it.

entries.name: GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName
entries.description: (display, name): looks name up in the table at 0047bca0 ('VGA_8', 'VGA_4', 'BMP_8') and returns the driver id from 0047bcac: 1, 0 or 3; 4 for an unknown name. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_DriverIdFromName.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00452d90; tables at 0047bca0 and 0047bcac

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetAttribute
entries.description: (display, which): the same jump table as DBSIM's GLDisplay_GetAttribute (00481244), with the globals for 5, 8 and 0x10 at 0047e539, 0047dd35 and 0047c422. Every direct call site passes GL_GetGlobal7's object (0048e17c) with 0 then 1, the screen width and height: WinWin95Display_Ctor builds the rect {0, 0, width, height} from them and WinMouseProducer_SetCentre halves them for the screen centre.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile and disassembly at 00452df0 and its three callers

entries.name: GLDisplay_SetAttribute
entries.description: (display, which, value): the setter twin of GLDisplay_GetAttribute, the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_SetAttribute: 9/10/11 store +0x1c/+0x20/+0x24 (mirrored to 0047c3fe/0047c402/0047c406 for the current display), 2 calls 0047e55c(value, display+4) and re-copies +0x28/+0x2c to 0047c40a/0047c40e, 0x10 stores 0047c422, 0x11 calls 0047e5c0(value). Returns 1, or 0 for any other which.

entries.name: GLDisplay_GetCurrent
entries.description: GL_GetGlobal(7): the current display. A second copy of GL_GetGlobal7 (0045f741), called by Gfx_SelectRenderTarget and GLDisplay_SetClipBlock. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLDisplay_GetCurrent (00481411).

entries.name: GL_ClearGlobal7
entries.description: GL_SetGlobal7(0). Gfx_SelectRenderTarget calls it.

entries.name: GL_SetGlobal7
entries.description: (value): GL_SetGlobal(7, value). Gfx_SelectRenderTarget installs its display with it.

entries.name: GLBitmap_Ctor
entries.description: GLBitmap constructor (vtable 0047be58, RTTI name 'GLBitmap', 0x1a bytes, over GLPrimitive 0047be84 and GLBase 0047e986): clears the data size +0xa, the data pointer +0xe, +0x14 and +0x16. The compression type is the word at +0x12 (0 raw, 1 RLE, 3 LZH).

entries.name: GLBitmap_Dtor
entries.description: GLBitmap destructor (vtable 0047be58, RTTI name 'GLBitmap', 0x1a bytes): (bmp, flags) reinstalls the vtable, Mem_DeleteArray of +0x16 when the int16 +0x14 is non-zero and of +0xe when +0xa is non-zero, GLBase_Dtor(bmp, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. ShellMap_BuildRelief runs it on a local with flags 2.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00453054; RTTI at vtable-0xc

entries.name: GLBitmap_Draw
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags): hands the bitmap at +4 to the blit (0045421f, which calls Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch) with GL_GetGlobal7. A compressed bitmap (+0x12 nonzero) is first unpacked by GLBitmap_Decompress into the buffer at 0048e18c, which stands in for the data pointer (+0xe) and size (+0xa) for the call; the buffer is then freed unless 0048e188 is set. ESGrid_Paint, ESBitmap_Paint, ShellMap_PaintIcon and ShellMap_PaintNavMarkers draw through it.

entries.name: GLBitmap_DrawScaled
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags, size): GLBitmap_Draw's scaled twin, handing the bitmap at +4 to 004536eb with an extra size argument, with the same GLBitmap_Decompress path for a compressed bitmap. ShellMap_PaintIcon and TSBitmapPart_Render draw through it.

entries.name: GLBitmap_DrawStretched
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flip, size, angle): GLBitmap_DrawScaled's shape for a stretched and rotated draw, handing the bitmap at +4 and all four arguments to GLDisplay_DrawBitmapStretched (and so Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled) with GL_GetGlobal7's display, through GLBitmap_Decompress first for a compressed bitmap (+0x12). ShellMap_PaintRelief stretches the relief bitmap with it.

entries.name: GLBitmap_Decompress
entries.description: Unpacks a compressed GLBitmap: the data at +0xe starts with the unpacked size, followed by [+0xa] - 4 packed bytes. Allocates the unpacked size into 0048e18c with Mem_NewArray, wraps the packed bytes in a MemRWStream, reads it through an RLERStream (compression 1) or LZHRStream (compression 3) into the buffer, and returns the size. Any other compression type, or 0048e188 set, returns 0 without unpacking.

entries.name: RLERStream_Dtor
entries.description: RLERStream vtable 0047a70c slot 0 (stream, flags): decrements *005ddec0, Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here, which is why the dump's table at 0047a710 starts one slot late.

entries.name: MemRWStream_Dtor
entries.description: MemRWStream vtable 0047a6e4 slot 0 (stream, flags): decrements *005ddec0, Stream_BaseDtor(stream, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here, which is why the dump's table at 0047a6e8 starts one slot late.

entries.name: GLDisplay_DrawBitmapScaled
entries.description: (display, bitmap, position, flags, size): Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch(bitmap, position, flags, size); display is not read. GLBitmap_DrawScaled calls it with GL_GetGlobal7's display.

entries.name: GLDisplay_DrawBitmapStretched
entries.description: (display, bitmapDims, position, flip, size, angle): Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled(bitmapDims, position, flip, size, angle); display is not read. GLBitmap_DrawStretched calls it with GL_GetGlobal7's display, as GLBitmap_DrawScaled does GLDisplay_DrawBitmapScaled.

entries.name: GLBitmap_DrawAtOrigin
entries.description: GLBitmap vtable 0047be58 slot +0x1c, the draw: GLBitmap_DrawUnflipped at {0, 0} in the current context. Every widget paint draws its face and frame bitmaps through this slot, after Window_BeginPaint has set the context to the widget's rect.

entries.name: GLBitmap_DrawUnflipped
entries.description: (bitmap, point): GLBitmap_Draw(bitmap, point, 0). The GLBitmap counterpart of DBSIM's Bitmap_BlitUnflipped.

entries.name: GLBitmap_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x28000e 'GLBitmap': 0x1a bytes from the arena DAT_00481244, GLBitmap_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read with (stream, mode). Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: OldGLBitmap_Construct
entries.description: The load function VSHELL's GL class-item table (0047bcd0) registers for tag 0x280000 'Old GLBitmap': returns 0, so an item in the old bitmap format loads as nothing.

entries.name: GLBitmap_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLBitmap vtable 0047be58 slot 0: returns 0x28000e, GLBitmap_Construct's tag.

entries.name: GLBitmap_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLBitmap slot +4: 0xd for the header GLBitmap_ReadFromStream reads, plus the data size +0xa and 4 per entry of the +0x14 array.

entries.name: GLBitmap_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLBitmap slot +8: the same sum with base 0x1a, the object's size.

entries.name: GLBitmap_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLBitmap slot +0xc (bitmap, stream): the 13-byte bitmap header, then its blocks: int16 width +4 and height +6, a byte into +8, a byte whose low nibble and bit 4 replace those of +9 (the bitmap type Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch tests), the compression byte into the word +0x12 (0 raw, 1 RLE, 3 LZH); clears +0xe and +0x16; the uint32 data size +0xa and the int16 count +0x14; then the data into an arena block at +0xe and count * 4 bytes at +0x16. DBSIM's 00481c80 reads the same.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00453838; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00453838 DBSIM 00481c80; the .DCI files' embedded bitmaps

entries.name: GLBitmap_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLBitmap slot +0x10 (bitmap, stream): writes the header and blocks GLBitmap_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order.

entries.name: Stream_ReadByte
entries.description: (stream, dst): reads 1 byte through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18). GLBitmap_ReadFromStream reads its flag and compression bytes with it, where DBSIM's GLBitmap read calls DBSIM's Stream_ReadByte.

entries.name: Stream_WriteByte
entries.description: (stream, value): writes the low byte of its value argument through the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14). GLBitmap_WriteToStream writes its flag and compression bytes with it.

entries.name: GLPalette_Dtor
entries.description: GLPalette vtable 0047bf10 slot +0x18 (palette, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the array +8 when the int16 +4 is non-zero, and when +0xc is non-zero frees the first dword of each of its 8-byte entries at +0x10 and then the array; GLBase_Dtor(palette, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: Palette_ApplyToDisplay
entries.description: (palette): 00453b63(GL_GetGlobal7's display, palette's int16 +0xe, int16 +0xc, entries +0x10), then 00406c4d(palette). Shell_CommitPalette runs it on CurrentPaletteHandle.

entries.name: GLPalette_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x28000f 'GLPalette': 0x14 bytes from the arena, GLPalette_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read.

entries.name: GLPalette_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLPalette vtable 0047bf10 slot 0: returns 0x28000f, GLPalette_Construct's tag.

entries.name: GLPalette_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLPalette slot +4: 8 + 4 per colour (+4) + (count + 1) * 2 per table of +0x10.

entries.name: GLPalette_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLPalette slot +8: the same sum with base 0x14.

entries.name: GLPalette_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLPalette slot +0xc (palette, stream): the colour count +4 and the int16 +6, then 4 bytes per colour into an arena block at +8; the table count +0xc and the int16 +0xe, then for each table an int16 length and that many int16s into an arena block, recorded as {block, length} 8-byte entries at +0x10.

entries.name: GLPalette_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLPalette slot +0x10 (palette, stream): writes what GLPalette_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order.

entries.name: GLPalette_Ctor
entries.description: GLPalette constructor (vtable 0047bf10, RTTI 'GLPalette', 0x14 bytes): stamps ClassItem, GLBase and its own vtable, and clears the colour count +4 and the table count +0xc. GLPalette_Construct runs it.

entries.name: GLFont_Dtor
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot +0x18 (font, flags): decrements the live-object counter at *005ddec0, restores GLFont_Vtable, frees each block GLFont_ReadFromStream allocated (+0x1e when +0x18 is non-zero, +0x22 when +0x1a is, +0x26 when +4 is, +0x2a when +0xc is -1, +0x2e when +8 is -1) with Mem_DeleteArray, GLBase_Dtor(font, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: Font_GlyphWidth
entries.description: One glyph's advance: the per-glyph width table at font +0x2a indexed by the character less font +0x08, unless font +0x0c holds a fixed width other than -1.

entries.name: Font_MeasureString
entries.description: Sums Font_GlyphWidth over a string, with no tracking. What right and centred alignment subtract from the field width.

entries.name: Font_CellHeightCopy
entries.description: Returns the int16 at font+0x0a, the glyph cell height: a byte-identical second copy of Font_CellHeight. Font_DrawGlyph calls it.

entries.name: Font_CellHeight
entries.description: Returns font +0x0a, the glyph cell height. Font_CellHeightCopy is a byte-identical second copy at a different address. Both text paints centre with this, not with the ink height -- which is font +0x16 and is what the glyph blitter subtracts.

entries.name: Font_DrawGlyph
entries.description: Blits one glyph, placing its top-left at { x, y - font[+0x16] } -- and font +0x16 is the .DFN header's inkHeight field, so the caller's y is an ink baseline rather than a top or a cell bottom.

entries.name: Font_DrawString
entries.description: Draws a run of glyphs. Tests the draw context's +0x231 for 1 and then 2, so alignment is 0 left, 1 right, 2 centred against the field width at +0x235; then advances glyph by glyph. The y it is given is an ink baseline.

entries.name: GL_Blit
entries.description: (context, bitmapData, point, flags): drops the context and calls Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch(bitmapData, point, flags). GLBitmap_Draw and Font_DrawGlyph reach the blitter through it.

entries.name: GLFont_Construct
entries.description: The class-item load function VSHELL's GL class-item table (0047bcd0) registers for tag 0x280005 'GLFont': (stream, mode) Arena_Alloc's 0x32 bytes from the arena DAT_00481244, stamps the ClassItem, GLBase and GLFont vtables in turn (0047f834, 0047e986, GLFont_Vtable), then calls the object's vtable +0xc read (GLFont_ReadFromStream) with (stream, mode) and returns the object. VshellClassItem_LoadItem reaches it through the registry entry's loadFn.

entries.name: OldGLFont_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x280003 'Old GLFont': returns 0, so an item in the old font format loads as nothing.

entries.name: GLFont_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot 0, the class-item tag getter: returns 0x280005, the tag VSHELL's GL class-item table (0047bcd0) registers GLFont_Construct under and every .DFN file's type tag carries. The class is GLFont by its RTTI record and by that table's name string.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 004542d0; vtable 0047bf68 (RTTI GLFont); GL class-item table entry 0047bd0c

entries.name: GLFont_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot +4 (font): 0x1a for the header GLFont_ReadFromStream reads, plus the pool length +0x1a, 4 per glyph (+4) for the offsets, 4 per entry of the +0x18 array, another 4 per glyph when +0xc is -1 and 4 per +6 entry when +8 is -1. For those last two blocks GLFont_ReadFromStream reads 1 byte per glyph and 2 per entry, so the getter overstates them.

entries.name: GLFont_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot +8: GLFont_GetStreamSize's sum with base 0x32, the object's size, in place of the 0x1a header.

entries.name: GLFont_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot +0x10 (font, stream): writes the fields GLFont_ReadFromStream reads, in the same order and with the same block sizes, including the count << 2 passed to Stream_WriteDwords for the +0x18 array.

entries.name: GLFont_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLFont vtable 0047bf68 slot +0xc (font, stream): reads the .DFN header, eleven int16s into +4..+0x18 and the pool length into +0x1a, then the variable blocks into arena allocations: the +0x18 array (Stream_ReadDwords with count << 2, which reads count * 16 bytes into a count * 4 allocation; GLFont_GetStreamSize counts count * 4, and every retail file has count 0), the glyph pool (+0x1a bytes) to +0x22, the glyph offsets (+4 dwords) to +0x26, the glyph widths (+4 bytes) to +0x2a when +0xc is -1, and +6 words to +0x2e when +8 is -1. Layout: docs/formats/dfn-hfn-dci.md. Identical up to helper names to DBSIM's 00482908.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile and disassembly of 00454474; es2_naming.py diff VSHELL 00454474 DBSIM 00482908

entries.name: Stream_Read
entries.description: (stream, count, buffer): calls the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18).

entries.name: Stream_Write
entries.description: (stream, count, buffer): calls the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14).

entries.name: Stream_WriteDwordsCopy
entries.description: (stream, count, src): writes count * 4 bytes through the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14); a second copy of Stream_WriteDwords (00460eb0). GLFont_WriteToStream calls it.

entries.name: Stream_ReadDwordsCopy
entries.description: (stream, count, dst): reads count * 4 bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18); a second copy of Stream_ReadDwords (00460ecc). GLFont_ReadFromStream calls it.

entries.name: GLPrimitive_Draw
entries.description: GLPrimitive vtable 0047be84 slot +0x1c, the draw: does nothing. GLBitmap overrides it with GLBitmap_DrawAtOrigin.

entries.name: GL_DrawLine
entries.description: (gl, from, to): Gfx_DrawLine(from, to), ignoring the first argument. Font_DrawGlyph calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GL_DrawLine (00482c38).

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x280001 'GLBitmapArray': 0xc bytes from the arena, GLBitmapArray_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLBitmapArray vtable 0047c0a8 slot 0: returns 0x280001, GLBitmapArray_Construct's tag.

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLBitmapArray slot +4: 4 for the count plus ClassItem_ItemTotalSize of each bitmap; 0 as soon as one reports 0.

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLBitmapArray slot +8: 0xc + 4 per bitmap, plus each bitmap's GetMemorySize.

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLBitmapArray slot +0xc (array, stream): the uint32 frame count +4, an arena array of that many pointers at +8, and each frame loaded with VshellClassItem_LoadItem(stream, 0): the frame table a .DBA's users index (array +8, count +4).

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLBitmapArray slot +0x10 (array, stream): the count, then each frame through ClassItem_StoreItem.

entries.name: Stream_WriteDword
entries.description: (stream, value): writes its 4-byte value argument through the stream's write slot (vtable +0x14).

entries.name: Stream_ReadDword
entries.description: (stream, dst): reads 4 bytes through the stream's read slot (vtable +0x18).

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_Ctor
entries.description: GLBitmapArray constructor (vtable 0047c0a8, RTTI 'GLBitmapArray', 0xc bytes, over ClassItem): stamps the vtables and runs 004549e0(this, 0, 0). GLBitmapArray_Construct runs it.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x28000c 'GLRectangleRegion': 0x18 bytes from the arena, GLRectangleRegion_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion vtable 0047c020 slot 0: returns 0x28000c, GLRectangleRegion_Construct's tag.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion slot +4: returns 0x10, the rect.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion slot +8: returns 0x18, the object's size.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion slot +0xc (region, stream): reads the 16-byte rect into +8.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion slot +0x10 (region, stream): writes the rect +8.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x28000d 'GLEdgeTableRegion': 0xc bytes from the arena, GLEdgeTableRegion_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion vtable 0047c14c slot 0: returns 0x28000d, GLEdgeTableRegion_Construct's tag.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion slot +4: with a table (+8), 4 + 4 per entry (the table's int16 count at +2); without one, 2.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion slot +8: with a table, 0x14 + 4 per entry beyond the first; without one, 0xc.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion slot +0xc (region, stream): an int16 count; 0 leaves no table, otherwise an arena table of 8 + 4 per entry beyond the first at +8 with the count at its +2, an int16 into its +0 and count * 2 int16s from its +4 (Stream_ReadWordsCopy).

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion slot +0x10 (region, stream): a count of 0 when there is no table or it is empty; otherwise the count, the table's +0 and its entries (Stream_WriteWordsCopy).

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_Ctor
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion constructor (vtable 0047c020, RTTI 'GLRectangleRegion', 0x18 bytes, over GLRegion and GLBase): stamps ClassItem, GLBase, GLRegion and its own vtable, constructs the rect at +8 (RectI_Ctor) and sets the region type +4 to 0. GLRectangleRegion_Construct runs it.

entries.name: GLRectangleRegion_Dtor
entries.description: GLRectangleRegion vtable 0047c020 slot +0x18 (region, flags): decrements *005ddec0 twice (its own level and GLRegion's), GLBase_Dtor(region, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: GLCursor_Construct
entries.description: The load function the GL class-item table registers for tag 0x28000b 'GLCursor': 0x10 bytes from the arena, GLCursor_Ctor, then the object's vtable +0xc read. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: GLCursor_GetClassTag
entries.description: GLCursor vtable 0047c0fc slot 0: returns 0x28000b, GLCursor_Construct's tag and the .DCI files' type tag.

entries.name: GLCursor_GetStreamSize
entries.description: GLCursor slot +4: 8 for the hotspot plus ClassItem_ItemTotalSize of the bitmap at +4; 0 when that is 0.

entries.name: GLCursor_GetMemorySize
entries.description: GLCursor slot +8: 0x10 plus the bitmap's GetMemorySize.

entries.name: GLCursor_ReadFromStream
entries.description: GLCursor slot +0xc (cursor, stream): the 8-byte hotspot {x, y} into +8, then one class item, the cursor's bitmap, into +4 (VshellClassItem_LoadItem). See docs/formats/dfn-hfn-dci.md for the .DCI layout.

entries.name: GLCursor_WriteToStream
entries.description: GLCursor slot +0x10 (cursor, stream): the hotspot, then the bitmap through ClassItem_StoreItem.

entries.name: GLBitmapArray_Dtor
entries.description: GLBitmapArray destructor (vtable 0047c0a8, RTTI name 'GLBitmapArray', 0xc bytes): deletes each bitmap in the array at +8 (count +4) through its virtual destructor, frees the array with Mem_DeleteArray and the object when flag & 1.

entries.name: GLCursor_Ctor
entries.description: GLCursor constructor (vtable 0047c0fc, RTTI 'GLCursor', 0x10 bytes, over GLBase): stamps ClassItem, GLBase and its own vtable, constructs the hotspot at +8 (Rtl_ReturnArg) and clears the bitmap +4. GLCursor_Construct runs it. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: GLCursor_Dtor
entries.description: GLCursor vtable 0047c0fc slot +0x18 (cursor, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, deletes the bitmap +4 through its vtable +0x18 with 3, GLBase_Dtor(cursor, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's GLCursor_Dtor (004834bc).

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_Ctor
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion constructor (vtable 0047c14c, RTTI 'GLEdgeTableRegion', 0xc bytes, over GLRegion and GLBase): stamps ClassItem, GLBase, GLRegion and its own vtable, sets the region type +4 to 2 and clears the table +8. GLEdgeTableRegion_Construct runs it.

entries.name: GLEdgeTableRegion_Dtor
entries.description: GLEdgeTableRegion vtable 0047c14c slot +0x18 (region, flags): decrements *005ddec0, restores the vtable, frees the table +8 when set, decrements once more for GLRegion, GLBase_Dtor(region, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set.

entries.name: GLRegion_Dtor
entries.description: GLRegion vtable 0047c124 slot +0x18 (region, flags): decrements *005ddec0, GLBase_Dtor(region, 0), then Mem_Delete when flags bit 0 is set. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: Gfx_DrawLine
entries.description: Draws a one-pixel line between two inclusive {x, y} endpoints in the pen colour at context +0x228. The shell asks for horizontal, vertical and 45-degree runs only.

entries.name: Line_ClipToRect
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Line_ClipToRect, line for line: clips a-b in place against the inclusive rect {x0, y0, x1, y1}, returning 0 when the segment is wholly beyond one bound. Gfx_DrawLine clips through it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045554c, diffed against DBSIM 00483b60

entries.name: Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Line_ScanConvertToSpanRegion, line for line: the int16 span region {top, count, {x0, x1} per row} of a one-pixel Bresenham line. Gfx_DrawLine fills the result.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045564c, diffed against DBSIM 00483c60

entries.name: Gfx_FillPolygon
entries.description: (count, points{x, y}[]): offsets the points by the current context's translation when its +0x208 is set (clearing it for the call and restoring it after). Fewer than three points draw a pixel, a line or a closed outline in the fill's colour. Otherwise it dispatches on the fill at +0x228: type 0 (a colour, optionally a ramp entry) and 6 fill through a span routine pointer, 1 goes to 00458438, 4 draws the outline, 5 and 7 go to the routine at 0047e5c4. The fill is scan-converted by Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion and clipped by the clip mode at +0x204: none, the rect +0x20c (Poly_ClipToRect), or each rect or span region of the clip list, the span regions through SpanRegion_Intersect. Gfx_BandedTriangle fills through it.

entries.name: Gfx_FillPolygonReversed
entries.description: (count, points): for more than two points copies them in reverse order (20-point stack buffer, no bounds check) and calls Gfx_FillPolygon; when the fill at context +0x228 is type 5 it also reverses the fill's per-vertex list at +8 for the call, then restores the pointer.

entries.name: Gfx_FillPolygonEitherWinding
entries.description: (count, points): sums the shoelace cross products in 64 bits; zero or less goes to Gfx_FillPolygonReversed, otherwise (and for one or two points) to Gfx_FillPolygon. Does nothing for count 0.

entries.name: Poly_ClipToRect
entries.description: (count, points, out, rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}): Sutherland-Hodgman clip against an inclusive rect, x pass then y pass, crossings computed from the outside endpoint with truncating 64-bit division; returns the new count. Gfx_FillPolygon's clip modes 1 and 2 use it.

entries.name: Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion
entries.description: (count, points, out): scan-converts a convex, clockwise outline of int32 {x, y} points into an int16 span region {top, rows, {x0, x1} per row} by Bresenham chains. Gfx_FillPolygon's span fills go through it. Span rules in the doc.

entries.name: Gfx_FillRect
entries.description: Fills a rect of four int32s, corners inclusive, through the {mode, colour} pair at context +0x22c: mode 0 is a solid fill, mode 6 a blit through a 256-entry lookup table. Callers normalize their corners before every call.

entries.name: Rect_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two rects {x0, y0, x1, y1} (inclusive) into out and returns out, or 0 when they do not overlap. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Rect_Intersect.

entries.name: SpanList_FromRect
entries.description: (rect{x0, y0, x1, y1}, out): writes int16 y0 at out+0, the row count y1 - y0 + 1 at out+2, then one int16 pair {x0, x1} per row from out+4. Gfx_FillRect builds its span list in the buffer at PTR_DAT_0047c429 with it.

entries.name: Gfx_FillSpanList
entries.description: (spans, origin): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_FillSpanList: copies the span list into the buffer at PTR_DAT_0047c425 translated by origin (and the context's translation when +0x208 is set) and fills it with the fill at +0x228 -- type 0 through the span routine 0047e540 with its colour (a type-4 colour resolved through the ramp records at 0047dd39), type 6 through 0047e544; other types return -- clipped by the clip mode: none, the rect at +0x20c (0045794d), or each entry of the clip list. Gfx_FillEllipse fills its spans with it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045766c, diffed against DBSIM 00486928

entries.name: SpanRegion_Intersect
entries.description: (a, b, out): intersects two span regions ({int16 top row, int16 row count, then an {x0, x1} int16 pair per row}) row by row into out. Rows before the first overlap are dropped, a gap after it is written as the empty span {1, 0}; returns out with its row count trimmed after the last overlapping row, or 0 when the regions share no row or no span overlaps. Gfx_DrawLine and Gfx_FillRect clip against span regions with it.

entries.name: SpanList_ClipToRect
entries.description: (rect, spans, out): clips a span list {int16 top row, int16 row count, {x0, x1} per row} to rect {x0, y0, x1, y1}, dropping rows outside it and clamping x ranges. Gfx_FillSpanList calls it twice. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpanList_ClipToRect (00486c09).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 0045794d; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00486c09

entries.name: Gfx_BandedTriangle
entries.description: 8-bit 'Gouraud' triangle: cut into one flat band per palette index between its corners' colours, each band a quad through the polygon filler.

entries.name: Gfx_FillBandedPolygon
entries.description: Fill type 1 of Gfx_FillPolygon, (count, points): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_FillContourPolygon. Maps each vertex's ushort shade (fill +0xc) through the ramp the fill colour's low word names (records at 0047dd39), fans triangles from vertex 0 and fills each with Gfx_BandedTriangle with the fill set to type 0, then restores its colour and type 1.

entries.name: Gfx_FillEllipse
entries.description: Ellipse in the box it is given; the map uses it for the intro pen.

entries.name: Math_AbsInt
entries.description: Returns |x| of an int32 by the sign-mask idiom (x ^ (x >> 31)) - (x >> 31). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_AbsInt (004886bf). Gfx_FillEllipse calls it.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch: offsets position by the clip block's translation when block+0x208 is 1, hands a type-1 bitmap (byte +5 low nibble) to Bitmap_BlitTransparent, and otherwise dispatches on the clip mode +0x204 to the raster routine at 0047e5a8 (mode 0, no rect) or 0047e5b0 (mode 1, and mode 2 only when the block holds a region, with the rect at +0x20c). GL_Blit calls it.

entries.name: Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Bitmap_GrabClipDispatch (00488868), identical after normalisation: (bitmap, point, flags) zeroes the bitmap's data (+0xa, size +6), clears the low nibble of +5, sets the format byte +4 to 8 when the display depth 0047c3f6 is 8 and it differs, or when the depth is 4 and it is not 4; offsets the point by the context's translation when +0x208 is 1; then reads the screen into the bitmap through the routine pointer 0047e5ac, unclipped for clip mode +0x204 0, clipped to the rect +0x20c for mode 1, and once per region rect for mode 2. ESAlert_HandleEvent saves the screen under an alert with it.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitScaledClipDispatch
entries.description: (bitmap, position, flags, size): Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch's scaled twin: the same translation, then by clip mode +0x204 the raster routine at 0047e5b4 with (bitmap, size[0], size[1], &position, rect, flags), rect null in mode 0 and the block's +0x20c in mode 1, and in mode 2 only when the block holds a region. There is no transparent branch. GLDisplay_DrawBitmapScaled calls it.

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled
entries.description: (bitmapDims, position, flip, size, angle): the VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled: source quad (0,0), (cols-1,0), (cols-1,rows-1), (0,rows-1), mirrored in x by flip bit 2 and in y by bit 1; destination quad (0,0), (w,0), (w,h), (0,h) from size, each corner rotated by the binary angle (00459196, Math_Rotate2DPoint_Thunk) and translated by position; filled with Gfx_FillPolygon through a type-5 bitmap fill {5, 4, source quad, bitmap} installed at the context's +0x228 and restored after. GLDisplay_DrawBitmapStretched calls it.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00458f68, compared with DBSIM 00488a8c

entries.name: Math_BuildRotation2DInto
entries.description: (out, angle): Math_BuildRotation2D(angle, out), the arguments the other way round. Bitmap_BlitRotatedScaled calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_BuildRotation2DInto (00488cbb).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 00459196; es2_naming.py diff against DBSIM 00488cbb

entries.name: Math_Rotate2DPoint_Thunk
entries.description: One-line forwarder to Math_Rotate2DPoint with the same arguments, as DBSIM's Math_Rotate2DPoint_Thunk (00488cd1).

entries.name: Bitmap_BlitTransparent
entries.description: The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Bitmap_BlitTransparent, over the clip block PTR_DAT_0047c3a8, with the same code stream decoded by the same helpers (SpriteCode_*, Raster_Span*, Math_NegateIf at 00459649-00459728). Bitmap_BlitClipDispatch hands it type-1 bitmaps.

entries.name: SpriteCode_Count
entries.description: (code): code & 0x3f. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_Count.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRun
entries.description: (code): code & 0x80. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_IsRun.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsLiteralRun
entries.description: (code): whether bit 6 is clear. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_IsLiteralRun.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFillRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 0047e5a4 (slot 25) with (colour, y, x0, x1). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_SpanFillRegion.

entries.name: Raster_SpanFill
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, colour): calls the raster routine at 0047e5a0 (slot 24) with (colour, y, x0, x1). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_SpanFill.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopyRegion
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the region-clipped raster routine at 0047e59c (slot 23) with (pixels, y, x0, x1). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_SpanCopyRegion.

entries.name: Raster_SpanCopy
entries.description: (y, x0, x1, pixels): calls the raster routine at 0047e598 (routine slot 22) with (pixels, y, x0, x1). The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Raster_SpanCopy.

entries.name: Math_NegateIf
entries.description: (flag, value): -value when flag is non-zero, else value. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Math_NegateIf; Bitmap_BlitTransparent calls it.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEnd
entries.description: (code): whether the top two bits are clear. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_IsRowEnd.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension
entries.description: (byte): 1 when non-zero with the top two bits clear, else 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_IsRowEndExtension.

entries.name: SpriteCode_IsEnd
entries.description: (code): whether code is 0x40. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's SpriteCode_IsEnd.

entries.name: RasterDriver_FindRoutineTable
