entries.name: AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate
entries.description: (thread, rate): stores rate at +0x4e and, when its sign flips, re-runs AnimThread_SetTarget with the current target. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's AnimThread_SetPlaybackRate (004795cc).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile at 004651c4; compared with DBSIM 004795cc

entries.name: AnimThread_Advance
entries.description: (thread, dt): unless parked at its target, advances the intra-frame offset by dt * rate (+0x4e) >> 8, crossing frames forward (AnimThread_CommitGroundMovement) or backward (AnimThread_UncommitGroundMovement), taking a found transition at its frame (AnimThread_LoadGroundTransform) and setting the at-target bit on reaching the target. AnimThread_StepAll calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's AnimThread_Advance (00479614).

entries.description: (animList, sequence, frame): the int16 at +2 of the frame's 6-byte record (sequence +0xc), the number of transitions leaving the frame. AnimThread_FindTransition calls it; DBSIM inlines it.

entries.description: (animList, sequence, frame): the int16 at +4 of the frame's 6-byte record, the index of its first transition in the 8-byte table at animList+0x1e. AnimThread_FindTransition calls it; DBSIM inlines it.

entries.description: (seq, frame, target, flag, rate): the sequence's vtable +0x28 (ANSequence_FrameShortOfTarget) when rate is not negative, else +0x2c (ANSequence_FrameShortOfTargetBackward). AnimThread_FindTransition calls it; DBSIM inlines the choice.

entries.description: (a, b, t, out): blends two 12-byte ANAnimList transform records (3 Euler shorts then 3 translation shorts) by a Q10 factor (0x400 is all b), the rotations along the shortest arc. 00465574 calls it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Anim_BlendKeyframeTransforms (00492600).

entries.name: ShellRandom_Reset
entries.description: Cursors to 0x18/0x37 and the 112-byte seed table from 0047f7b4, byte-identical to DBSIM's.

entries.description: (state, n): ShellRandom_Reset then n steps. Startup passes GetTickCount() & 0x7f.

entries.description: VSHELL's additive lagged Fibonacci step over a 56-entry int16 table, cursors at +0x70/+0x71 -- DBSIM's Math_RandomNext.

entries.description: (state, n) -> (ShellRandom_Next & 0x7fff) % n.

entries.description: Empty body. ShellRandom_Reset's last call, as Math_RandomSeedNoOp is Math_RandomSeed's.

entries.description: (GetTickCount() - base) >> 4: the timer the map intro runs on, one tick 16 ms.

entries.name: Time_InitSimClock
entries.description: 005ddbb8 = 005ddbba = 0x100, 005ddbc4 = 1000, 005ddbc6 = 005ddbbc = 005ddbbe = 1000 / 10 = 100 and 005ddbc0 = 100, then 005ddbc8 and Shell_TimerTicks' base 005ddbcc = GetTickCount(). DBSIM's copy, Time_InitSimClock (0046773c), divides by 8, so its unit is 125 ms where this one's is 100 ms. Ghidra had no function here.

DBSIM's copy, Time_BeginSimTick (004677bc), waits 40 ms. Ghidra had no function here.

entries.name: Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding
entries.description: (count, points, out): does nothing for count 0. For more than two points sums the shoelace cross products in 64 bits; a sum of zero or less (anticlockwise on screen, or degenerate) goes to Poly_ScanConvertReversed, otherwise, and for one or two points, straight to Poly_ScanConvert. Called by Poly_BuildSpanList.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00465e0a and its two entry wrappers; DBSIM copies matched by byte comparison

entries.name: Poly_ScanConvertReversed
entries.description: (count, points, out): for more than two points copies the points in reverse order into a 100-int stack buffer (no bounds check) and scan-converts that with Poly_ScanConvert, so an anticlockwise polygon comes out clockwise; otherwise passes points through unchanged.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of 00465e0a and its two entry wrappers; DBSIM copies matched by byte comparison

entries.name: Poly_ScanConvert
entries.description: (count, points, out): the int32 twin of Poly_ScanConvertToSpanRegion: scan-converts a convex, clockwise outline into {top, rows, then an int32 {x0, x1} pair per row} by the same rules (docs/polygon-fill.md#scan-conversion). Called only through Poly_ScanConvertEitherWinding and Poly_ScanConvertReversed.

entries.name: Event_Post

entries.name: EventQueue_Append
entries.description: (queue, event): PtrVector_Append(queue+0x11, event); when that fails, counts 0048dc28 and Assert_Report (include\WHANDLER.H line 0x43). Event_Post and Pointer_MoveTo append to 005ddbd0 with it.

entries.name: EventQueue_Pump
entries.description: Drains the event queue at handler+0x11. A mouse move (type 0x20, sub-code 0) re-runs Widget_HitTestTree from the display root and, when the answer changes, sends leave (0x10) to the old target and enter (8) to the new; any other event with no target goes to the current pointer target at handler+1. Then Event_Deliver.

entries.name: Pointer_SetTarget
entries.description: Pointer_Leave, then Pointer_Enter with the given widget: moves the pointer's target without a hit test.

entries.name: Pointer_Unlock
entries.description: Clears the pointer lock, +0x1f of the pointer state at DAT_005ddbd0, and hit-tests again at the last position, sending a leave and an enter if the target changed. While the lock is set EventQueue_Pump skips the hit test and every mouse event goes to the current target; ESDialog_HandleEvent, SaveScreen_BeginRename (004377d2) and 0043bc0a set it.

entries.name: Widget_HitTestTree
entries.description: Widget_HitTestTree(handler, widget, point): null when the widget is hidden (+0x11 bit 2) or the point is outside it; otherwise tries its children in list order (newest first) recursively and returns the first hit, or the widget itself. The pointer's target on every mouse move.

entries.name: Pointer_Leave
entries.description: Sends a leave event (0x10) to the pointer's current target and clears it. The leave is what clears a pressed widget's +0x45, cancelling the click.

entries.name: Pointer_Enter
entries.description: Sets the pointer's target (hit-testing from the display root when passed null) and sends it an enter event (8); then sets the cursor from the first +0x35 up the parent chain.

entries.name: Event_Deliver
entries.description: Finds the receiver with Event_FindReceiver, discards the event when there is none, otherwise makes the point local (Event_ToLocal) and calls the receiver's vtable slot 0.

entries.name: Event_FindReceiver
entries.description: Walks from the event's target (+0x20) through Window_Parent to the first widget whose event mask +0x39 has the event type's bit; the result goes to event+0x1c. How a click on a Text reaches its parent.

entries.name: Event_ToLocal
entries.description: Subtracts the event target's absolute origin (+0x15, +0x19) from the event point (+0x10, +0x14).

entries.name: PtrVector_PopFront
entries.description: (vector): 0 when the count (+0) is 0; otherwise asserts it positive (d:\include\ptrarray.h line 0x60, PtrArray::operator[]), takes element 0 of the data at +10, removes it with PtrVector_RemoveAt(vector, 0) and returns it. EventQueue_Pump drains its queue (+0x11) with it.

entries.name: WinTimer_InstallAlarm
entries.description: Adds an alarm for a widget to the WinTimer's twenty-entry table at DAT_005ddbd4 (asserts 'WinTimer::installAlarm > too many' in code\wintimer.cpp). The edit field installs one at 500, 500 when it takes focus.

entries.name: WinTimer_RemoveAlarms
entries.description: Removes every WinTimer alarm installed for a widget.

entries.name: Timer_Remove
entries.description: (timers, index): removes a timer by moving the last record into its slot and decrementing the count at +0x141.

entries.name: Timer_Tick
entries.description: Advances a timer list by the GetTickCount delta since the last tick (stored at +0x145). Timers are 16-byte records from +1 (count at +0x141): target, remaining ms, period ms, id. An expired timer posts a WinTimerEvent (target at +0x20, id at +0x24) with Event_Post and reloads from its period; a timer with period 0 is then removed (Timer_Remove).

entries.description: (mono, ch): sends DeviceIoControl code 5 with the single byte ch. Its only caller, maybe_Mono_Clear, passes a space (0x20); the name assumes code 5 fills the screen with that character.

entries.name: DarkMono_PutChar
entries.description: (mono, a, b, ch): sends DeviceIoControl code 6 with a 6-byte packet {a, b, ch} of 16-bit words. Mono_PutChar passes (y, x) as (a, b).

entries.name: DarkMono_PutString
entries.description: (mono, a, b, text): sends DeviceIoControl code 7 with a 0x58-byte packet {a, b, length, text}: 16-bit words, then the text truncated to 80 characters. Mono_Print and Mono_Printf pass (y, x) as (a, b).

entries.name: Eh_InitExceptBlock
entries.description: Borland C++ exception-frame prologue: links the caller's frame record into the FS:[0] SEH chain. Called first by most VSHELL functions with a destructor-bearing local, the click thunks included; not part of any dispatch.

entries.name: Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount
entries.description: Borland RTL helper (the RTL's __GetPolymorphicDTC; no name string for it in the image). Given an object and the offset of its vptr, returns the destructor count stored in the dynamic type's typeinfo: vptr, back by the offset-to-top at vptr[-4], then the typeinfo pointer at -0xc, field +0x20. Returns 0 for a null object. Every polymorphic delete runs '*DAT_005ddec0 += Rtl_GetPolymorphicDtorCount(p, 0); p->vdtor(3)' to keep the exception handler's live-destructor count right.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile and disassembly; calling pattern in every polymorphic delete, e.g. VolRStream_Dtor

entries.name: Rtl_VectorDelete
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_delete_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_delete_' at 00480f50): (array, elemSize, count, mode, dtor). Takes the count from array[-1] when mode & 0x10, runs dtor(elem, 2) on each element from last to first under the mode & 7 calling convention, then frees the block with Mem_DeleteArray when mode & 8 and returns 0; otherwise returns the block start.

entries.name: Rtl_VectorNew
entries.description: Borland RTL _vector_new_ (named by its own error string 'Illegal mode in _vector_new_' at 00480f70): (mem, elemSize, count, mode, ctor). Allocates count*elemSize bytes with Mem_NewArray when mem is null, plus 4 when mode & 0x10, in which case the count is stored in that first dword. Runs ctor on each element in turn with the calling convention mode & 7 selects (1 and 5 push this, 2 pushes it callee-cleaned, 3 passes it in EAX). Returns the first element (past the count), or 0 when the allocation fails.

entries.name: Rtl_PureError
entries.description: The Borland RTL's pure-virtual-call handler: __ErrorExit("Pure virtual function called") (00480f90). Every pure slot of an abstract class's vtable points here: ClassItem's five, EventProducer's two, EventConsumer's, WinButton's +4, WinCursor's, WinDisplay's eight and Map's slot 0. DBSIM's copy is at 00496684. Ghidra had no function here.
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly at 0046b624; es2_naming.py vtables VSHELL

entries.name: Shell_QuitFlag
entries.description: Nonzero ends the shell's main loop in 00401525. The main menu's QUIT, VIEW DEMO and INSTANT ACTION set it, and so does launching a mission; Shell_RunFrames stops early on it.

Tested first by all nine tab-strip handlers, which return without doing anything when it is zero -- before even the already-on-this-tab check. Nothing that writes it has been traced, so whether it is an input gate, a shell-running flag or something else is unknown.

entries.name: Shell_CloseAllowed
entries.description: Set before the main loop and by the startup widget's hide, cleared by its show. WM_CLOSE and the display hotkeys are ignored while it is clear.

entries.name: g_VolumeGroup
entries.description: Pointer to the shell's VolumeGroup (volume pointers from +0, count byte at +0x78). VolRStream's constructors assert it is set; VolRStream_Open searches it with VolumeGroup_FindEntry.

entries.name: VolumeGroup_BufferSize
entries.description: The BuffRStream buffer size VolumeGroup_AddVolume hands Volume_LoadVolume for each volume file it opens. VolumeGroup_Ctor stores 0x400 and VolumeGroup_SetBufferSize stores its clamped argument.

entries.name: Key_VkTable
entries.description: MainWndProc's 0x54 dword table of virtual-key codes: a key's position in it is its set-1 scancode, the key code VSHELL's keyboard works in. Punctuation VKs are absent, so those keys send nothing.

entries.name: EsTextBinHandle

entries.name: ShellButtonFontHandle

entries.name: CurrentPaletteHandle

entries.name: ShellBackdropBitmap

entries.name: maybe_PaletteDirtyFlag

entries.name: PaletteNameTable
entries.description: 20 char* to dpl\*.dpl, indexed by Shell_InstallPalette. 0 intr_pt1, 1 palette, 2 arming, 3 cam_er, 4 cam_moon, 5-9 br_w1..br_w5, 10-14 db_w1..db_w5, 15-19 alph/delt/omic/brav/luna. Read out of the data segment; the three per-stage runs are what show the campaign stage counts from 1 at runtime.

entries.name: Key_CommandFilter

entries.name: Key_CommandTable

entries.name: Key_CharTable

entries.name: Key_CharTableShifted

entries.name: Input_EventTime

entries.name: HercTypeIdTable
entries.description: Nine int16 searched by Herc_TypeToIndex to map a chassis type to its catalog index. Retail contents are 0-8 in order.

entries.name: HercCapacityTable
entries.description: Hardpoint capacity per chassis index: 3, 5, 5, 8, 9, 9, 10, 4, 7. Diverges from herc_inf.dat +0x06 for the Raptor II, where this table wins.

entries.name: WeaponClassTable
entries.description: Thirty int16 searched by Weapon_ClassIndexForId: weapon catalog ids 0-18 then 22-32, omitting the three Bull weapons.

entries.name: HercComponentGroupTable
entries.description: Six groups of up to three int16, each -1 terminated, partitioning the 13 external component indices exactly once: {0,1} {2,4} {3,5} {6} {7,9,11} {8,10,12}. The granularity the repair bay and scrap valuation price externals at.

entries.name: ArmoryQueueFreeSlots
entries.description: Free weapon-build workspace slots, 0-5. Printed as "Workspace Available:", and 5 minus it as "Workspace In Use:". Save block 2 opens with this value.

entries.name: ArmoryQueueSlots
entries.description: Five int16, one weapon catalog id per build-queue slot, 0 for empty. The rest of save block 2.

entries.name: WeaponGrant_UnitIds
entries.description: 22 int16 weapon ids, one per campaign-flag slot 0x15-0x2a, the weapon Armory_GrantCampaignWeapons adds flag[s] units of. Its loop runs to slot 0x31, reading seven more words past the table that are not weapon ids.

entries.name: WeaponGrant_UnlockValues
entries.description: 33 int16, one per weapon id: the campaign-flag value that unlocks the weapon. Read only where WeaponGrant_UnlockSlots is not -1.

entries.name: WeaponGrant_UnlockSlots
entries.description: 33 int16, one per weapon id: the campaign-flag slot whose value unlocks the weapon, -1 for none. Eight are set: ATC75 0x34, ATC100 0x35, L400 0x32, L500 0x33, TARG 0x39, SHLD 0x38, TURB 0x3a, ENRG 0x3b.

entries.name: CampaignStage
entries.description: The player's campaign stage, first half of the career position pair. Counts from 1 at runtime where the save stores it from 0: the briefing, debrief and theater palette runs are all reached as stage plus a constant, and the campaign map's Earth-to-Moon switch and the location-art table's fourth entry both fall at stage 5.

entries.name: CampaignMissionInStage
entries.description: Mission within the stage, second half of the career position pair. Zero is what makes the mission tab open on the campaign map rather than a briefing.

entries.name: RepairTargetTable
entries.description: Six int16 repair targets by level: 100, 89, 79, 59, 29, 0.

entries.name: RepairLevelTable
entries.description: Six int16 condition-band floors by repair level: 90, 80, 60, 30, 1, 0.

entries.name: Avi_StopRequested
entries.description: Avi_Play's loop condition: cleared before playback, and the movie ends when a mouse button down in the window procedure, or Esc or Space, sets it.

entries.name: Avi_Playing
entries.description: 1 while Avi_Play has a movie on screen, 0 otherwise; Avi_Play is its only writer. WinButton_HandleEvent and ESButtonBitmap_HandleEvent ignore mouse events while it is set, and the window procedure drops button messages (after a press has ended the movie) and the options hotkeys.

entries.name: MovieQueue_WriteIndex
entries.description: Movie_Enqueue's slot in MovieQueue_Entries, modulo 10.

entries.name: MovieQueue_ReadIndex
entries.description: Movie_PlayQueue's slot in MovieQueue_Entries, modulo 10.

entries.name: MovieQueue_Running
entries.description: 1 from the start of a Movie_PlayQueue run until the next call finds the ring empty; Movie_PlayQueue is its only writer. WinButton_HandleEvent and ESButtonBitmap_HandleEvent ignore mouse events while it is set.

entries.name: Movie_FileTable
entries.description: 86 char* avi\ paths indexed by movie id, unchecked: pt1-hc4 for 0-0x43, then intr_pt1, intr_pt2, c1-c5, alph_th, delt_th, omic_th, brav_th, luna, transm3, end1a, death, victory, credits, dropship for 0x44-0x55.

entries.name: MovieQueue_IntroSkipped
entries.description: Set by a mouse button down (MainWndProc) or Esc/Space (Avi_Play) while MovieQueue_PlayingIntro is set; Movie_PlayQueue then skips any further intro part. No store clearing it found (three stores, each 1).

entries.name: MovieQueue_PlayingIntro
entries.description: Set by Movie_PlayQueue for the entry being played when it is 0x44 or 0x45 (the intro), cleared for any other.

entries.name: maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled
entries.description: The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's maybe_g_DepthBufferEnabled (0049f270). When non-zero, both textured rasterizers run Raster_DepthTestSpan per row and, when the clip-span table DAT_0047e92c is set, draw its runs through the ...Clipped spans (TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA also stores the view depth in vertex +8 and adds edge flag 8, which TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB always does), and CellWalk_Polygon walks near to far. 0 in the image; every absolute-address operand found is a read.
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA/B and CellWalk_Polygon; docs/polygon-fill.md

entries.name: g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit
entries.description: VSHELL's counterpart of DBSIM's g_PerspectiveUseQuadraticFit (0049f278): when non-zero, TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB takes each row's starting u and v, and its last partial run's end, from Raster_BuildEdgeTables' quadratic fit instead of dividing. The hgrid cell callback 00429dac sets it per cell to (DAT_0047223c < the value it passes 00420279).
entries.source: VSHELL disassembly: writer 0042a9df in 00429dac, readers 00420f3b and 004211b1 in TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB

entries.name: g_TexturedPolyUseBitmapBrush
entries.description: Selects how TSTexture4Poly_Render fills a textured poly; both ways sample the frame. 0: the frame descriptor at g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] gives the UV corners, and the 3D positions go to TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA or B (g_TexturedPolyPerspective). Non-zero: the frame's bitmap comes from the DBA's pointer list (+8), and a type-7 bitmap brush {7, count, uvs, bitmap, remap row} is installed at the context's +0x22c with the UVs the bitmap's extent inset by 3 on each side and the remap row ((DAT_0047e9ac - 1) * shade & ~0xff) + DAT_0047e9a8 (0 while DAT_0047e9ac is 0); the vertices are projected (Poly_ProjectShapeVertices), near-plane clipped with the UVs when needed (Poly_ClipRingToNearPlaneWithUV) and filled through PolyFill_FillThenOutline, and the default brush 005d8000 is restored after. The runtime condition that sets this flag is not determined.

entries.name: g_TexturedPolyPerspective
entries.description: Selects TSTexture4Poly_Render's textured fill: 0 TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeA (u and v linear in screen space), non-zero TSTexture4Poly_RasterizeB (perspective-correct). The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's g_TexturedPolyPerspective (0049f274).
entries.source: VSHELL decompile of TSTexture4Poly_Render; disassembly read at 00422fbf

entries.name: ShellMap_DfnPanelPtr
entries.description: Global holding the loaded MAP.DFN panel object. Exhaustive address-xref search found only 2 referencing functions in all of VSHELL.EXE -- ShellMap_EnsureResourcesLoaded (the loader) and ShellMap_ReleaseResources (destructor call only). The parsed contents are never read back anywhere in VSHELL -- this specific load is dead/vestigial (the format's real, live consumer is DBSIM's cockpit font system, see ColorSchemePanels_LoadAll).

entries.name: Sos_MasterVolume
entries.description: Master volume, 0-100 (100 in the image), multiplied into every digital voice's volume by Sos_ApplyVolume and the voice start at 0042d96f. Sos_SetMasterVolume writes it. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_MasterVolume.

entries.name: Sos_LastError
entries.description: The last SOS result the backend stored: the driver open (0042df68) and Sos_ShutdownDrivers write their SOS calls' results here. Read by Sos_GetLastError. The VSHELL counterpart of DBSIM's Sos_LastError.

entries.name: ShellSound_Manager
entries.description: The shell's SFX manager (0x4c bytes), or null under -s.

entries.name: ShellSound_MusicVolume
entries.description: The music's volume, 0-100; 0 in the image and written only by the two fades.

entries.name: ShellSound_Running
entries.description: 1 between ShellSound_Start and ShellSound_Stop; the click sounds play only while it is set.

entries.name: InstantAction_Active
entries.description: Set by INSTANT ACTION's handler; MsnGen_BuildPlayerHerc gives the player the mission's own machine while it is set.

entries.name: RepairSelectedColumn
entries.description: Column of the repair screen's current selection: 0 the chassis picture, 1 the internal list.

entries.name: RepairSelectedCategory
entries.description: The selection's condition-array category, as Repair_HotspotCategory returns it.

entries.name: RepairSelectedRow
entries.description: Row of the repair screen's current selection.

entries.name: RepairSelectedIndex
entries.description: The selection's index within its category, as Repair_HotspotIndex returns it. With RepairSelectedCategory this is a HercStatus_Get argument pair.

entries.name: maybe_SaveScreen_EditMode
entries.description: The slot rename's state: 0 idle, 2 while a rename is live (SaveScreen_SelectSlot refuses to move the selection), 1 only transiently inside the SAVE handler before SaveScreen_BeginRename sets 2. ACCEPT and CANCEL write 0.

entries.name: SaveScreen_SelectedSlot
entries.description: Which save slot the list has selected. Parked at 10 on leaving the screen, which is past every row, so both SAVE and RESTORE test it against 10 before anything else.

entries.name: SaveScreen_RowCharSet
entries.description: The save screen rows' permitted-character set: ^, the digits, both alphabets and the space.

entries.name: CurrentTabIndex
entries.description: Which tab screen is up, 0-7, or 0xffff after a strip refresh. Every tab handler returns early when it already holds its own index, so clicking the tab you are on is a no-op.

entries.name: RegistrationSkillChoice
entries.description: The skill (and so the campaign difficulty) the registration screen is showing, 0-3. Stepped modulo 4 by FUN_0043bd15 and FUN_0043c01d, printed as estext.bin 0x35 + value, and passed to Game_NewCareer as the new player pilot's +0x25.

entries.name: ArmingSelectedHardpoint
entries.description: Which hardpoint the arming screen has selected.

entries.name: Squad_RosterClickFlag
entries.description: Set by the eight roster-row thunks around their Squad_SelectBay call; while set, the crew arm also assigns the bay to the selected row's pilot.

entries.name: DamageLevelBands
entries.description: Five int16, {89, 79, 59, 29, 0}, walked by Repair_DamageLevel with a strictly-greater test. Partitions identically to Repair_LevelForCondition's {90, 80, 60, 30, 1, 0} tested with <=.

entries.name: DamageLevelColors
entries.description: Six int16 palette entries, {14, 13, 12, 11, 10, 39}, indexed by damage level. Six colours against only four damage words in estext.bin, which is the retail overrun recorded in KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

entries.name: Arming_RowWeapons
entries.description: The 27 weapon ids the WEAPONS screen's inventory rows list: arm_weap.dat's 26 in file order, then None (0).

entries.name: Arming_GuidanceButtonsUp
entries.description: Whether the five guidance buttons are shown.

entries.name: Arming_FitArmed
entries.description: Set by each inventory row's thunk for the length of its Arming_SelectRow call; Arming_FitSelected fits only while it is set.

entries.name: Arming_LitRow
entries.description: The WEAPONS screen's lit inventory row, -1 in the image.

entries.name: Arming_ShownGuidance
entries.description: The guidance kind whose picture Arming_ShowGuidance last put up, -1 in the image; reset only by a row whose weapon takes no guidance.

entries.name: Arming_LitGuidance
entries.description: The guidance kind whose button Arming_ShowGuidance last lit, 0 in the image.

entries.name: CrewSelectedRow
entries.description: The crew screen's selected row, 0-3 (int16). The same 4-byte stride continues at 004776e0 as the row pilot pointers for rows 1-3.

entries.name: MissionLocationDbaTable
entries.description: Four char* -- dba\alph2.dba, dba\delt1.dba, dba\omic1.dba, dba\brav1.dba -- indexed by campaign stage minus one. Stage 5 branches to the lunar cutscene before the lookup, which is one of the three facts showing the stage counts from 1.

entries.name: Armory_LitRow
entries.description: The armory's lit row, 0-25, or -1 (0xffff in the image). Written by Armory_ClickRow and Armory_RightClickRow, reset by Armory_Leave.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_SelectedRow
entries.description: int16, the lit practice row; -1 in the image. Also the stage-0 mission a training career starts on (Career_SeedPosition); FUN_0041c58d uses the mission's own machine while it is below 4.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_RowChassis
entries.description: int16 per practice row, read as the low byte at row*2: 0,0,1,8,4,2,7,3 for rows 0-7, then 5,7,3 for INSTANT ACTION's rows 8-10. Written into prefs option 0x28 by PracticeScreen_SelectRow.

entries.name: GLFont_Vtable
entries.description: GLFont's 7-slot vtable (RTTI 'GLFont', 0x32 bytes, base GLBase): GLFont_GetClassTag, GLFont_GetStreamSize, GLFont_GetMemorySize, GLFont_ReadFromStream, GLFont_WriteToStream, VshellClassItem_DebugPrintType, GLFont_Dtor. The class-item interface only: the font's drawing is Font_DrawString and Font_DrawGlyph, which read the fields directly.

entries.name: g_TSTexture4PolyVtable
entries.description: TSTexture4Poly's vtable (RTTI 'TSTexture4Poly'), the one TSTexture4Poly_Construct stamps last. Slot +0x1c, TSTexture4Poly_Render, is what TSGroup_RenderPolys's per-item dispatch calls for a TSTexture4Poly; a TSBitmapPart draws through its own TSBitmapPart_Render, so the two do not share one render mechanism. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_TSSolidPolyVtable
entries.description: TSSolidPoly's real, fully-constructed vtable (found via TSSolidPoly_Construct's final vtable-pointer stamp). Slot +0x1c (TSSolidPoly_Render, FUN_00422a32) is what TSGroup_RenderPolys's per-poly dispatch (*(*polyPtr)+0x1c) calls for a TSSolidPoly, mirroring TSTexture4Poly's g_TSTexture4PolyVtable +0x1c slot exactly.

entries.name: g_TSObjectTypeRegistry
entries.description: 18-entry, 12-byte-stride table: {tag:uint32 matching a DTS chunk header's on-disk [subtype:u16][supertype:u16] bytes, constructorFnPtr, nameStringPtr}. Every tag matches a known DTS chunk tag (e.g. 0x0014000f = TSTexture4Poly) and sits beside its name string ("TSPoly", "TSGroup", etc.). This is the DTS-tree node factory VSHELL's and DBSIM's shared ThreeSpace engine uses to construct the right C++ class per on-disk chunk tag -- the reliable way to find any TS*/AN* class's real constructor (and from there its real vtable) when RTTI type-name strings have zero code references, as they often do in this binary (also seen for .BND's MECH string). Tag 0x0e is registered here but has no known retail .DTS chunk. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: Display_Current
entries.description: The display the pointer is on. Display_GetRoot reads its root widget at +5; Display_HopTo replaces it when the pointer crosses into a neighbour.

entries.name: Sos_BindRefCount
entries.description: Sos_BindLibrary's refcount; Sos_UnbindLibrary frees the library when it reaches 0. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_BindRefCount.

entries.name: MissionScreenView
entries.description: Which face the mission tab is showing: 0 the campaign map, 1 the briefing, 4 the debrief. Selects that view's palette and its screen content.

entries.name: VshellClassItem_RegistryBuckets
entries.description: Base of VSHELL's ClassItem registry bucket array (pairs of {int* entries, int count}, 8 bytes/bucket). Runtime-populated by static initializers -- reads as zero-length in the static image.

entries.name: ClassItem_CurrentFrame
entries.description: Pointer to the frame of the class item being read ({+0 type tag, +4 start, +8 end, ...}); VshellClassItem_LoadItem points it at its own and restores the previous one, ClassItem_CloseItem reads the end. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's ClassItem_CurrentFrame.

entries.name: Shell_SoundEnabled
entries.description: Cleared by -s (and by -v and -?); gates the sound manager's creation and ESButtonFont_HandleEvent's press sound.

entries.name: g_ShellPool
entries.description: The src\mymem.cpp pool behind Mem_New / Mem_NewArray, a 0x14-byte Memory object: The pool object (e.g. 0048239c): +0 base, +4 byte size, +8 free-list head, +0xc free bytes, +0x10 lowest free bytes seen. Every block starts with an 8-byte header: an allocated block holds 'KLBA' (0x41424c4b) at +0 and its size including the header at +4, the caller's data at +8; a free block holds the next free block at +0, its size at +4 and 'KLBF' (0x46424c4b) at +8. Initialised by Memory_Init at 00401576.

entries.name: ShellOptions
entries.description: VSHELL's copy of the 54-byte data\prefs.cfg option array -- the same file, layout, shadow and handler-table design DBSIM uses. Options 0x25-0x29 are the practice missions screen's five parameters.

entries.name: ShellOption_Sounds
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 1, SOUNDS: gates the shell's click sounds.

entries.name: ShellOption_GameResolution
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 4. The PREFERENCES screen row Game Resolution: 0 = High Res (640x480), 1 = Low Res (320x240). DBSIM's VideoMode_Configure freads the same byte out of the file and treats 1 as 320x240 and everything else as hi-res.

entries.name: ShellOption_ShellMusicTrack
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 5. Selects the shell's background music: non-zero loads hmi/shell1.wav, zero hmi/shell2.wav. Read only there; DBSIM never reads it.

entries.name: ShellOption_DisplayMode
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 6. The PREFERENCES screen row Display Mode: 0 = Window, 1 = Full Screen. DBSIM reads the same byte in VideoMode_Configure and writes it back at shutdown when the live state differs.

entries.name: ShellOption_CampaignMode
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 42. Seeds CampaignModeFlag (0048260c) in FUN_0040e17e, so campaign-versus-training survives a restart.

entries.name: ShellOption_Language
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 43. The LANG0.VOL folder: 0 eng, 1 fre, 2 ger. Copied into 0048227a by the shell's global init and read there by WeaponsBin_Open, which prefixes every .BIN it opens with that folder.

entries.name: ShellOption_RepairMode
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 44. The PREFERENCES screen row Repair Options, three ways -- 0 'AutoRepair All Hercs', 1 'Manually Repair My Herc', 2 'Manually Repair All Hercs' (estext.bin 0x113-0x115). Repair_Enter also prints it as the repair screen's mode readout, but branches only on 0 and 1.

entries.name: ShellOption_WeaponsBuildMode
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 45. The PREFERENCES screen row Weapons Building -- 0 AutoBuild Weapons, 1 Manually Build Weapons (estext.bin 0x111/0x112).

entries.name: ShellOption_MissionHercExtra
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 46. Which of stage 0's three demo missions the next INSTANT ACTION plays: InstantAction_SelectDemo selects practice row option+8 and steps the option mod 3. The row's chassis goes into option 40.

entries.name: ShellOption_SkipSierraIni
entries.description: prefs.cfg option 47. Non-zero skips the startup read of Sierra.ini in FUN_00401525. A retail prefs.cfg ships 1, so that file is never read in a retail install.

entries.name: ShellOptionsShadow
entries.description: Load-time shadow of ShellOptions; ShellOptions_Commit fires each changed option's handler against it.

entries.name: ShellOptionHandlers
entries.description: Per-option handler table, parallel to ShellOptions.

entries.name: maybe_HasGameInProgress
entries.description: The save screen's SAVE button is enabled only on this and a real row being selected, so it reads as whether there is a game to write out. Nothing that sets it has been traced.

entries.name: CampaignModeFlag
entries.description: 1 for a campaign, 0 for training. Selects which autosave slot 10 resolves to (GAME_R vs GAME_T) and gates salvage awards at debrief.

entries.name: SaveSlotTable
entries.description: 12 save slots, 94-byte (0x5e) stride: filename at +0x00 (13 bytes), display label at +0x0d (80 bytes), in-use byte at +0x5d. Slots 10 and 11 are the RESUME and TRAINING autosaves.

entries.name: MainMenu_CurrentGameInUse
entries.description: Not a global of its own: the in-use byte (+0x5d) of slot 10's entry in the 0x5e-byte slot table at 00482610. MainMenu_Show gates CONTINUE GAME on it.

entries.name: SquadPositionsInPlay
entries.description: The player structure's leading int16: squad positions in play, the player's counted as 0. Bounds the auto-repair (0040e862) and player.mec export (0040f1e4) loops; Squad_UpdateOnStrength puts a member on strength only below it; the crew screen lights the rows below it.

entries.name: PlayerPilotRecord
entries.description: The player's own 59-byte pilot record, same shape as a squadmate's. Its name buffer is at +0x04, which is why the copies in Stats_StageCurrentGame start four bytes into the record.

entries.name: PlayerPilotSkill
entries.description: The player pilot record's +0x25 (record base 00482a7c). Chosen once at registration, never advanced, saved with the career, and copied into script.dat's header as the mission difficulty.

entries.name: SelectedBaySlot
entries.description: Which of the eight HERC bay slots is selected, 0-7, or -1 for none. Indexes the bay pointer array at 00482ac3 and the per-slot widget arrays.

entries.name: Hangar_DebriefScrapCount
entries.description: int16 at +0x24 of the hangar at 00482ac3: machines the debrief scrapped. HercsDat_Clear zeroes it at every hangar load, Herc_SettleAfterMission adds one per scrap (INC at 00410d21), and Game_ProcessMissionResults copies it into campaign flag 8 (0040eef6), which the mission's .ENG debrief loss line tests.

entries.name: Debrief_PilotsLost
entries.description: int16: Squad_ProgressAll's count of pilots lost, the player included when at 0 condition, stored at 0040eea9. Game_ProcessMissionResults copies it into campaign flag 9 and hands it to Debrief_WriteReport as the Losses figure.

entries.name: CareerSalvage
entries.description: The career salvage pool, int32 -- the game's single currency, held in kilograms; printed in tons by the crew and Herc Construction screens and in kilograms by the repair detail panel and armory readout. Seeded to rand(0..10)*1000 + 100000, credited from results.dat, debited by repairs and armory purchases. Immediately precedes the campaign flag array in memory and in the save file.

entries.name: maybe_CampaignFlagArray
entries.description: The campaign flag store: 1000 int16 compared against by the .MSN condition/trigger opcode system (switch 0x119-0x11e: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=). Confirmed campaign-persistent by three independent serializers that each move exactly 2000 bytes of it: the save file writes it after the salvage pool (FUN_0040e37b/FUN_0040e4f2), FUN_0040e9cb writes it to data\mission.var before a mission and FUN_0040ea59 reads it back at debrief, where slot 0 is overwritten with the mission outcome. DBSIM's counterpart is DAT_004a9ef4. The 'maybe_' prefix is stale; rename to CampaignFlagArray on the next Ghidra pass.

entries.name: HercInfoTable
entries.description: gam\herc_inf.dat in memory: 9 records of 16 bytes. int16 each of chassis type, mass in tons, top speed in kph, hardpoints, price in tons, an unread field, build time in missions, and the availability flag. Stride and the +0x08 price offset confirmed via raw disassembly in Herc_ScrapValue (shl edx,4 then movsx ecx,word [edx+0x00483b5c] at 00413b93), not decompiler pointer math. The flag array is save block 7.

entries.name: WeaponsDat_RecordArray
entries.description: In-memory WEAPONS.DAT record array, 29 bytes/record. Stride confirmed via IMUL EDX,EDX,0x1d in raw disassembly (FUN_0041266a), not decompiler pointer-math (which mis-implied 116 bytes).

entries.name: WeaponsDat_RankTable
entries.description: One int16 per weapon id, read from weapons.dat after each record into an array parallel to WeaponsDat_RecordArray. Sorts the catalog: ranks 1-28 are a permutation over the ordinary weapons, NONE and the three Bull weapons hold 99, and MFAC holds 0.

entries.name: maybe_WeaponsBinFileHandle
entries.description: weapons.bin's stream/file handle, referenced alongside WeaponsDat_RecordArray in the WEAPONS.DAT loading call chain.

entries.name: HercExternalGroupValues
entries.description: Per-chassis unit values for the six external component groups, 9 rows of 33 int16. Expanded at load from damage.dat percentages against herc_inf.dat prices through FixedMulQ10.

entries.name: HercInternalValues
entries.description: Per-chassis unit values for the nine internal components. Column 13 of the same 9x33 int16 table as HercExternalGroupValues.

entries.name: WeaponScrapValues
entries.description: Per-weapon scrap value, 33 int16, expanded from damage.dat. The source column is the weapon's weapons.dat price times 100 for all thirty non-Bull ids, with the Bull trio zeroed.

entries.name: Avi_PaletteHandle
entries.description: The HPALETTE Avi_Play hands each movie; 0 until Avi_BuildPalette runs, which Movie_PlayQueue's startup call (argument 0) skips. Also stored at 0041deea by an undisassembled routine at 0041dea8 (236-entry palette) with no reference found.

entries.name: MovieQueue_Entries
entries.description: Ten 0x1c-byte movie entries: int16 id at +0 (0xffff for a free entry), a four-int rect at +2, int16 palette index at +0x12 (0xffff for none), the location-tab flag at +0x14 and a callback at +0x18. Written by Movie_Enqueue, played and freed by Movie_PlayQueue.

entries.name: ShellSound_PressSample
entries.description: Sample handle of hmi\gm_69.wav.

entries.name: ShellSound_MusicSample
entries.description: Sample handle of the shell music track.

entries.name: ShellSound_TabClickSample
entries.description: Sample handle of hmi\bptlt2.wav.

entries.name: ShellSound_SwitchSample
entries.description: Sample handle of hmi\lswitch2.wav.

entries.name: SaveSlotSummaryTable
entries.description: Eleven 67-byte (0x43) staging records, one per save slot: a 59-byte pilot record, then int32 salvage in kilograms, int16 campaign stage and int16 mission within the stage. What the save screen's detail panel prints.

entries.name: StartupAnimWidget
entries.description: The startup sequence widget MainMenu_BuildScreen builds over the whole window, frames dbm\bay2a_80 to bay2a_84, the last twice.

entries.name: QuitAlert
entries.description: The Alt+F4 QUIT alert widget QuitAlert_Build creates.

entries.name: RepairHotspotHandlers
entries.description: Twenty-five thunks in one table, filled by 00431f3c: sixteen for column 0 (the rects over the chassis picture) then nine for column 1 (the internal-component list). Each calls Repair_SelectHotspot with its own (column, row).

entries.name: SaveScreen_ExitTarget
entries.description: Where the EXIT button returns to: 0 rebuilds the main menu, 8 installs palette case 8 and refreshes the tab strip. Tab 1's handler writes 8 before entering.

entries.name: ShellRootWidget
entries.description: The backdrop-textured root every shell screen parents to.

entries.name: PaletteScopeWidget
entries.description: The shell's palette scope, {0, 0x1e, 0x27f, 0x1df} -- the canvas below the tab strip.

entries.name: ShellPanelWidget
entries.description: The full-screen panel at {0, 0, 0x27f, 0x1df}; every widget on the tab strip is its child.

entries.name: TabStripMenuButton
entries.description: The square button at {7, 4, 0x17, 0x1b}, dba\online.dba frames 0 and 1.

entries.name: TabButtonMainMenu
entries.description: Tab 0, caption estext.bin 0x13.

entries.name: TabButtonSave
entries.description: Tab 1, caption estext.bin 0x14.

entries.name: TabButtonWeapons
entries.description: Tab 2, caption estext.bin 0x15.

entries.name: TabButtonRepair
entries.description: Tab 3, caption estext.bin 0x16. Gated off in the training campaign.

entries.name: TabButtonBuild
entries.description: Tab 4, caption estext.bin 0x17. Gated off in the training campaign.

entries.name: TabButtonArmory
entries.description: Tab 5, caption estext.bin 0x18. The builder clears its +0x49 at construction and the strip refresh rewrites it; gated off in the training campaign.

entries.name: TabButtonCrew
entries.description: Tab 6, caption estext.bin 0x19.

entries.name: TabButtonMission
entries.description: Tab 7, caption estext.bin 0x1a.

entries.name: SquadSlotPictureWidgets
entries.description: Eight widgets, one per bay slot: the chassis picture each screen's hotspot overlay is parented to.

entries.name: SquadSlotRowWidgets
entries.description: Eight widgets, one per bay slot: the roster rows, whose +0x4d Squad_ShowPanel sets to 0x29 for the selected slot and 0x10 for the rest.

entries.name: HotspotHandlerTable
entries.description: The click handlers Hotspots_BuildOverlay indexes by an area's position within its chassis group -- ten entries for the arming tab, sixteen for the repair tab, written at the top of that function.

entries.name: Arming_DescriptionBin
entries.description: The wpn_desc.bin handle Arming_BuildScreen opens.

entries.name: ArmoryRowHandlers
entries.description: The armory's 26 row handlers, Armory_OnRow00..Armory_OnRow25, filled by Armory_BuildScreen and passed to ESRect_Ctor as row i's click handler.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_Rows
entries.description: The practice screen's eight mission-list row Panels, built by PracticeScreen_Build; PracticeScreen_SelectRow recolours the old and new row through it.

entries.name: PracticeScreen_RowHandlers
entries.description: The practice screen's eight row handlers, PracticeScreen_OnRow0..PracticeScreen_OnRow7, filled by PracticeScreen_Build and stored into row i's handler field +0x3d.

entries.name: g_ModelToView
entries.description: The current model-to-view transform (0x20 bytes), built by Raster_SetModelTransform and applied by Raster_ModelToView.

entries.name: g_ViewToModel
entries.description: The inverse of g_ModelToView, built by Raster_SetModelTransform.

entries.name: g_EyeInModelSpace
entries.description: The viewpoint in current model space: the origin through g_ViewToModel, set by Raster_SetModelTransform.

entries.name: g_ActiveBitmapArray
entries.description: Process-wide 'currently active DBA bitmap-array' context. TSShape_Render and TSShapeInstance_Render swap it to the shape's bound DBA (TSShape_GetBoundBitmapArray, shape+0x26) for the duration of the draw, then restore it. TSBitmapPart_Render indexes into this global by the part's bitmap tag, not anything owned by the poly's shape. It is a two-field context, not a bare DBA pointer: *g_ActiveBitmapArray (offset +0 of what it points to) is the DBA object (its +4 = frame count, +8 = frame pointer table, per TSBase::getBitmapPtr's assert), while g_ActiveBitmapArray[1] (offset +4 of the global's own stored value, NOT of the nested DBA object) points at a separate 20-byte-stride per-frame UV/texture-descriptor table -- see TSTexture4Poly_Render (00422af5). The builder of that second table is open. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_ActiveSurfaceRecords
entries.description: Global pointer, set from the active TSGroup's own +0x18 field by TSGroup_RenderPolys and TSBSPGroup_Render for the duration of one group's poly walk (save/swap/restore, the same shape as g_ActiveBitmapArray). Points at a flat int32[] where surface index k occupies 4 consecutive int32 slots (Front, FrontLine, Back, BackLine) -- a TSGroup surface entry's 8-short, 16-byte on-disk layout, which is why the file stores a group's surface count as surfaceCount*4. TSTexture4Poly_Render indexes it at byte offset field*4 (front) and field*4+8 (back) with the poly's surface field, which lands on one surface's Front/Back slots because that field holds surfaceIndex*4. See docs/formats/dts-texture-binding.md.

entries.name: g_Mono
entries.description: The shell's DarkMono debug-monitor object: +0 device handle for DARKMONO.VXD, +4 a flag set/cleared by 0046a5e0/0046a5ef. Built by Mono_StaticInit; Mono_Printf and its siblings write to it.

entries.name: Sos_UsingSos9503
entries.description: int16: Sos_BindLibrary sets 1 when it loads sos9503.dll (GetVersion below 0x80000000, or a major version above 3) and 0 when it loads sos32s03.dll. The VSHELL copy of DBSIM's Sos_UsingSos9503.
